It integrates key components such as a GPS module for location tracking, a GSM module for sending emergency alerts, and an intuitive interface comprising an LCD display and a push-button. The system operates by prompting users to confirm their safety through the push-button interface, with a countdown timer displayed on the screen. If the user fails to respond within the allocated time, an automated SMS alert containing the user’s real-time GPS location is sent to registered caregivers. This ensures that assistance is provided promptly in emergency situations. The hardware was selected and optimized for low power consumption and reliability, ensuring continuous operation. The results demonstrated efficient performance in message transmission, precise location tracking, and user interaction, making the system highly effective for its intended purpose. Limitations, such as dependency on network availability and potential issues in GPS signal reception in certain environments, were identified, suggesting areas for future enhancement. The proposed system addresses critical challenges faced by Alzheimer’s patients, such as the risk of wandering or becoming lost, by leveraging embedded technology to provide timely support. This work establishes a practical, cost-effective solution to improve the safety of Alzheimer's patients, while also offering a foundation for further advancements in assistive technologies.

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Fault Detection and Localization in Underground Power Cables: Improving Reliability in Power Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Underground power cables are essential for most power systems today but can experience insulation damage, short-circuit, and mechanical damage. Correct fault detection and accurate fault location is critical in order to reduce outage time and maintenance expenses. This paper proposes a new method for fault diagnosis of the underground power cables using IoT sensors, cloud computing, and ML techniques. The sensors send the voltage, current sensors and soil chemical variaations alongside temperature readings to the ThinkSpeak where they undergo preliminary processing. Three different Random Forest, DenseNet, and the customized pretrained transfer learning model are trained individually to predict and localize the faults using the preprocessed data. Random Forest globally predicts with ensemble decision trees, and DenseNet accurately identifies relationships between parameters if they are nonlinear. A number of Transfer Learning mechanisms are pertinent in analysing time series data and improving the fault prediction results. Different to hybrid systems, this study benchmarks each model and provides a comparison on their effectiveness. The presented results show the efficiency of the introduced framework for high accurate faults detection Random Forest 97%, DenseNet 93%, and transfer learning 99%. That is why based on IoT, cloud computing, and sophisticated ML approaches, this study offers a solution for real-time fault detection of the underground power cables, which can help to develop an intelligent power system.

articleTitle: AI–based IoT Real Time Air Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: In order to detect and forecast air pollutants, this study suggests a real-time air quality monitoring system based on AI and IoT. To offer precise and trustworthy air quality data, the system combines sensors, Internet of Things devices, and machine learning algorithms. With an accuracy rate of more than 90%, the suggested system can identify and predict air pollutants such as O3, PM2.5, and NO2. Stakeholders can access air quality data and get tailored suggestions using a mobile application and real-time data visualization dashboard. Proactive steps to lower air pollution are made possible by the system's predictive analytics capability, improving public health and environmental sustainability.

articleTitle: Investigating FPGA Gaming Systems: Real-Time Tic-Tac-Toe with Custom RISC, VGA Output, and Hardware Counters
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper presents an FPGA based real-time Tic Tac Toe gaming system with custom RISC processor, VGA output and hardware counters. In contrast, software-based implementation in traditional gaming systems can incur processing delays and increase resource overhead. We address these challenges in this research by developing a fully hardware-based solution that exploits parallelism and efficient resource utilization. With the proposed system, the behavior of latency and hardware utilization is optimized so that real time gameplay is with minimal latency. Synthesis and simulation confirm the implementation with low resource usage without compromising the smooth performance. The results validate the correctability of the approach based on using the FPGA for delivering it with interactive gaming experience with high responsiveness.

articleTitle: Automatic Soil Irrigation System using Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Efficient use of water resources in agriculture is extremely important for sustainable agriculture. The present paper proposes a novel automatic soil irrigation system to minimize the usage of water based on the actual content of soil moisture. The system integrates moisture sensors, a microcontroller and an automatic valve controller. The proposed system is precise in irrigation, saving water and providing the crop with the optimal amount of water. Experimental findings prove the efficacy of the system to manage soil water to the required level without much manipulation by man. It is scalable and may be utilized in diverse farm settings, and it achieves cost saving as well as environmental sustainability. The data is processed by IoT device that triggers automatic watering the instant the water level in the soil drops below a set reading. The system can be remotely accessed and monitored via web or mobile applications in a bid to enable farmers to efficiently manage watering.

articleTitle: Ambient Energy Capture from Human Footsteps using Piezoelectric Sensors
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research work explores footstep energy harvesting as a sustainable solution for urban energy needs. Using piezoelectric materials and electromagnetic induction, it converts pedestrian movement into electricity, ideal for high-traffic areas like train stations. Inspired by real-world applications in London and Tokyo, the study evaluates efficiency, economic benefits, and environmental impact. While individual steps generate minimal power, large-scale implementation can reduce fossil fuel reliance and enhance smart city energy systems. If one could further laminate the code for collecting energy under the assemblies of hybrid panels integrating solar and wind energy, it would surely boost this one towards greener and efficient urban spaces. The proposed prototype finds a sustainable solution for energy harvesting effectively.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Intelligent System for Helmet Detection and Automated Penalty Enforcement using AI & ML
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The increasing number of road accidents due to non-compliance with helmet regulations highlights the need for intelligent systems to enhance rider safety. This paper presents an IoT-enabled system that utilizes Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Learning (ML) to detect riders without helmets and enforce penalties automatically. The system integrates a Raspberry Pi with a camera module to capture real-time images of motorcyclists at traffic signals. AI-powered object detection models, such as YOLOv5, determine helmet usage, while Optical Character Recognition (OCR) techniques extract license plate details for violators. The system transmits violation data to a centralized server via IoT communication protocols, where an automated penalty system processes the information and notifies the rider through SMS or email. By automating helmet detection and penalty enforcement, this system enhances road safety, reduces manual intervention, and ensures adherence to traffic regulations.

articleTitle: Real-Time Detection of Road Objects and Lane Markings for Autonomous Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research focuses on the development of an advanced object and lane recognition system for autonomous vehicles, leveraging the YOLOv8 Deep Learning (DL) model. The primary goal is to ensure accurate, real-time recognition of road objects, lane boundaries, and other critical features to enhance autonomous navigation. The methodology involves preprocessing and augmentation of a diverse dataset, followed by training and testing the YOLOv8 model. This approach ensures robustness under varying environmental and traffic conditions, including occlusions and lighting challenges. The final model is integrated into an intuitive user interface that provides real-time visual feedback, enabling seamless interaction and monitoring. Comprehensive evaluations were conducted to validate the system’s performance. The results demonstrated high accuracy in recognizing objects like vehicles, and pedestrians, as well as stable lane recognition across diverse scenarios. Despite minor limitations in extreme conditions, the system proved to be reliable and efficient for real-world applications. Future work will aim to expand functionality by incorporating additional sensors like LiDAR and optimizing the system for edge devices to reduce computational overhead. Additional features, such as traffic sign recognition and obstacle prediction, will also be explored. The proposed system serves as a robust foundation for enhancing Autonomous Vehicle (AV) technology, contributing significantly to road safety and intelligent transportation systems. Through innovative integration of machine learning techniques, this research addresses key challenges in autonomous navigation and lays the groundwork for further advancements in the field. This research addresses inaccurate object detection and unstable lane recognition in autonomous vehicles. The proposed system improves accuracy and reliability for safer self-driving technology.

articleTitle: Floral-Structured Circular Patch Antenna for WLAN Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: In order to overcome the limitations of space and signal efficiency in WLAN applications, this work proposes a small 20 × 30 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> antenna that is developed on a FR4 epoxy substrate (εr = 4.4). With a return loss of -16.487 dB at 3.2 GHz and -13.11 dB at 5.8 GHz, the suggested antenna achieves excellent impedance matching and ensures low signal reflection (VSWR = 1.36). Simulations using CST Studio Suite 2024 confirm its excellent efficiency, steady radiation, and broadband performance. In contemporary wireless networks, its compact design maximizes utilization while improving operational reliability. Cost-effectiveness and structural stability are provided by the use of FR4 material. The suggested antenna's broad bandwidth and multiband characteristics make it the perfect choice for next-generation WLAN systems, where efficiency and small size are essential.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Hybrid Energy Harvesting System using Piezoelectric and Thermoelectric Transducer for Efficient Lighting Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The main aim of this proposed system is to reduce the utilization of off-grid lighting, energy bills, and carbon footprints. The Compact Piezoelectric Transducer (CPET) employs a 25mm PZT plate, easier to deploy than the 50mm PZT and 700mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> rubber pad used in standard systems. The Thermoelectric Transducer (TEC 12706) using Bismuth Telluride delivers 6W for 3 hours, whereas the current system is based on a 50mm PZT in series with three modules and a bespoke TET system with an externally powered 1000W lamp. The hardware setup Produced enough electricity to operate a 6W LED light for 3 hours per day and the energy management circuit achieved an 85% efficiency, while IoT connectivity proposed for immediate observation. Based on the detailed study it is observed that the proposed method is superior to this existing method in terms of energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Reviving Darkness: Enhancing Low Visibility Images in Adverse Conditions using an Optimized Zero-DCE Model
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Capturing clear images in low-light environments such as fog, rain, and moonlight is a major challenge, impacting applications like surveillance, autonomous driving, and nighttime navigation. Existing deep learning-based methods, including Zero-Reference Deep Curve Estimation (Zero-DCE), often struggle with over-saturation, unnatural color balance, noise amplification, and loss of structural details. This research introduces an Optimized Zero-DCE Model that specifically addresses these limitations by refining the loss function to achieve a balance between brightness enhancement, noise suppression, and color consistency. The model incorporates adaptive parameter tuning and an improved training strategy to prevent over-enhancement and retain fine details. Experimental results show that the optimized model significantly enhances image quality, achieving a Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) of 21.90 and a Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) of 0.9469, outperforming conventional enhancement techniques. These improvements enable more reliable low-light vision for safety-critical applications, ensuring better clarity and usability in extreme environmental conditions.

articleTitle: Bluetooth Controlled Grasscutter
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Lawn and field maintenance can be a laborious process, either needing manual labor or costly automated machines. The conventional cutting of grass is a time-consuming, labor-intensive. and in some cases, dangerous process. In order to solve these problems, we introduce the Bluetooth-Controlled Grass Cutter, a smart and effective product aimed at making lawn care easier. Our system has a wirelessly operated grass cutter that is controlled through a mobile app using Bluetooth technology. This allows users to control the cutter remotely, doing away with physical labor while providing precision and safety. The design features a motorized blade system, an easy-to-use control panel, and a rechargeable battery for environmentally friendly use. Through the integration of automation and remote accessibility, this project provides a low-cost and hassle-free alternative to traditional grass-cutting methods. For home gardens, public parks, or farming fields, this innovation increases efficiency, reduces labor, and facilitates a smarter approach to green space maintenance.

Author Keywords: and Infrastructure SDG 11 Sustainable Cities and Communities SDG 12 Responsible Consumption and Production

articleTitle: Affordable Autonomous Driving System using Arduino Uno
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: An autonomous vehicle is one that can travel and complete its functions without the assistance of an operator. There are three main types of autonomous vehicles: air, ground, and submersible. They are a relatively new subset of robotics. They can be used in a number of scenarios when it would be unsafe, impractical, or impossible to have a human operator present. The car will be equipped with of sensors to monitor the ambience and make decisions regarding its own actions. A human controller is not necessary for an autonomous vehicle to function. Through the use of its sensors, the vehicle gains a limited understanding of its surroundings, which control algorithms utilize to decide what to do next in relation to a mission goal that is supplied by the human. This completely removes the necessity for any person to keep an eye on the mundane duties that the car is performing.

articleTitle: Cost and Reliability Optimization in Multi-Source Renewable Energy Microgrids Using Advanced Evolutionary Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research addresses the challenge of optimizing micro grid Operations driven by renewable energy— wind, solar, hydro, and biomass—to minimize operational costs while ensuring high system reliability. We evaluate three optimization techniques: Non-dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm II (NSGA-II),Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO),and Genetic Algorithm (GA). Comparative analysis reveals that PSO provides the most effective trade-off between price reduction and Dependability improvement, outperforming NSGA-II and GA. These findings demonstrate the superiority of PSO in enhancing microgrid performance, offering valuable insights for cost-effective and reliable energy management.

articleTitle: Automatic Garbage Collector using Sensors and Internet of Things
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The Automatic Garbage Collector is an IoT-based system designed to automate waste collection. A line follower robot, ESP32, ultrasonic sensors, and a servo motor with electromagnets were all integrated into the system to efficiently detect, gather, and move trash without the need for human assistance. A smart dustbin with an ultrasonic sensor detects the fill level and sends a signal to ESP32-2 via MQTT. ESP32-2 activates an Arduino-controlled line follower robot, which navigates to the bin. Real-time updates were made possible with MQTT communication, guaranteeing prompt trash disposal. An ultrasonic sensor detects obstacles, triggering a buzzer for safety. The robot, equipped with a 360° servo motor and electromagnets, lifts the filled bin, replaces it with an empty one, and transports the garbage to a central disposal area. This system improves efficiency, reduces human effort, optimizes waste management, and ensures a cleaner environment. The research addresses inefficiencies in traditional waste collection, such as delays and high labor costs, by implementing a fully automated approach. The system's real-time communication and autonomous operation make it a scalable solution for smart cities.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Hexagonal Koch Fractal Antenna
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: a hexagonal microstrip patch antenna serves as the core of the design. In order to lower the side lobe level, the hexagonal-shaped patch central portion is also eliminated. A new fractal antenna design is suggested and examined. Finally, a prototype is built and measured in order to validate our concept. The results show that, with a bandwidth of 13.33%, 13.31%and 5.14%, the reflection coefficient remains -10 dB for 2.3125-2.6 GHz, 3.1234-3.5227 GHz and 4.8626-5.191 GHz. According to the simulation research, the antenna can cover two relevant WLAN bands, which are IEEE standards 802.11a (2.4 to 2.4835 GHz) and 5 GHz WLAN, n40 with 2.3 GHz and n41 (2.5 GHz). An antenna with the appropriate size can emit radiation in two bands: the low band, which spans 2.3125 to 2.6 GHz, and the high band, which spans from 4.8626 to 5.191 GHz, with maximum gains of 4.242 dB.

articleTitle: Analysis of Compensation Network in Resonant Inductive Power Transfer (RIPT) for Electric Vehicle Charging
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: In wireless power transfer application, Inductive power techniques are commonly used for Battery Charging for electric vehicle. Wireless Power Transfer offers a promising avenue for automating power delivery to consumers, reducing the necessity for manmade interface. On other side, appropriate vehicle to grid linking and appropriate control and compensation network are needed for efficient wireless power transfer method. Compensation topologies are essential for ensuring optimal power delivery between primary and secondary to enable effective and reliable power transfer. This paper presents WPT used in Series-Series compensation topologies.

Author Keywords: Resonance Inductive Power Transfer (RIPT) Compensation Topologies

articleTitle: An Efficient Urban Building Height Rover using Ultrasonic Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: A significant proportion of mobile surveying systems in the market are not economically viable due to their inconvenience in operation such as large size, complex data processing requirements and limited accessibility to areas without vehicle access. This paper proposes a model to deploy a rover-based system to address the challenges to measure the height of the building and object in urban environments using a low-cost, easy-to-assemble system comprising ultrasonic sensors, stepper motors and a laser system. Here, it integrates calibration mechanisms to be highly accurate, and the rover's modular architecture promotes robustness and easy replication for multiple scenarios. This advances the measurement of building heights in urban settings by enhancing users’ control of the process, and in delivering results that reflect local requirements.

articleTitle: Design Adaptive Controller for EV Bidirectional Converter with Renewables
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The paper aimed at EVs, prioritizing fine-grained control over electric vehicles' charging and discharging procedures by predetermined reference values. The electric vehicle operates G2V and V2G modes of operation. Additionally, a photovoltaic (PV) system is integrated with the grid to facilitate renewable energy sharing. To enhance battery performance during both charging and discharging cycles, a combined PI and SMC are implemented across both control strategies. In G2V mode, the battery is charged using energy from the conventional AC grid as well as the PV system. During V2G operation, power from both the EV battery and the PV system is delivered to the AC load, effectively reducing the demand on the grid. A Full-Bridge Converter governed by PI-SMC control and a VSC managed by an SRF controller is employed to stabilize the DC-Link voltage and ensure reliable power delivery to the AC load. The system was modeled in MATLAB/Simulink and validated through real-time testing on an OP-4500 platform under SIL conditions.

articleTitle: Development and Optimization of Frequency Divider in Integrated Circuits Leveraging Transvidkan Gate Architecture
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: In modern society, electronic systems have become indispensable to daily life. As technology evolves, these systems grow increasingly intricate, leading to challenges such as heightened power demands and reduced physical space for microchip components. Reversible logic addresses these challenges by enabling power- computing and zero-energy dissipation, offering a efficient pathway to design advanced combinational and sequential circuits. Among emerging solutions, the Modified Gate Diffusion Input (MGDI) technique stands out as an innovative strategy for low-power digital circuit design. This method optimizes transistor count, minimizes signal delay, and reduces energy usage without compromising architectural simplicity. Comparative studies between conventional CMOS technology and alternative pass-transistor logic approaches highlight these advantages. Quantum-Inspired Gates, such as the Double Feynman Gate, Feynman Gate, and NOT Gate, exemplify this paradigm shift. This study presents a transistor-level implementation of key Quantum-Inspired Gates and analyzes the experimental outcomes to demonstrate their practical viability. This paper final outcome is analysis of frequency divider circuit.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Tri-band Quarter Mode SIW Antenna for Sub-6GHz, WLAN and WIFI Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The paper presents the circular shaped quarter mode substrate integrated waveguide (SIW) based slot antenna for triple band applications. The substrate material used in this design is FR-4 with a thickness of 1.6 mm. as 4.4 and copper thickness of 35um. The CST simulation tool is used to simulate the proposed antenna and extract the results. The antenna resonates with three resonant frequencies those are 3.5GHz, 4.49GHz and 5.39GHz respectively. The S11, VSWR, gain in dBi and bandwidth values are -26dB, 1.1013, 5.04dBi and 103 MHz at 3.5GHz frequency -27dB, 1.0905, 4.1dBi and 105MHz at 4.49 GHz frequency. -17dB, 1.3186, 3.48dBi and 145MHz at 5.39 GHz frequency. also radiates bidirectional radiation patterns at all resonant frequencies and well suited for wireless applications.

articleTitle: Design and Optimization Towards Sustainable Automatic Green Slicing System
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research study aims to develop a versatile and efficient solution for maintaining lawns and gardens. Utilizing IoT for remote control and automation, this machine combines Arduino Uno and NodeMCU for managing robotic movements, alongside an ultrasonic sensor for obstacle detection. In the proposed system, the machine can operate autonomously to detect and avoid obstacles and allows manual control via IoT when needed. This dual-mode operation enables users to supervise grass cutting effectively, offering a blend of convenience and safety.

articleTitle: Safety Assurance of LPG Gas Through IoT in Industries
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Liquefied Petroleum Gas (LPG) is heavily used in industries, so its safety assurance is a matter of top priority. Gaseous leaks and LPG depletion from cylinders can lead to dangerous situations, and therefore an intelligent monitoring system is needed. This paper presents an Internet of Things (IoT)-based industrial LPG safety system. The system described herein tracks a large quantity of LPG cylinders in real-time and detects gas leaks using very sensitive gas sensors. When detected, an alarm process is triggered to raise an MP3 player voice alarm, give an SMS warning to the user, display a "Gas Leakage" warning on an LCD screen, and automatically open windows/doors while turning on an exhaust fan to disperse the gas concentration. The system also monitors the LPG level in every cylinder and notifies when a cylinder is low, enabling replacement on time. All real-time information and historical reports are collected and processed through the ThingSpeak IoT platform. The intelligent system enhances industrial safety by way of anticipatory alerting and automated action, minimizing risks associated with LPG usage. The addition of IoT ensures real-time monitoring and decision-making from a distance, significantly improving workplace safety and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: A Novel PV Array Reconfiguration-Technique to Maximize Power Generation under Shading Conditions
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Partial shading conditions (PSCs) pose a great challenge to photovoltaic (PV) arrays and result in high power losses as well as reducing the lifetime of PV modules. Traditional PV arrangements are incapable of reducing such losses. A new Jigsaw Sudoku Puzzle-based reconfiguration method for improving PV arrays' power output under shading is presented in this research. The technique is designed to redistribute the effects of shading uniformly throughout the array, reducing mismatch losses and enhancing overall efficiency. A 6×6 PV array is simulated and modeled in MATLAB/Simulink, comparing the performance of the proposed method with conventional configurations, such as String-Parallel (SP), Fully-Cross-Tied (FCT), and Novel Shade Distribution (NSD). Performance metrics like global peak power points, conversion efficiency, form factor, power dissipation losses, open-circuit voltage, short-circuit current, Output Power Improvement, and number of peaks are evaluated. The findings prove that Jigsaw Sudoku Puzzle-based reconfiguration improves power output considerably, increases efficiency, and minimizes power dissipation losses when compared to traditional configurations and is thus a practical solution for reducing the negative impacts of partial shading in PV systems.

articleTitle: IoT and ML for Air Pollution Monitoring with Real Time Data and Prediction of Health Advisory
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Air pollution is a major environmental and health concern, especially in urban areas where high pollution levels can severely impact individuals with respiratory conditions. This paper presents an IoT and ML-based Air Pollution Monitoring System designed to provide real-time air quality monitoring, predictive analytics, and intelligent route optimization. The system utilizes an IoT module installed at traffic signals, equipped with air quality sensors to monitor CO, CO₂, and smoke levels. The collected data is displayed on an LCD screen, informing commuters of pollution levels and health advisories. A mobile application integrates real-time pollution data and ML-based predictions to assess outdoor safety, particularly for individuals with respiratory conditions. The system employs a Decision Tree Classifier to generate personalized health advisories based on pollution levels and user-reported symptoms. Additionally, the system offers intelligent route optimization, suggesting alternative routes with lower pollution exposure using real-time sensor data and historical trends. For seamless operation, Firebase is used for real-time data synchronization, ensuring accurate and timely updates. The integration of IoT and ML enables continuous air quality monitoring and proactive health measures. This research aims to enhance public awareness, encourage healthier urban mobility, and support smart city initiatives by providing data-driven insights and reducing pollution exposure risks.

articleTitle: Sensors based Smart Pillow for Quality Sleep Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Sleep quality is a vital aspect of human health and well-being, with increasing interest in the development of non-invasive, cost-effective methods for monitoring sleep. Traditional methods of sleep analysis, such as polysomnography, are both costly and invasive, which has led to the growing demand for wearable and non-wearable alternatives. In this paper, we propose a smart pillow system designed to monitor sleep quality through the integration of Force Sensing Resistor pressure sensors and NTC thermistors. The system uses an ESP32 microcontroller to process pressure and temperature data and predict sleep stages. Results from a series of experiments show that the system can accurately detect sleep quality and provide real-time feedback through an Arduino IDE platform on a connected laptop. This paper presents the detailed design, methodology, results, and future implications for this system as a non-invasive, low-cost sleep tracking solution.

articleTitle: Fire Extinguishing Robot using IoT
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This project aims to design and develop an autonomous robot that can detect and extinguish fires in real time. The system integrates an ESP32 microcontroller as the central processing unit an ESP32-CAM module for video streaming and advanced fire detection, and multiple sensors including a flame sensor for fire detection and an ultrasonic sensor for obstacle avoidance. A servo motor and water pump are employed for directional control and water pump are employed for directional control and water dispensing, respectively. The robot operates by continuously scanning its environment using the flame sensor. Upon detecting a fire, the system activates the water pump and adjusts the servo motor to aim the water jet at the flame. The ultrasonic sensor ensures that the robot can navigate around obstacles and reach the target efficiently. The ESP32-CAM adds an optional layer of functionality by providing live video feed for remote monitoring or enabling image -based fire detection through AI models. This compact, cost-effective, and versatile system is designed to enhance fire safety in residential, industrial, and commercial settings by providing rapid response and reducing human intervention in hazardous situations.

Author Keywords: and Fire Safety Robotics are few of them

articleTitle: Quantitative Assessment of Static Plantar Pressure and Foot Structure in Overweight Young Adults
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Increased BMI is linked to foot disorders and neuromuscular conditions, yet its impact on plantar pressure in young adults is not well understood. This study investigates the effects of elevated BMI (BMI > 25) on plantar pressure in young adults (ages 18-21), considering both male and female participants, using static protocols. Eighty-one participants—35 overweight (BMI > 25, 27.93 ± 3.06) and 46 control (BMI < 25, 21.42 ± 2.16)—were analyzed for peak plantar pressure (PPP), foot weight distribution, width, and angle in both forefoot and hindfoot regions. Results showed that the overweight group had higher hindfoot PPP, significant gender differences in PPP and foot contact area, and left-foot dominance. These findings suggest that excess weight affects foot structure and sensitivity, supporting the need for regular monitoring of plantar parameters using wearable AI for improved foot health.

articleTitle: Automated Milk Boil Prevention System using ToF Sensing and Servo-Controlled Stove Adjustment
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper presents the creation of a system that prevents milk from boiling. An SG90 servo motor, a VL53L0X ToF sensor, and an ESP32-S3 T-Display are used in the system's implementation. When a predetermined threshold is achieved, the servo motor is triggered to automatically turn the stove knob in response to the rising milk level sensed by the VL53L0X sensor. The integration of automated control and real-time monitoring improves ease and efficiency. The method reduces milk waste and improves safety, making it appropriate for both home and commercial kitchens. The system's dependability in identifying boiling milk and reacting suitably has been confirmed by experimental findings.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of Five Level Multilevel Inverter for EV Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The design and simulation of a self-amplitude modulated five-level inverter aimed at reducing voltage stress on converter switches in electric vehicles (EVs) are presented in this paper. Conventional inverters with lower voltage levels usually cause significant voltage stress, particularly at the semiconductor switches, which leads to faster switching losses, lower efficiency, and a shorter tool life. By providing a stepped voltage waveform and reducing the stress gradients between the switching devices, a five-level inverter is suggested as a solution to these problems. Self-amplitude modulation ensures the most effective voltage degree balancing, which simultaneously enhances the device's dependability and performance. The five-level inverter layout is mainly based on a special modulation technique that improves the overall power quality by minimizing harmonic distortion and reducing voltage stress. Because the transition between voltage level is more gradual and smooth, this design effectively reduces switching losses when compared to traditional inverters, which also enhances the electrical car motor's overall performance. The results of the simulation show the effectiveness of the suggested inverter in terms of efficiency, reduced stress at the converter switches, and voltage waveforms. This technique can improve the overall performance and sustainability of electric vehicles by reducing electricity losses and extending the life of power electronic devices.

articleTitle: N Floor Elevator Control System using PLC
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This article presents an optimized Elevator Control System (ECS) utilizing Siemens PLC and TIA Portal software to simplify motor control for forward and reverse movements. Traditional elevator control systems involve complex coding and hardware-intensive configurations for motor direction control. This research addresses the issue of excessive code complexity and hardware dependency by developing an optimized logic circuit-based approach that streamlines the programming process. The proposed method significantly reduces coding effort, enhances system reliability, and minimizes hardware requirements, making elevator control more efficient and cost-effective. Experimental validation demonstrates improvements in response time, energy efficiency, and overall system performance. This work contributes to modern building automation by offering a simplified, scalable, and energy-efficient solution for elevator systems.

articleTitle: Electrical Mesh and UV Light based Economical Mosquito Avoidance System
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: A low-cost, non-microcontroller based device is proposed to lower mosquito populations in delimited and slum areas, hence preventing the transmission of diseases including dengue, malaria, and the Zika virus., particularly in metropolitan areas with high population densities and poor access. Conventional approaches to controlling mosquitoes, such as chemical insecticides, larvicides, and adulticide sprays, frequently have drawbacks, including negative effects on the environment, expensive prices, and inconsistent effectiveness. In order to tackle these problems, An affordable, non-microcontroller based device has been deveped that is intended to be used in low-resource environments. This device uses a combination of neutralizing and enticing methods to try and drastically reduce mosquito populations. Because of its straightforward and durable design, which makes building and maintenance simple, it may be deployed in vulnerable communities by governmental and non-governmental organizations alike.

articleTitle: Multi-Source Power Integration for EV Charging
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This project aims to promote more sustainable urban transportation by facilitating the adoption of electric vehicles (EVs) and integrating renewable energy sources into charging infrastructures. By incorporating solar energy harnessed from photovoltaic (PV) panels, the initiative seeks to reduce reliance on fossil fuels and lower carbon footprints associated with urban mobility. Additionally, the exploration of wireless charging technology for auxiliary systems, such as wipers, enhances convenience and operational efficiency in densely populated environments. The project focuses on optimizing energy usage and storage in EV charging systems to improve overall energy efficiency and reduce operational costs. Furthermore, the design of a flexible system allows for the seamless integration of various power sources, ensuring practicality across diverse urban settings and supporting future expandability. The implementation of this multi-source power integration framework not only addresses current urban transportation challenges but also sets the stage for scalable solutions that can adapt to evolving energy landscapes. By fostering collaboration among stakeholders, including city planners and technology providers, the project aims to create a sustainable ecosystem for electric mobility. Ultimately, this initiative contributes to the broader goal of transitioning to a low-carbon urban future, making cities more resilient and livable.

articleTitle: IoT-Driven Intelligent Waste Management System with Disinfectant Spray
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The rapid increase in urban waste generation demands innovative solutions to improve public health and operational efficiency. This paper presents an IoT-driven intelligent waste management system that integrates real-time monitoring, dynamic route optimization, and automated disinfectant mechanisms. Smart bins equipped with ultrasonic, gas, rain, and infrared sensors transmit data via ESP8266 Wi-Fi/GSM modules to a cloud platform (ThingSpeak), enabling anomaly detection and route optimization using a modified Travelling Salesman Problem (TSP) algorithm. A solenoid-based disinfectant system reduces bacterial load by 98% (verified through lab testing [5]), while the TSP algorithm reduces collection time by 40% and fuel consumption by 30% compared to traditional methods [4]. A three-level dashboard (admin, collector, user) provides actionable insights through a mobile app. Deployed in a 1 km<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> testbed with 10 bins, the system demonstrates scalability and cost-effectiveness. Future work includes integrating machine learning for predictive analytics and automated waste segregation. This solution aligns with UN Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs) 11 and 13 [1], promoting cleaner cities and climate action.

articleTitle: ESP32-CAM-based Wireless Human Detection System with PIR Sensor and Instant Alerts via GSM and Blynk App
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Security and observation are fundamental in different applications, counting private security, mechanical checking, and smart city administration. This paper presents a cost-effective, remote human location framework that coordinating a Inactive Infrared (PIR) sensor, ESP32-CAM, Worldwide Framework for Portable Communications (GSM) module, and the Blynk stage for real-time checking. The framework identifies human development utilizing the PIR sensor, captures pictures through the ESP32-CAM, and sends moment alarms through GSM and Blynk, empowering clients to get notices on their versatile gadgets. By dispensing with the require for complex wiring, the framework improves effectiveness and ease of arrangement. Outlined to be power-efficient, versatile, and user-friendly, it guarantees dependable security observing. Test comes about show tall precision in human location and quick caution transmission, making it reasonable for different security applications. A comparative investigation with existing frameworks illustrates made strides in discovering unwavering quality and decreased reaction timecite1. This inquire about contributes to the progression of farther reconnaissance arrangements and lays the establishment for future upgrades, such as AI fueled acknowledgment and cloud-based capacity for improved security administration. .

articleTitle: IoT based Harbour Surveillance Aqua Guard RC Canoe
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: India’s harbour ecosystems face significant environmental and security risks that require constant attention. The current surveillance system involves manual supervision and less than basic threshold alerted detection to critical events with limited integration of harbour environmental monitoring. Thus, this thesis proposes an IoT anomaly detection system that amalgamates environmental monitoring and real-time surveillance monitoring management. Aqua Guard RC Canoe is proposed to monitor the harbour area that can generate data for anomalies and threats present due to environmental sensors like pH, turbidity, anemometer, temperature, humidity, ESP32 camera, and GPS. It delivers the seamless interconnectivity of sensory devices, transmission, and integration on the IoT network. When an anomaly is detected, the system will be configured to raise alarms and generate visual evidence to initiate a swift response mechanism to the anomaly. For flexible and real-time monitoring of various spots in the harbour, it will be mounted on a remote-controlled mobile boat. A more proactive flow of decisions for risk mitigation is expected from the aggregation and surveillance data as well as environmental parameters to get a balanced view of the conditions of the harbour.

articleTitle: Machine Learning based Voltage Regulation for PV System using Buck Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper presents the issue of voltage instability in a solar-powered system due to fluctuations in solar irradiance. These fluctuations in solar irradiance cause oscillations in output voltage and reduce the efficiency of the overall system. To overcome this issue, the paper proposes a solar-powered DC voltage regulation system that employs machine learning techniques to maintain the system’s operational stability. The primary source of energy is from a PV system and it includes a buck converter that regulates the output voltage. A microcontroller, integrated with a machine learning model using K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm, continuously monitors the solar irradiance, load requirements, and system voltage and adjust the buck converter’s duty cycle. By leveraging the historical data and predictive analytics, the proposed system can expect fluctuations in solar irradiance and load, thus enabling effective voltage regulation. This system reduces dependency on grid power. It enhances energy efficiency and system operational stability.

articleTitle: IoT-based Vehicle Ignition and Safety System
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The increase in road accidents and non-compliance with safe riding practices highlight the need for intelligent transportation systems. This paper presents an IoT-based motorcycle ignition and safety system designed to monitor rider behavior and vehicle safety in real time. The system incorporates three key functions: helmet detection, alcohol level monitoring, and accident detection. Helmet usage is verified using the RC522 RFID module, ensuring compliance with safety regulations. The MQ3 sensor detects alcohol consumption, preventing intoxicated riding. Additionally, the NEO-6MV2 GPS module provides real-time location tracking, while a voltage sensor monitors battery health. A servo motor and an electric throttle replace the conventional throttle, enabling speed regulation through user-defined limits via the Blynk app. The system also integrates remote monitoring through Telegram, sending real-time updates on CO gas levels, alcohol detection, battery status, and GPS coordinates. An emergency override feature allows the vehicle owner to start the motorcycle in critical situations while notifying trusted contacts. By leveraging IoT and smart control mechanisms, this system enhances road safety, promotes responsible riding behavior, and ensures rapid response in emergencies, paving the way for a scalable motorcycle safety model.

articleTitle: Automated Data Collection System for Advanced Vehicle Detection and Traffic Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper presents a real-time traffic analysis and vehicle detection solution aimed at boosting emergency response times, particularly for ambulance detection. The system employs the YOLOv11 model to identify ambulances across various conditions and uses four side cameras at key intersections for comprehensive traffic monitoring. By fine-tuning the YOLOv11 model with a custom dataset, the system achieves high accuracy in detecting ambulances in diverse scenarios. The integrated framework dynamically adjusts traffic signals, suggests alternative routes to reduce delays, and sends automated notifications to authorities and emergency services. This approach enhances traffic management, prioritizes ambulances, and supports public safety and efficient emergency response. The system's real-time capabilities and scalability make it a valuable solution for modern cities aiming to improve traffic flow and emergency service efficiency. The research demonstrates that utilizing advanced technologies can effectively address critical challenges in urban traffic control and emergency management, ultimately enhancing public safety and streamlining emergency response processes.

articleTitle: Integrated IoT-based Hazard Detection and Automated Waste Management System for Environmental Safety
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Waste management is a critical challenge in urban environments, where inefficient disposal methods contribute to pollution, public health risks, and operational inefficiencies. Traditional waste collection systems lack real-time monitoring, leading to overfilled bins, delayed disposal, and increased environmental hazards. In this research, an IoT-based smart dustbin system is designed to optimize waste management through automated real-time monitoring. The system integrates an ultrasonic sensor to detect waste levels, an IR sensor for user interaction, and a temperature sensor for fire hazard detection. A key novelty of this research is the incorporation of three MQ gas sensors for toxic gas detection, ensuring early identification of hazardous emissions from waste decomposition. The data is transmitted via a Wi-Fi module to a web-based dashboard, displaying waste levels, gas concentrations, timestamps, and geolocation. Additionally, an automated GSM-based SMS notification system alerts municipal authorities when the dustbin is full or detects hazardous gases. While IoT integration enhances urban sanitation and operational efficiency, challenges such as power consumption and network dependency persist. To address these concerns, our system optimizes data transmission intervals and leverages energy-efficient components. This approach enables seamless waste management, reducing manual monitoring efforts while fostering a cleaner and safer urban environment.

articleTitle: Proactive Obstacle Monitoring and Prevention System
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Accidents caused by essence track barriers, such as animals, debris and people violations weighing important safety and operating risk. The project introduces an active obstacle and introduces the prevention system that integrates infrared (IR) and ultrasound sensor, wireless communication, GPS-based train positioning and bio-related preventive systems to increase rail security. The system detects obstacles when using IR and ultrasonic sensors and transmitting real-time alerts through the Lura wireless module. A GPS-based selective warning mechanism ensures that only trainers leading to an obstacle get information by optimizing communication efficiency. In addition, bioacoustics releases prevention systems ultrasonic sound waves to retreat to prevent conflict of wildlife. The system is powered by solar energy, which ensures energy efficiency and scalability in remote areas. Field experiments show high identification accuracy, rapid notification transfer and effective animal prevention, leading to cost -effective, scalable and reliable growth in rail security for this solution. By reducing the collision of trains with obstacles, it improves rail security, protection of wildlife and operational efficiency.

articleTitle: Global Maximum Power Point Extraction using SEPIC Converter for Agriculture Farming Purposes
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This proposed system is designed to develop and enhance a SEPIC converter-based solar charger that delivers a constant DC output. It achieves this by integrating soil moisture sensing, along with a relay and water pump, to facilitate IoT capabilities and enable automated, real-time control of irrigation processes. The converter is of the SEPIC converter type with PI control for stable voltage regulation. Optimized power performance is achieved by using a PIC microcontroller. Sensors for soil moisture levels allow control of the pumps and real-time monitoring through an Android application based on IoT. It was designed so that the system would use solar energy very efficiently and give stable output regarding the voltage produced. Automated irrigation, based on the moisture present in the soil, saves water. It monitors in real time using IoT and enhances control and efficiency over the system of a user. The SEPIC-based solar charger with IoT-based automation is the right application in the agricultural and domestic sectors because it reduces dependency on the supply of a grid and also brings smart irrigation under its domain, enhancing both energy and water management.

articleTitle: Real-Time Flood Risk Assessment and Forecasting with Hybrid BiCNN and Deep Learning Models
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The catchment viewpoint has historically been the preferred approach for flood estimation and management among water resources engineers, hydrologists, and statisticians. This perspective considers meteorology, geography, and geology of a specific catchment when assessing flood potential. Enhanced methodologies are necessary for improved flood predictions due to the limitations in breadth and accuracy of traditional methods. In response to these challenges, this research employs VMD to enhance the quality of the input data utilised for model training. A novel technique utilising BiCNN is proposed, integrating bilinear interactions into the CNN architecture to capture complex spatial and channel-wise correlations. The model attained an F1 Score of 96.92%, a recall of 92.64%, a precision of 94.23%, and an overall accuracy of 96.84% on previously unseen images, indicating exceptional performance. The flood risk assessment results validate that the proposed strategy is superior than other advanced methodologies. The findings suggest that the development of a reliable flood risk assessment grading system facilitates more precise and timely flood predictions. This advancement may result in improved flood management strategies and more informed decision-making during a crisis.

articleTitle: Analysis of Solar PV Inverter Systems by using May Fly Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research paper presents a novel method for utilizing the Mayfly Algorithm to optimize solar photovoltaic inverter systems is introduced. Conventional maximum power point tracking techniques frequently experience inefficiencies in dynamic environments, power losses, and sluggish convergence. The suggested method efficiently adjusts to changes in temperature and irradiance, improving tracking precision and system stability. According to simulation studies, the Mayfly Algorithm outperforms traditional techniques in terms of power losses, energy output, and convergence speed. The results demonstrate how well it works to boost solar inverter performance, which makes it a viable way to improve grid integration and renewable energy efficiency.

articleTitle: Motor Drive Fault Detection and Control System for Industrial Robots
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The main focus of this project is to develop a MATLAB Simulink model for fault detection in motor drives controlling system in industrial sector that provides dynamic support to machines, helps to improve efficiency and enhance productivity. This model is a non-invasive and ergonomic framework which integrates real-time monitoring. This model is designed to enhance the faults detection in time intervals so it will be helpful for the persons to rectify it. By using the method, the industries can enhance their production and the motors can also be protected from getting damaged up to 40% of faults can be reduced based on the temperature and more than 60% of the faults can be observed through the vibration levels.

articleTitle: Impact of Pollution on the Performance of High-Voltage Insulators under Alternating Current
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The study investigates the impact of pollution severity on the performance of the disc porcelain high-voltage insulator, focusing on the real model under alternative current conditions. Artificial pollution was applied to specific zones of the insulator to simulate real-world conditions. The flashover voltage and leakage current were measured to evaluate the influence of pollution severity. Results showed that as the leakage current of the pollution layer increased, the flashover voltage decreased, indicating reduced insulator rigidity. The leakage current increased with higher applied voltages and pollution severity, highlighting a critical mode where the current surged abruptly under severe conditions. This study provides valuable insights into the effects of pollution on high-voltage insulators, emphasizing the need for effective management to ensure reliable operation.

articleTitle: Human Stress and Zone based Vehicle Speed Control
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The proposed system known as "Human Stress and Zone-Based Vehicle Speed Control" is a modern and state-of-the-art method to promote road safety by combining real-time monitoring of driver stress with automatic speed control in specified zones. It employs a range of physiological sensors like temperature, heart rate, and galvanic skin response (GSR) to measure the level of stress in the driver. When detecting increased stress, the system immediately simulates slowing down the vehicle speed, thus reducing driver distraction and the risk posed by slowed reaction times. Besides, speed control is implemented through radio frequency identification (RFID) in sensitive areas to include school and hospital campuses. This environmental speed adaptation in real-time fuses environmental information with driver-centered stress monitoring for optimal driving behavior. Monitoring both environment and driver stress also forms the two-pronged approach, which aids in compliance with traffic rules and overall road safety. Human Stress and Zone-Based Vehicle Speed Control is a cutting-edge, innovative, and integrated system that uses state-of-the-art technology to encourage responsible and safer driving.

articleTitle: An Experimental Analysis of Side and Bottom Loaded Truncated Conical Shape Solar Cooker
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: By using sunlight to prepare meals, solar cookers offer a more environmentally responsible option to conventional techniques. They can provide enough heat to boil water, prepare meals, or disinfect food by concentrating sunlight, which provides a sustainable way to lower energy use and lessen environmental effect. Present work shows the analysis of truncated conical type solar cooker (TCSC) with side and bottom loading of food into it and resist to heat flow through the composite slab. Aluminum tray, saw dust and outer casing comprises of composite wall. Drastic temperature drop can be seen at the slab due to the insulation provided. Various cooking vessels were used to place the food/thermic fluid inside and measured the temperature using thermocouple with temperature indicator. TCSC is loaded with thermic fluid in the cooking vessel (CV), one is placed on lugs and the other on floor of the tray. There was an increase in temperature of CV placed on lugs compared to vessel on floor. Difference of 10° – 20° was noted between CV with and without lugs in conical type cooker. Comparing CV kept on floor and lugs, lugs shown 10.4% increase in temperature of CV, reduces time for cooking.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Web Controlled Surveillance Robot using Computer Vision
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: In this paper developed a surveillance robot that uses a USB camera and web interface for remote control. The robot's unique feature is its ability to conduct real-time video surveillance in hazardous areas, eliminating risks to human safety. The robot incorporates a Raspberry Pi camera module that captures high-quality images sent wirelessly to a remote operator via a user-friendly web interface. The Raspberry Pi and camera module work together to capture and transmit clear images. A Python program controls the robot's movement and streaming functions, interfacing with the web interface through the Flask framework for smooth communication. It combines a dedication to security and safety with the ability of technology to improve society, all the while highlighting the enormous potential that Raspberry Pi can contribute to the field of defense. The results show an efficient response time of about 0.35 seconds, accurate control capabilities with an average deviation of 5%, a significant operational endurance of about 2 hours and 45 minutes, and a minimal visual latency of around 0.6 seconds. These results highlight the usefulness and effectiveness of the created monitoring system in actual situations, proving it to be an effective instrument for boosting security and safety.

articleTitle: You Only Look Once Version 8 (YOLOv8)-Driven Emergency Vehicle Detection and Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) based Traffic Signal Prioritization
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The research develops a traffic management system that integrates You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8) for emergency vehicle detection and Graph Neural Network (GRAPH NEURAL NETWORKS (GNNs))-based traffic signal prioritization to address the inefficiencies of traditional traffic management systems. These systems often fail to detect emergency vehicles accurately and adapt traffic signals in real-time, leading to delayed emergency responses and traffic congestion. The proposed system leverages You Only Look Once version 8 (YOLOv8)'s superior object detection capabilities and GRAPH NEURAL NETWORKS (GNNs)-based reinforcement learning to dynamically adjust traffic signals based on real-time road conditions. Experimental results demonstrate a 40% reduction in emergency vehicle response time and a 35% improvement in traffic flow, showcasing the system's ability to enhance urban traffic performance and emergency response efficiency.

articleTitle: IoT-based Fuel Integrity Monitoring System for Automobiles
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Fuel adulteration is a significant issue that affects vehicle performance, engine longevity, and environmental safety. Contaminants present in adulterated fuel not only degrade fuel quality but also contribute to increased fire accidents and incomplete combustion which causes harmful gas emissions. Reports from the national road safety department indicate a sharp rise in fire incidents due to fuel adulteration, highlighting the need for an efficient detection system. The proposed IoT-based fuel quality detection system addresses this issue by analyzing key fuel parameters density and temperature to determine adulteration levels. Using a load cell and temperature sensor, the system accurately measures these parameters and displays the adulteration percentage on an LCD screen, alerting consumers to potential fuel scams. By ensuring fuel purity, this system enhances vehicle engine efficiency, prevents premature engine failure, and mitigates fire hazards. The implementation of this system contributes to safer transportation, reduced environmental impact, and increased consumer awareness regarding fuel quality.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Communication Protocols (I2C, SPI) for Embedded Applications with IMU Sensor using Verilog
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Effective communication protocols are to be ensured in crucial embedded application that helps for timely data transfer in connected environments, impacting efficiency, energy use, and resource management together with parallel processing of data. Among the available protocols Inter-Integrated Circuit (I2C) and Serial Peripheral Interface (SPI) are widely used due to their distinct features for various applications and their simplicity in data transfer scheme. In this work we aim to assess I2C and SPI performance in embedded application particularly a fall detection system using Verilog HDL, focusing on data transfer rate, power consumption, latency, and hardware complexity. It is evident from the study that I2C's two-wire interface and its capacity of multi-device support make it suitable for power-sensitive applications, though it operates at lower speeds. In contrast, SPI provides high-speed, full-duplex communication but requires more GPIO pins, limiting scalability in implementation. The study offers a comparative analysis through Verilog simulations, with the help of Xilinx Hardware that helps firmware designers to choose the best protocol for their embedded applications. Results obtained emphasize the trade-offs between speed, energy efficiency, and hardware complexity, aiding in the optimization of embedded system designs.

articleTitle: Evaluating Edge Detection Algorithms for Robust Image Processing and FPGA Implementation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Edge detection is crucial in image processing and medical imaging. Various operators have been developed, including Sobel, Canny, Robert, and Prewitt. The Sobel edge detection algorithm is widely used to compute pixel intensity gradients in X and Y directions to detect edges. It applies convolutional kernels to estimate gradients, emphasizing areas with significant intensity changes. Sobel is recommended for hardware implementation due to its efficiency and minimal noise reduction. However, Sobel, Prewitt, Robert, and Canny operators may struggle with noisy images but perform well on high-quality ones. Edge detection plays a key role in image analysis. Microsoft Visual Studio and MATLAB are used for FPGA implementation and noise level assessment (SNR).

articleTitle: CMOS Ring Oscillator for Optimized 5G Mobile Communication Performance: Design and Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Oscillator circuits generate precise and reliable clock signals, essential for applications ranging from simple wristwatches to complex satellite systems, particularly in long-distance communication. These circuits can be built using either passive or active components, each with its own advantages and drawbacks. In the current era of mobile communication, the emphasis is on interoperability and low power consumption, driving the need for compact, battery-powered electronics. VLSI-based ring oscillators have emerged as an ideal solution due to their power efficiency, compactness, and wide tuning range. This paper presents a novel CMOS ring oscillator designed to function as a Voltage Controlled Oscillator (VCO). The proposed architecture combines the benefits of a current-starved ring oscillator and a negative-skewed delay, achieving optimized control and supply voltages while producing a dominant frequency with minimal harmonic distortion. By carefully selecting passive components, this design is well-suited for 5G applications that require high frequency and low power consumption.

articleTitle: Enhancing Earthquake Prediction and Early Warning Systems using CapsNet-BiLSTM Models
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: EEW are crucial for enhancing catastrophe resilience by delivering real-time notifications to individuals, governments, communities, and businesses. These devices assist in reducing damage and loss by facilitating timely intervention prior to the seismic activity impacting impacted regions. The efficacy of EEW relies on precise data processing, necessitating sophisticated methods to reduce mistakes induced by noise and data discrepancies. This research introduces a multi-phase earthquake prediction system that combines a 1D CapsNet with a LSTM network. Wavelet techniques are utilised for pre-processing to mitigate noise and outliers, hence improving data balance, while a hybrid Feature Processing Algorithm (FPA) is implemented for feature extraction. The LSTM network identifies temporal relationships in seismic data, whereas the 1D CapsNet extracts advanced features from sequential input, enhancing total prediction accuracy. The suggested 1D-Caps-LSTM model has exceptional efficacy in earthquake prediction, surpassing other methodologies with an accuracy of 95.64%. The results underscore the model's efficacy in augmenting EEW systems and bolstering disaster preparedness. The proposed architecture utilises deep learning techniques to provide a dependable mechanism for prompt earthquake alerts. Subsequent study may concentrate on real-time implementation and the expansion of the system to various geographical areas.

articleTitle: Novel Quaternary Circuits based on Hybrid GNRFET-RRAM Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper investigates the design and performance of novel quaternary logic gates implemented using a hybrid graphene nanoribbon field-effect transistor (GNRFET) and resistive random-access memory (RRAM) technologies. A comparative analysis is conducted against equivalent circuits utilizing carbon nanotube field-effect transistors (CNTFETs) and RRAMs. The proposed GNRFET-RRAM architecture demonstrates significant performance advantages, exhibiting improvements of up to 55.64%, 71.61%, and 87.43% in propagation delay, power consumption, and power-delay product (PDP), respectively, compared to the CNTFET-RRAM gates. These findings highlight the potential of the hybrid GNRFET-RRAM approach for realizing energy-efficient and high-speed quaternary logic circuits and thereby contributing to the advancement of next-generation computing paradigms.

articleTitle: Intelligent Email Spam Detection: A Machine Learning-Based Approach
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Email spam emails frequently contain dangerous material like viruses, phishing attempts, and fraudulent schemes. Email spam detection is an essential component of cybersecurity. Machine learning models are required to increase accuracy and efficiency because traditional rule-based filtering strategies are insufficient to handle developing spam techniques. This study investigates how well five popular machine learning algorithms—Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Support Vector Machine (SVM), Decision Tree, and Multinomial Naïve Bayes (MultinomialNB) to detect and categorize spam emails. Different methods are used by each of these models to examine email content and detect spam. MultinomialNB is a probabilistic classifier founded on the Bayes theorem, excels at text classification problems. By merging several decision trees, Random Forest, an ensemble learning technique, improves generalization and decreases overfitting while increasing prediction accuracy. A linear model for binary classification called logistic regression uses learned weights for several features to calculate the likelihood that an email is spam. SVM, a potent classification method, finds the best hyperplane in a high-dimensional space to distinguish between spam and non-spam emails. A rule-based approach called a Decision Tree uses a hierarchical structure of decision nodes to classify emails, making it simple to use and analyze. A dataset of tagged spam and non-spam emails is used to assess the performance of these models. To ensure a thorough evaluation of the model, the dataset is divided into training and testing sets. To compare the efficacy of the models, evaluation criteria accuracy is employed. While all models perform well, the results show that SVM offer superior accuracy and achieved 98.45% accuracy. The results emphasize how crucial it is to choose the right machine learning models depending on the properties of the dataset, available computing power, and intended performance indicators.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of Low Power High Speed Multi Bit Flip-Flop using Various Design Logics
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Power dissipation accounts for high-performance digital systems in the deep sub-micron region. As a result, power within compact systems is vital. A Multi-bit flip-flop(MBFF) is a sequential logical circuit essential for storing digital information in numerous digital gadgets, enhancing the general performance of digital circuits. Traditional MBFFs experience significant power usage and require a greater number of transistors. This paper uses conventional CMOS to investigate four distinct kinds of MBFF: transmission gates, pass transistors, and GDI gates. According to simulation findings, the suggested GDI-based MBFF has the lowest PDP. The number of transistors needed to create an MBFF is lowered in PTL compared to others. T-SPICE is used to simulate the circuits in PTM 16 nm manufacturing technology.The simulation is performed regarding the delay, power, as well as Power Delay Product (PDP) at supply voltages of 0.8 V, & 1 V.

articleTitle: Deep Analysis and Detection of Skin Disease using YOLO-NAS Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The project aims to develop a machine learning system using the YOLO-NAS algorithm to identify and classify skin diseases. The system is trained on a skin disease dataset featuring conditions like cellulitis, impetigo, athlete's foot, nail fungus, ringworm, cutaneous larva migrans, chickenpox, and shingles. YOLO-NAS enhances both speed and accuracy by optimizing its architecture through neural architecture search. Real-time detection provides immediate feedback to assist healthcare professionals in evaluating skin conditions. The methodology includes data preprocessing, model training, validation, and testing, with augmented and balanced datasets to ensure robustness. The model achieves 78% accuracy, evaluated using precision, recall, and F1 score. The project aims to revolutionize skin disease diagnosis by providing high accuracy and real-time feedback, helping clinicians make swift decisions. Additionally, the model's predictions will be made transparent to users, ensuring interpretability. By improving efficiency and delivering quick responses, this project strives to enhance skin disease management and improve clinical outcomes.

articleTitle: VANET-based Ambulance Alert System for Vicinity Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research presents a comprehensive approach to improving emergency response efficiency in urban environments through a VANET-Based Ambulance Alert System. Traffic congestion often delays ambulances, posing serious risks to critical patients. To address this, we leverage V2V communication using RYLR998 transceiver modules and ESP32 microcontrollers to detect ambulances and transmit real time alerts to nearby vehicles. These alerts, delivered through visual and auditory cues, enhance driver awareness and encourage yielding, facilitating quicker emergency response. Our methodology includes analyzing emergency response times, developing and testing the system, collecting and analyzing data, and implementing public awareness initiatives. By improving emergency vehicle navigation and reducing accident risks, this system contributes to safer roads and supports the adoption of smart transportation solutions in urban settings.

articleTitle: Vehicle Accident Detection and Alert System
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Transportation has great importance in our daily life and its development had made many of our chores much easy. With population growth, the demand for vehicles has increased tremendously, which has created an alarming situation in terms of traffic hazards and road accidents.
