The road accidents percentage is growing exponentially and so are the fatalities caused due to accidents. However, the primary cause of the increased rate of fatalities is due to delay in emergency services. Many lives could be saved with efficient rescue services. The implementation of automatic vehicle accident detection alert systems to provide timely aid is crucial. Our concept would assist in detecting an accident and determining its location, which would then be communicated to the rescue team and the rider's emergency contacts. Our vehicle accident detection alert system would also have a feature for alcohol detection, if the rider has consumed alcohol above certain limit then the car won't start and an alert would be sent.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Liquid Insulation using Molecular Sieves in Transformer Oil
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The Electrical properties of the used transformer oil have improved by using molecular sieves. This paper shows how well the UOP, Grace Davison and Zeochem molecular sieves help to increase the dielectric properties of the used transformer oil, it reduces the moisture and pollutant content present in transformer oil. Usually used transformer oil contains moisture and dust which reduces the thermal stability and dielectric strength of the oil. To avoid this Karl Fischer titration was used to reduce the moisture. After reduction, key parameters including breakdown voltage, viscosity, flash point, fire point, and acidity were evaluated. The result shows a reduction in acidity and an improvement in breakdown voltage, this result demonstrates how well the molecular sieves help to restore the insulating properties of the transformer oil. From this study, the molecular sieves help to enhance the used transformer oil life span, performance and operations in high voltage systems.

articleTitle: Adaptive Flight Stabilization System using Proportional Integral Derivative (PID) Control and Sensors
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper presents the design and development of a low-cost flight stabilizer using an Arduino microcontroller and an MPU- 6050 accelerometer and gyroscope sensor to address instability issues in small unmanned aerial vehicles (UAVs). The primary challenge tackled in this study is the accurate measurement and real- time compensation of external disturbances affecting aircraft orientation. To achieve this, the proposed system continuously acquires accelerometer and gyroscope data to compute pitch, roll, and yaw, which are processed through a PID (Proportional- Integral-Derivative) control algorithm for precise motor adjustments. Key challenges such as sensor calibration errors, noise filtering, and response lag are systematically analyzed and mitigated through optimized signal processing techniques. Experimental results validate the system’s effectiveness in maintaining stable flight under dynamic conditions, demonstrating that low-cost embedded systems can provide reliable flight stabilization for small UAV applications.

articleTitle: Design of Wireless Power Transmission Coils with Relative Position Transience
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Wireless Power Transfer (WPT) represents a transformative approach to charging, eliminating the need for physical connectors and offering enhanced convenience and efficiency. The efficiency of power being transferred across the coil is based on various parameters, which includes coil dimensions, air gap, angle of alignment and the support circuity. Literature presents the design of compensation circuity to improve the effectiveness of power transfer. This research work proposes a design of compensation circuit which maintains a constant voltage of 12V across the secondary side. In this work, significantly incorporates a Blynk app using an embedded processor which continuously monitors the system in real-time. This inclusion in WPT system which enhance the effectiveness of the control system.

articleTitle: Predicting Fuel Efficiency using Tensorflow for Sustainable Transportation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: As the automotive industry seeks to enhance environmental sustainability, predicting vehicle fuel efficiency has become crucial. This project aims to develop a deep learning model using TensorFlow to accurately predict fuel efficiency based on various factors such as vehicle specifications, driving conditions, and engine performance. A dataset sourced from the UCI Machine Learning Repository was utilized, encompassing diverse vehicle types and their corresponding fuel efficiency metrics. Through data preprocessing and model training, our approach involves employing a neural network architecture optimized for regression tasks. The results demonstrate the model's ability to provide reliable predictions, contributing to more informed decisions regarding vehicle performance and fuel management. Ultimately, this project serves as a stepping stone towards improving fuel efficiency in vehicles, promoting greener transportation solutions.

articleTitle: Soft-Starting of BLDC Motor with Model Predictive Control for Electric Vehicles using STM32
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This work introduces a soft-starting method for a Brushless DC Motor (BLDCM) based on a Voltage Source Inverter (VSI) and Model Predictive Control (MPC). The designed configuration successfully removes initial inrush currents and high starting torque. MPC provides accurate speed control by slowly raising the voltage fed to the VSI, which decreases the switching stress on the inverter. Consequently, the VSI switches handle lower frequencies, greatly reducing switching losses. The system's performance is analyzed on the MATLAB-Simulink platform for ensuring a thorough and credible analysis. Moreover, MPC provides a smooth rise in voltage during abrupt load changes, constantly updating according to iterative predictions to result in stable and controlled voltage waveforms.

articleTitle: Hybrid Utilized Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research study aims to develop a hybrid-powered electric vehicle that utilizes both solar and wind energy to reduce its reliance on traditional fossil fuels. The vehicle is equipped with a photovoltaic panel on its roof and a wind turbine mounted on a pole attached to the back of the vehicle. The project methodology involves designing and building a prototype of the vehicle, as well as conducting experiments to test its performance and energy efficiency. The vehicle is tested under various conditions, including different wind speeds, solar radiation levels, and driving scenarios. The key findings of the project demonstrate that the hybrid-powered electric vehicle with solar and wind energy is capable of achieving significant reductions in greenhouse gas emissions and fuel consumption compared to traditional gasoline-powered vehicles. The vehicle is also able to generate surplus energy, which can be stored in a battery and used to power other devices. Ultimately, the hybrid electric car driven by solar and wind energy has the potential to be a sustainable and environmentally friendly alternative to typical gasoline-fueled automobiles, as well as contribute to the creation of a more sustainable mode of transportation.

articleTitle: Analysing Shortest Path for Rescue Vehicles in Disaster Stricken City
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: In crises of urban disasters, evacuate SELSURF rescue vehicles into the affected area in real time to save lives and maximize rescues. Our work is to find the most appropriate route in a world where road networks could be attacked and destroyed. Various algorithms are used for finding the shortest path to prevent the death rate, out study focuses a famous popular shortest path algorithms emphasizing Dijkstra's algorithm and analyze its performance with various shortest path algorithms like Bellman-Ford, Johnson's algorithm, A*, and Ant Colony Optimization and proved that Dijkstra algorithm will work best in scenarios where environment is static, A* will work best in cases when environment is dense with too many objects and moreover ACO would provide that dynamic capability like real time scenarios. Our study finalizes the optimal routing strategies for emergency responders of disaster management systems and should be taken into consideration to reduce response times and save lives

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of Dual-Band Microstrip Patch Antenna for Multiple Input Multiple Output(MIMO) Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This project is all about designing a dual- band microstrip patch antenna in a 2x2 array setup, specifically for MIMO applications. The design and optimization are done using ANSYS HFSS simulation software. To overcome issues such as mutual coupling and bandwidth limitations, a 2 × 2 array configuration is proposed to improve spatial diversity and increase antenna efficiency. The antenna features an radiating plate shaped like an upside-down L is etched on an FR-4 substrate with a loss tangent as low as 0.0024. A defected ground structure is incorporated to extend the band width and improve impedance matching. The system operates at two distinct frequency ranges, 3.42-3.64 GHz and 4.91-6.62 GHz, and provides a return loss of less than-10 dB, ensuring efficient power transfer and minimal signal reflections. This design provides a reliable and high-performance MIMO wireless solution (like WiFi, UWB and 5G) that supports multiple channels and meets the requirements of today's wireless networks.

articleTitle: Simulation Modeling of a Hybrid Energy System Integrated with Electric Vehicle
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Recent advancements in electrical power grids have seen a significant integration of renewable energy sources (RESs) and a growing emphasis on leveraging electric vehicle (EV) batteries. In this article, the HRES of wind and solar PV are integrated with electric vehicles (EVs) for battery charging. With the help of HRES and Bidirectional Converter, the battery can be charged. The integration of HRES (Wind and Solar Energy System) and electric vehicle power stations brings several advantages and provides a cost-effective way. This paper discusses the Comprehensive simulation of an HRES-powered EV charging station integrated with solar panels and wind turbines using MATLAB. By using PID and FOPID controller voltage, Current and power of HRES are presented. The SOC of the battery is carried out in MATLAB by using PID and FOPID controller. The solar Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) is ensured by Solar PV-FOPID and the wind MPPT is ensured by WT-FOPID.

articleTitle: Survey on Metamaterial SRR Absorber Structures for IoT Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The evolution of IoT devices is increasingly driven by the need for autonomy through self-powering systems, presenting significant technical challenges. As demand for independent IoT solutions grows, innovative energy-harvesting systems are essential for enabling devices to function without traditional power sources. These systems capture ambient energy from sources like solar, thermal, vibration, or electromagnetic waves, addressing sustainability concerns and supporting the development of energy-efficient IoT ecosystems in resource-constrained environments. Split Ring Resonator based Metamaterial perfect absorbers (MPAs) have gained attention for their ability to achieve complete electromagnetic wave absorption within subwavelength structures. This paper reviews recent advancements in the theory, design and characterization of metamaterial absorbers.

articleTitle: Performance-Optimized EV Fast Charger using Bridgeless Switched-Inductor Cuk Converter and STSMC
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This study presents a high-performance onboard quick charging system for electric vehicles that uses a BridgeLess Switched Inductor (BLSI) Cuk converter that is managed by a premium Super Twisting Sliding Mode Controller (STSMC). By addressing the shortcomings of conventional pi controllers, the proposed solution guarantees improved dynamic responsiveness, reduced voltage and modern ripple, and improved stability under a variety of load scenarios. The BLSI cuk converter operates at greater obligation cycles and achieves excessive step-down benefit in order to prevent strength mismatches and lessen the strain on electrical switches. The addition of STSMC enhances manipulation precision and robustness while enabling faster and more powerful charging. MATLAB/Simulink simulation results and experimental validation demonstrate the recommended system's capacity to deliver superior performance, reduced factor strain, and advanced performance as a scalable solution for next-generation EV fast charging.

articleTitle: Performance Analysis of Electric Vehicle Battery Management System using Interleaved Converter Topologies
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The application of electric vehicles (EVs) is increasing at a fast rate due to pollution concerns, growing fuel consumption, and government intervention. Battery is among the most important components in EVs. Voltage fluctuation, heat, etc., during charging may adversely impact the performance of the battery. To solve these types of problems, a Battery Management System (BMS) is utilized to safeguard and optimize the battery operation. Although there are many control techniques for BMS implementation, proper selection of the converter topology is also critical for better performance. In this work, we use the Constant Current (CC) charging mode through interleaved converter topologies and examine their performance in a BMS through MATLAB/SIMULINK. Interleaved converters are employed because of their high dynamic response, high efficiency, low inductor current ripple, and high power density.

articleTitle: Smart Temperature Monitoring System with GPS Integration for Pharmaceutical Safety
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The Temperature monitoring procedure relies on an Arduino Uno Microcontroller to perform accurate real-time temperature monitoring operations. It is paired with a temperature sensor which operates as a low-cost solution for different environments. The device shows real-time temperature data on an OLED screen that delivers easily read able critical temperature readings through high-contrast display while consuming minimal power. This paper proposes a system which allows users to set custom temperature threshold levels that automatically activate warning alerts when measurements reach those preselected values to boost security applications. A Bluetooth module was integrated into the system to enable smartphone-based data transmission which allows users to monitor temperatures from their mobile phones through an application. This paper demonstrates how Arduino-based systems handle real-time temperature monitoring by providing dependable affordable solutions for temperature monitoring control and remote function control.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Solar Powered Induction Heater
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The Solar powered full bridge high frequency Induction Heater is presented in this paper. This topology is used to integrate the photovoltaic principle and electromagnetic Induction Principle. This green power system supports the cooking in residential and industrial application. The proposed high frequency induction heater is powered by power generated from the solar panel. Hence, the operating cost of the system is to be zero. The high frequency induction heater is constructed by two power electronic switches and two capacitors. By the application of this proposed high frequency inverter produces the exact high frequency ac signal for the heating element. Hence, the effective electromagnetic induction is developed and the more amount of heat generated in the bottom of the cooking pan. This inverter injects a lesser number of harmonic components. The present system supports the quality of power and maintains the reliability of the power system. The above mentioned solar powered induction heater is simulated and tested. Finally, validate the desired result of this present invention. The advantages of a solar induction heater are zero operating cost, No smoke, Utilization of green energy, Cool kitchen, Easy cleaning, No carbon emission and good efficiency.

articleTitle: Solar based Rocker Bogie Rover for Planetary Surface Exploration
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The Solar-Based Rocker Bogie Rover is a cutting-edge, IoT-capable robotic vehicle built for efficient transportation in unseemly landscapes. The device utilizes solar energy via a solar panel that harvests energy from sunlight in the form of electrical energy stored within a battery to provide an ongoing supply. The voltage sensor also keeps a watchful eye on the state of the battery for effective power handling. ESP32 microcontroller is the processor hub that maintains real-time sensing information and directs many components. An ultrasonic sensor is used for detecting obstacles so that the rover can move safely without colliding with anything. A motor driver controls the speed of the motors so that it can move in any direction with accuracy. The rocker bogie mechanism offers better stability and flexibility on rough terrain, which is ideal for planetary exploration and off-road use. A servo motor changes its angle according to distance information, which improves maneuverability for difficult terrain. IoT integration supports remote monitoring and control, offering real-time energy consumption, battery condition, and navigation route data. The rover also has a modular design, making it customizable to suit specific uses, e.g., space exploration, military reconnaissance, and search and rescue operations. Future improvements can be the use of AI for navigation and more sophisticated environmental sensors to enable better performance under harsh conditions.

articleTitle: Intelligent Task Scheduling Algorithm using Real-Time STM32 Processor
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The main aim of this proposed system is to design an efficient dynamic real-time task scheduling algorithm for autonomous vehicles in order to reduce latency, error rate and enhance the power efficiency. The Demerits of the existing model has static real time task scheduling will be solved by the high-performance ARM processor for dynamic real-time task scheduling. The FreeRTOS is used as an open-source software solution in providing better task scheduling to prioritize the sensor activities depending on the environmental factors and the user customization. The Proposed method employs an AI-based strategy for reduction in Power efficiency from 5mw to 3mw, Computational Latency reduced to 30 ms to 10 ms and improvements in resource utilization in a hard real-time system. The RTOS and STM32 based module is used for task scheduling for prioritizing data in autonomous vehicles for resource optimization, and minimal power consumption and thereby performing efficient and adaptive tasks in Self Driving Vehicles.

articleTitle: Exploring the Dark Web and Dark Nets: Contemporary Trends, Security Threats, and Future Research Directions
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research offers a thorough examination of the Dark Web's and Dark Nets' changing environment, highlighting the increasing influence these platforms have on online privacy, security, and criminal behaviour. This study investigates the revolutionary effect these hidden networks have on both lawful and illicit operations, with a focus on new trends like cryptocurrency-driven trade and sophisticated anonymization techniques. A thorough analysis of the Tor network and its changing function in preserving user anonymity in the face of sophisticated cyber threats and increased worldwide monitoring is part of the investigation. In addition, the study digs into the emerging security challenges—ransomware, AI-driven cyberattacks, and privacy risks—posed by these networks, providing insights into countermeasures such as blockchain-based security solutions and machine learning-based threat identification. The future course of the Dark Web and Dark Nets is also studied, taking into account ethical issues, legal obstacles, and possible developments like quantum-resistant encryption and decentralised anonymization methods. This study intends to contribute to a more nuanced understanding of these hidden online ecosystems, highlighting their current cybersecurity implications and anticipating future issues in an increasingly linked digital world.

articleTitle: ARP Spoofing Attack Detection to Prevent DDoS Attack
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: In today's digital landscape, cyber threats such as Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) Cyberattacks pose a serious threat to organizations, often resulting in substantial financial losses and harm to their reputation. These attacks can disrupt the availability of resources, preventing legitimate users from accessing essential services.to mitigate such threats, we propose a machine learning-based approach utilizing Support Vector Machine (SVM) and Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) algorithms. The primary objective is to monitor and analyze network activity in real time, identifying potential attack patterns. This research focuses on detecting ARP spoofing attacks, which are often used to execute Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks. We propose a real-time detection mechanism that efficiently identifies and mitigates such threats. The approach is tested in different network environments, and results show that it significantly reduces unauthorized access and improves overall security. Our findings emphasize the need for robust security measures to prevent network traffic manipulation and unauthorized intrusions.

articleTitle: Low Power PCB Design for Capacitor-based Uninterruptible Power Supply (UPS)
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: A small and effective uninterruptible power supply (UPS) circuit to provide a steady 5V output for low-power applications. The circuit makes use of BF245 JFET transistors (Q1 and Q2) to switch automatically, a 1N4007 diode for rectification, and capacitors for voltage storage and stabilization. The 4700μF capacitor (C1) serves as an energy backup, and C2 (1μF) smoothes voltage variations. Resistors R1 (10KΩ), R2 (1.8KΩ), and R3 (1MΩ) are essential to bias and stabilize the circuit for proper transistor operation. Output voltage is controlled by the 500KΩ load resistor (RL) and held at a constant 5V. The PCB design must make trace routing, thermal, and component placement optimized for efficient operation with minimal interference. Designed for uninterrupted power supply, this circuit offers smooth switching between main power and stored power, thus being ideal for sensitive electronic applications wherein momentary power interruption should be alleviated.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of Intelligent Line Follower Restaurant Servant Bot
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Customers frequently have inconsistent experiences with traditional restaurant service models because of issues like lengthy wait times, ineffective order processing, and a heavy reliance on human employees. Restaurant Servant Bot is an IoT based intelligent robotic resolution that automates order taking and food delivery in restaurants. Different customers can place orders using a table device and the list of the order is displayed with an OLED display. This device wirelessly sent the order to kitchen and assigned to the Bot. Chef read the order and prepared the order and place on the top of the Bot. The Bot autonomously navigates using line-following technology can be controlled by Bluetooth to avoids obstacles and detects food loading via weight sensors. After delivering the order it sends delivery confirmation to the central system. The Restaurant Server Bot is a cutting-edge tool designed to make dining at restaurants more efficient and enjoyable and cost effective. The outcome of this research is Restaurant Servant Bot significantly reduces service time, minimizes human intervention, enhances operational efficiency, and improves overall customer satisfaction while offering a cost-effective alternative to traditional restaurant service methods.

articleTitle: Experimental Investigation of Solar PV System using Various Partial Shading Condition
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Partial shading is another important cause influencing the output power of photovoltaic (PV) arrays for several reasons and occurs due to moving clouds, buildings, towers, and trees, which influence the system to change its pattern of power generation. Traditionally, partial shading can be ascertained in an open circuit by measuring its voltages as well as at short circuit once the load was disconnected. What is impressive is that the method does not isolate the load but, instead, uses a normal digital camera with image processing techniques in MATLAB to detect partial shading. Images of the PV array are taken by the camera, and then real-time image processing will identify the shading. The control signals generated based on the detected patterns of shading are used to energize relays that electrically reconfigure the array to maximize power output. The technique proposed will ensure efficient operation of the PV system, even at times when shaded conditions prevail. Experimental results of the proposed approach on an 80W solar system have shown the increase in power output by 12% with the help of the approach. It is highly suitable for small-scale PV plants in the range of 1 kW to 5 kW.

articleTitle: A Hybrid Signal Denoising Approach using Wavelet Decomposition and Neural Network-based Thresholding
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Signal denoising is a most important and fundamental task in signal processing. This is crucial for improving the quality of noisy data in applications like communication systems, audio processing, and biomedical signal analysis. While traditional methods such as Wavelet Thresholding and Wiener Filtering have been effective in reducing noise and also pose a challenge in balancing noise removal and signal preservation. This can be particularly observed in the presence of non-stationary noise. This paper presents a novel hybrid denoising approach that integrates Wavelet Decomposition with a Neural Network-based Thresholding. Initially the process starts with decomposing the noisy signal using the Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT). Then it is applied to a neural network to adaptively threshold the approximation coefficients. Such a process preserves detail coefficients. The denoised approximation is then used to reconstruct the signal, ensuring that both noise reduction and fine details are maintained. Experimental results show that the proposed method outperforms traditional techniques in terms of performance metrics. Mean Squared Error (MSE) for the proposed method is reduced to 0.22239, while the Signal-to-Noise Ratio (SNR) increases to 3.5143 dB, and the Peak Signal-to-Noise Ratio (PSNR) reaches 6.5289 dB. The Structural Similarity Index (SSIM) is 0.37442, indicating good structural preservation. In comparison, Wavelet Thresholding and Wiener Filtering achieve higher MSE values and lower SNR. Additionally, the Cosine Similarity of the denoised signal is 0.82984, suggesting a strong resemblance to the clean signal. The proposed technique shows promise for real-time denoising applications, offering superior performance in terms of both noise removal and signal preservation.

articleTitle: Advanced Train Detection and Gate Control System using ATmega328P and Passive Infrared Motion Sensor
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research work describes the design and application of an automatic train detection and gate control system using the ATmega328P microcontroller and Passive Infrared (PIR) motion detectors. The system is designed to improve safety and automation at rail level crossings through the detection of train movement and the control of the gate accordingly. Two PIR sensors are placed in appropriate locations to monitor the entry and exit of a train. According to sensor inputs, the microcontroller turns on LEDs for visual indication and servo motors for gate operations. The suggested design reduces human error, offers real-time response, and is energy-efficient with low power consumption. The experimental outcomes confirm that the system identifies the train presence and executes gate operations in a timely and guaranteed fashion, and thus it is a good solution for urban as well as rural railway crossings.

articleTitle: Child and Women Safety Measures using iBeacon Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: A smart real-time tracking system featuring a compact wearable device is designed to enhance the safety of children and women by utilizing IoT-driven technology and a secure database for efficient movement monitoring. This system operates on four key pillars: outdoor localization, cross-platform communication, server integration, and user engagement. The tracking mechanism comprises a wearable device embedded with an iBeacon and a built-in MEMS accelerometer, seamlessly linked to a smartphone application. The system begins with sensor calibration to establish reference values, followed by continuous tracking of sensor variations, particularly accelerometer data, to detect motion patterns with precision. Once paired with the designated Android application, the wearable device analyze movement data and transmits GPS coordinates to a centralized server, ensuring real-time location tracking of both the device and the associated iBeacon. Planned future improvements include the integration of Google Maps for enhanced real-time visualization, interactive monitoring, geofencing alerts, and emergency response notifications, making the system more robust and responsive to safety concerns.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Lithium Ferro Phosphate Battery Pack using MATLAB
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The adoption of Electric Vehicles (EV) has grown substantially due to concern about environmental pollution, fossil fuel depletion and rising fuel cost. The battery pack is the core of EV functionality, which is serving as the primary energy source. As the battery technology determines the vehicle’s range, efficiency and charging capabilities, it is a crucial component for EV performance. This paper focus on the analysis of Lithium Ferro Phosphate (LiFePO4) battery characteristics for e-bike applications. A 44V, 12Ah battery pack was developed by connecting 12 cells in series, each with a parallel connection. The main objective of this paper work is to assess the battery pack’s performance under varying load conditions. Current and voltage measurements were recorded, and MATLAB simulations were conducted to analyze input-output waveforms for different resistor values. The results provide insights into the efficiency, voltage stability, and discharge characteristics of the battery pack, offering valuable data for optimizing e-bike battery performance.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of a 4-bit Wallace Tree Multiplier using 180nm CMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper presents the design and implementation of a 4-bit Wallace tree multiplier using Analog custom-designed blocks in GPDK 180nm. The Wallace tree multiplier serves as a fundamental digital system component for rapid arithmetic operations so this research optimizes area together with power consumption by applying Analog design principles. The proposed design system eliminates complex digital logic by using partial product generation coupled with full adders and half adders and direct propagation for partial product reduction. The use of transistor level design allows the Analog approach to minimize the silicon area and power consumed by the system while retaining computational accuracy. The designing process happens through AND gates which create partial products followed by adding efficient adder circuits for iterative reduction and completing the final addition with a simplified architecture structure. The proposed multiplier shows potential for embedded and portable applications because it creates an efficient solution which combines low power usage with reduced area needs. The multiplier is designed and verified Cadence Virtuoso tools to achieve accurate simulations and optimal layout implementations in the GPDK 180nm environment.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Real-Time Landslide Monitoring using Waterbody Sensors
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Landslides pose a significant threat to human life and infrastructure, necessitating effective monitoring and early warning systems. Traditional methods often fail to provide real-time data, leading to delays in hazard response. To address this issue, an IoT-enabled real-time landslide monitoring system has been developed, integrating soil moisture sensors, vibration sensors, and GPS modules, all managed by an ESP32 microcontroller. The system continuously monitors soil saturation and ground movements, transmitting critical data via a GSM module to a remote server or mobile device. Upon detecting abnormal conditions, it triggers instant alerts to local authorities and stakeholders, enhancing preparedness and response strategies. This solution improves landslide prediction accuracy and offers a proactive disaster management approach, significantly reducing potential losses in high-risk areas. Keywords: IoT, landslide monitoring, real-time monitoring, early warning system, disaster management, environmental monitoring, soil saturation, ground movement detection, real-time alarms, location tracking.

articleTitle: Crosstalk Analysis of MWCNT based Through Silicon Vias for Quaternary Logic Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This study investigates crosstalk in coupled through-silicon vias (TSVs) for quaternary logic circuits. Using an electrical equivalent circuit model and HSPICE simulations, the crosstalk (i.e., both functional and dynamic crosstalk’s) in TSVs with multi-walled carbon nanotubes (MWCNTs) as conductors and various polymer liners (polyimide, polypropylene carbonate (PPC) and benzocyclobutene (BCB)) is analyzed and compared to single walled CNT (SWCNT)-based TSVs. The power dissipation and PDP are also evaluated. The study finds that BCB-based coupled MWCNT TSVs significantly reduce crosstalk particularly at reduced TSV heights and improved overall performance compared to SWCNT-based TSVs. Therefore, MWCNT-based TSVs with BCB liners are deemed most suitable for quaternary logic integrated circuits.

articleTitle: PCB Design of Low Noise Class D Amplifier
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper presents a PCB design for a Low Noise Class D Amplifier tailored for Home Theater applications. The circuit components, including cabinets and other modules, were carefully selected to ensure low-noise performance. Power supply and grounding techniques were meticulously optimized to enhance signal clarity. A high-performance Class D amplifier IC was employed to achieve superior efficiency. The PCB layout was precisely designed to minimize noise coupling, thereby ensuring high-fidelity audio output. These optimizations make the proposed design highly suitable for use in home theater systems. Experimental validation and simulation results confirm the design's effectiveness in delivering high-quality audio with minimal distortion.

articleTitle: Advanced Low-Power Hybrid Full Adder Design using MUX Transmission Gates and Dynamic Sleep Signal in MTCMOS Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The increasing demand for low-power electronic devices has necessitated innovative circuit design techniques to minimize power consumption while maintaining high performance. In arithmetic circuits, the full adder is a fundamental component, widely used in applications such as Digital Signal Processing (DSP), Digital Image Processing (DIP), Wireless Sensor Networks (WSN), Satellite Communication, and Arithmetic Logic Units (ALU). Conventional full adder designs suffer from high power dissipation and increased leakage currents, limiting their efficiency in low-power applications. This research addresses these challenges by proposing a 1-bit hybrid full adder that integrates transmission gate logic and XOR logic with Multi-Threshold CMOS (MTCMOS) technology. The key novelty of this design is the incorporation of a dynamic sleep signal for the sleep transistors, which significantly reduces static power consumption to negligible levels. The proposed design was implemented using Cadence Virtuoso with a 90nm GPDK technology node. Performance evaluation demonstrated a dynamic power consumption of 2.03906 μW, a critical path delay of 2.4963 ns, and a power-delay product (PDP) of 5.0918 fJ, indicating superior efficiency compared to existing designs. The results validate the effectiveness of the dynamic sleep-based MTCMOS approach, making it a promising solution for energy-efficient VLSI circuit design.

articleTitle: Linearly Flared Enhanced Antipodal Vivaldi Antenna Design
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper presents a novel linearly flared antipodal Vivaldi antenna design for Ultra-Wideband (UWB) applications, addressing the limitations of traditional exponential flaring. The proposed antenna eliminates the need for complex exponential curves while maintaining broad impedance bandwidth and improved gain. Fabricated on a compact 50 × 32 mm<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> FR4 substrate with a 1.6 mm thickness, the design ensures miniaturization without compromising performance. Experimental validation using a Vector Network Analyzer (VNA) confirms an impedance bandwidth of 1.56 GHz to beyond 15 GHz, achieving a bandwidth percentage of 174%. Measured results in an anechoic chamber demonstrate a peak gain of 13.17 dBi and an average gain of 7.61 dBi, showcasing excellent directivity. Theoretical analysis, supported by surface current distribution, further validates the effectiveness of the linear flaring approach in enhancing radiation characteristics. This design provides a compact, high-gain solution for UWB applications.

articleTitle: TZSI-Infused Adaptive Voltage Conditioning via High-Precision Vectorial Modulation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper presents a TZSI -Infused Adaptive Voltage Conditioning Topology to substantially refine the power characteristics in a grid-connected solar power setup at the Coupling Node, which is critical for mitigating disturbances and ensuring stable operation. In this approach, conventional VSI Inverters are replaced with TZSI, which offers remarkable advantages such as bidirectional voltage conversion, a wider electric potential gain range, reduced passive component requirements, and lower electric potential stress on the switching devices. To optimize the detection and compensation of voltage anomalies, while minimizing harmonic distortions in the injected voltage, a high-precision vectorial modulation framework with hierarchical multi-stage boost optimization (UVF-OCBC) is adopted. The architecture’s efficacy is thoroughly evaluated under challenging conditions, including harmonic-rich voltage dips, swells, and interruptions. To validate the effectiveness of TZSI, the system is evaluated through extensive MATLAB-based simulations and comparative analytical studies.

articleTitle: Wind Energy Conversion System using Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator and Single Ended Primary Inductor Converter with Parrot Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: A Wind Energy Conversion System (WECS) using a Permanent Magnet Synchronous Generator (PMSG) and a Single-Ended Primary Inductor Converter (SEPIC) is widely employed for efficient energy conversion and improved controllability. While PMSGs ensure reliability, SEPIC adapts to varying wind speeds, maintaining output stability. However, system efficiency may decrease due to generator and converter losses, especially at low wind speeds. The SEPIC’s switching dynamics can also increase Total Harmonic Distortion (THD), affecting power quality and load compliance. Addressing these challenges, this paper proposes an approach for WECS using PMSG and SEPIC converter. The proposed method is Parrot Optimizer (PO) The primary aim of the proposed approach is to minimize the THD, ripple factor and maximize the efficiency of the WECS. The proposed PO optimizes the operational parameters such as duty cycle, switching frequency to ensure efficient energy conversion in the wind energy system. Fuzzy logic Control (FLC), Non-Dominated Sorting Genetic Algorithm III-Finite Element Analysis (NSGA III-FEA), Jumping Spider Optimization Algorithm (JSOA) are some of the existing methods that are compared with the proposed method once it is implemented in MATLAB. The proposed PO technique achieves a THD of 0.81%, a ripple factor of 0.93%, and an efficiency of 98.5%, outperforming existing methods. This demonstrates its effectiveness in minimizing harmonic distortion, reducing ripple factor, and maximizing efficiency for reliable wind energy conversion.

articleTitle: Power Fault Analysis and Monitoring System using Simulink
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research paper presents a full system for power fault detection, protection, and monitoring with MATLAB Simulink. The model effectively identifies various power system faults like short circuits, line-to-line faults, and three-phase faults, which can lead to equipment malfunctioning, power shutdowns, and safety risks. With the aid of Simulink, the system models the fault condition and effectively examines prominent parameters like voltage drops, current surges, and power quality variations. The model features standard power system components like three-phase sources, transformers, circuit breakers, and fault blocks to simulate actual conditions. The monitoring techniques are employed to quantify system response during faults, enabling effective pattern recognition and prompt fault response. The proposed system demonstrates effective fault detection, prompt protection schemes, and optimal system recovery strategies. This research presents valuable information for power system reliability enhancement and serves as a handy guidebook for engineers and students to understand fault dynamics and protection techniques.

articleTitle: Hybrid Solar-Wind Power for EV Charging and Grid Support with Advanced Control
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The new proposed system combines the wind and solar renewable energy systems for the grid support and for charging the electric vehicle. The plant uses PV panel and wind mills in generation of power for charging the EVs and feeding the power to the grid and synchronizing battery storage system. This advanced control system shall incorporate the Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) which would assist in extraction of power both from solar and wind devices. The power converters are controlled by a Pulse Width Modulation PWM generator to convert renewable power into useful electricity. The boost-ky converter provides the benefits of regulated energy buffering and discharge, the process of restoring a system balanced state, it involved energy generation, EV charging and grid support. In the case of single phase system, the grid inverter converts DC power from the renewable sources or the battery into AC power suitable for grid export. In during the times more energy is produced than is required, the system discharges the excess to the utility favouring the balance and optimization of the electricity grid. The grid provides continuous EV charging as a backup when renewable generators are producing less power. This approach ensures that EV charging is acceptable from the aspects of sustainability, organization and cost. The stability of the system by minimizing on the utilization of non-renewable resources in energy production. This strategy presents a realistic and sustainable solution to tackle this problem of providing renewable energy into the energy and the transportation sectors.

articleTitle: Investigation of Multilevel Inverter with MultiCarrier PWM Techniques for E-Vehicle Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The proposed work investigates the application of multilevel inverters (MLIs) combined with multicarrier pulse width modulation (PWM) strategies for electric vehicle (EV) systems. MLIs are known for their capability to synthesize high-quality AC waveforms with minimum total harmonic distortion (THD), which play a vital part in enhancing the quality of power and efficiency of EV drive trains. Different multicarrier PWM techniques are also examined for their effectiveness in reducing harmonic content, improving switching efficiency, and ensuring smooth torque control. The analysis emphasizes the benefits of MLI-PWM combinations in minimizing power losses, improving thermal management, and extending battery life in EVs. However, challenges such as system complexity, voltage balancing, and control algorithm intricacies are also considered. The findings suggest that with continued advancements in power electronics and control strategies, Future electric vehicles' performance and energy efficiency will be greatly improved by MLIs using multicarrier PWM approaches.

articleTitle: Extreme Learning Machine based Smart Rose Cultivation Incorporated with IoT Sensors
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) is the network of interlinked devices with many sensors, software and other advanced technology for the communication of data. It is the widely used technology in the modern real time application. In this work we have utilized it for the cultivation of smart rose garden. It is the delightful fusion of IoT and the nature and provides better rose cultivation. The sensors of IoT can be used to monitor various parameters such as temperature, soil moisture, remote controlling and monitoring etc., the data that are collected from the sensors are stored to the cloud based server for further insightful analyzing. From the stored data, the artificial intelligence technique Extreme Learning Machine (ELM) is used to predict the various parameters such as disease, nutrient deficiency, and soil moisture level. The proposed technique effectively predicts the parameters and alerts the farmers continuously about the defects and make the rose cultivation very reliable. Simulations are Python and for smart farming Raspberry Pi based microcontroller is used. The output states that the proposed work surpasses all the existing works and provides better rose cultivation by maintain the environment as healthier as possible.

articleTitle: Utilization of Li-Fi Technology for Black Box in Ground Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Inspired by the aircraft flight data recorders, the study aims to invent a universal Black Box prototype for automobiles-for safe vehicle usage and accident analysis, plug on minimum circuitry and inexpensive model to provide complete security over the vehicle, better medical assistance for the casualty, and fast insurance claim process. It uses Li-Fi technology for enabling real-time, fast data delivery in vehicle and infrastructure communication without lag. Additionally, the Black Box also enables Car-to-Car Communication for the detection of probable collision threats through sudden movements of proximity vehicles. It also analyzes in real-time through simulation, which works towards collision risk reduction, and real-time safety improvement involves quality vehicle diagnosis and providing timely hazard information. With predictive analytics and rapid data sharing, this model gears up for intelligent transport networks that benefit emergency action and insurance processing while accident prevention is possible by proactive detection of hazards and creation of situational awareness. It is a very important breakthrough on road safety technology.

articleTitle: LexiEase AI : An AI Powered Dyslexic Support System
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The development of an intelligent, dyslexia-specific support system is the need of the hour to ensure inclusion and personalization. The work presents an artificial intelligence-driven system, which involves state-of-the-art machine learning and NLP techniques, for identifying and assisting dyslexics. Our system encompasses a broad range of dyslexia screening tests, such as phonological awareness tests, memory tests, and oral reading, for which dyslexics may be tested using state-of-the-art models like DistilBERT and DeepSpeech. A Random Forest classifier generates certain dyslexia score to classify the severity levels and give customized learning pathways. The system will also integrate document simplification, mind map generation, and writing assistance features in order to make it holistic.

articleTitle: Optimized PV Panel Control in Hybrid DC Microgrid Systems Using Whale Optimization & Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: As the demand for reliable and sustainable energy grows, DC microgrids powered by renewable sources are becoming an efficient alternative for modern power systems. This research introduces an optimized control strategy for a DC microgrid that combines solar, wind, and batteries, ensuring efficient power management and uninterrupted energy supply to connected loads. The system leverages the Whale Optimization Algorithm combined with Reinforcement Learning to enhance Maximum Power Point Tracking for solar panels, enabling real-time adaptation to changing environmental conditions. A dedicated power converter controls the DC bus voltage, and the battery circuit maximizes charging and discharging to maintain system stability. Additionally, a power flow management algorithm is developed to ensure optimal energy distribution among the three sources. The proposed approach is implemented and tested in SIMULINK under varying solar and wind conditions. Simulation results demonstrate improved energy harvesting, faster convergence, enhanced voltage regulation, and higher system efficiency. This research contributes to the advancement of smart and self-sustaining DC microgrids, providing an intelligent solution for renewable energy management.

articleTitle: Knee Rehabilitation Orthosis Extension Assistance During Walking based on the IoT Platform
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research study shows the design and development of an Internet of Things-based knee orthosis that aids in walking extension is addressed in this study. The load on injured joints during rehabilitation is the main problem addressed. To allow for real-time tracking and remote monitoring, the system incorporates biomechanical sensors such as MEMS, gyroscope, heart rate, and pressure sensors. It facilitates the healing process after surgery by redistributing weight and lowering knee compression. Personalized therapy modifications are made possible by wireless access to a cloud platform. The device's ability to enhance recovery outcomes is demonstrated by the performance evaluation, which reveals notable increases in mobility and rehabilitation efficiency.

articleTitle: A Review of Signal Processing Algorithms Techniques in Asynchronous Motor using AI
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper presents an overview of the precise models that have been utilized to investigate induction motors under faulty conditions using Artificial Intelligence techniques. A comprehensive explanation of each typical category is given, as well as the strengths and weaknesses in their capacity to replicate various kinds of flaws using AI Techniques.

articleTitle: Memristor based Crossbar Array using CNN for Image Processing Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Image processing has become one of the popular neuromorphic computing applications in recent years. Most of the application areas require an efficient and real time image processing system. Memristor is a useful memory device which plays an important role to design an image processing system and realization of hardware design. Due to the non-volatile nature of memory and less power consumption, Memristor has a huge application in the field of image processing. Being a memory device, Memristor can preserve data and parameters during processing time and reducing the need for data transfer as well as storage. In this research, Memristor in the form of CNN architecture will store the image extracted data where pixel image is given as an input and voltage pulses are generated according to the pixel value. The voltage pulses are then applied as input to the Memristor crossbars and compared with a certain threshold voltage above which an output neuron responds. The above mention system is trained for image recognition applications in real time scenarios. The real time image processing based Memristor system can have huge application areas such as medical imaging, security, computer vision and robotics.

articleTitle: Design a Real-Time Landslide Detection and Alerting System for Early Warning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Landslides pose a significant threat to life and infrastructure, particularly in vulnerable terrains. This paper presents the design and implementation of a real-time landslide detection and alerting system that offers early warnings to reduce disaster impact. The system integrates MEMS-based accelerometers and soil moisture sensors to monitor soil movement and moisture levels continuously. An ATmega328P microcontroller processes the sensor data and triggers alerts when predefined thresholds are exceeded. Notifications are sent via GSM (SIM800L) modules to designated authorities and local residents, accompanied by an audible alarm and buzzer for on-site alerts. The system is powered by a rechargeable lithiumion battery with solar support, ensuring uninterrupted operation even in remote areas.Experimental results demonstrate the system's rapid response time and high detection accuracy. By providing timely alerts, the proposed solution enhances community preparedness, rapid evacuation, and minimizes loss, making it a supports reliable tool for disaster risk reduction in landslide-prone regions.

articleTitle: Adaptive Residual Group Dual-Channel Pulse-Coupled Neural Network for Autonomous Drone Navigation in Complex Urban Wind Zones
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Drones play a crucial role in civil engineering tasks such as logistics and data collection. While existing autonomous drone research focuses on safe path planning in static environments, urban navigation remains a challenge due to dynamic factors like wind disturbances, complex building layouts, and signal interference. Traditional autonomous navigation methods struggle in urban settings, where wind variations, GPS limitations, and unpredictable obstacles affect flight stability. Most existing approaches rely on extensive external data sources, increasing computational complexity. Therefore, an efficient, sensor-based solution is required to enable drones to navigate dynamic wind zones with real-time adaptability and high precision. This study introduces a Residual Group Adaptive Dual-Channel Pulse-Coupled Neural Network with Cat Hunting Optimization (RGADCPCNNet-CHO), which leverages local RGB camera and GPS data to enhance drone navigation without relying on external inputs. The framework integrates Window-Aware Guided Image Filtering (WGBF) to refine GPS-estimated wind force with RGB camera data, while a Cswin Transformer extracts features such as obstacles, wind drift, velocity, and position. The RGADCPCNNet handles path planning, and Cat Hunting Optimization (CHO) optimizes hyperparameters for better adaptability. The proposed model achieves 99.15% accuracy, 99.14% recalls, 0.99 explained variance ratio (EVA), and a low RMSE of 0.41, demonstrating superior performance over existing methods.

Author Keywords: Residual Group Adaptive Dual-Channel Pulse-Coupled Neural Network

articleTitle: Smart Hybrid Energy Management for Renewable Energy Optimization using Random Forest Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The present hybrid energy management systems are static rule-based. They are not able to respond to unpredictable alterations of renewable energy sources and internal load dynamics which leads to poor utilization of energy and increases power losses. This work is aimed at developing Smart Hybrid Energy Management System (SHEMS), which has been based on Random Forest Algorithm for optimum control of solar, wind, hydro and piezoelectric energy sources. This SHEMS for monitoring real-time environmental, load requirements, and state-of-charge battery data with optimizing the distribution of the energy dynamically to maximize the efficiency and reliability of the system. Experimental findings indicate an increase in energy efficiency by 15-25%, drastic reductions in power wastage, and system stability improvements. Furthermore, IoT-based monitoring and control are also included in the scheme, which can further improve hassle-free operations in flexibility with future smart energy applications. These results render SHEMS a feasible and scalable solution for further-hybrid energy management in renewable energy systems.

articleTitle: Multi-Factor Vehicle Security: RFID, Fingerprint Authentication, and GSM-based Alert Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Advanced multi-user authentication systems have become vital because vehicle security incidents have increased. A Multi-Layer Authentication Vehicle Security System is developed through the integration of ESP32 microcontroller with fingerprint biometrics and RFID-based ID using the same platform. The RFID cards relate to specific fingerprints allowing different authorized users to safely access their vehicles through this system. RFID verification on EM18 modules stops unauthorized card entry into the vehicle. RF identification success allows the RS307 sensor to finalize the verification through fingerprint matching procedures. Users get three try attempts for verification following which the GSM (SIM900A) system sends an alert to the registered account holder. Low power usage combined with prompt reaction is enabled by the ESP32. Internal tests demonstrated that the GSM module reacted within three seconds while fingerprint authentication succeeded at 98.67% and RFID authentication presented 99.33% success leading to a total system efficiency rate of 98.66%. The system delivers powerful security along with secure multiple user authentications and affordable solutions to stop unauthorized system entry. Security through multi-layer authentication works by implementing various verification methods. The system will benefit from upcoming technological developments that merge cloud-based monitoring systems with AI authentication methods to enhance security and make the system more adaptable.

articleTitle: Integration of Piezoelectric and Light-Dependent Resistor Sensors for Efficient Generation and Utilization of Electricity for Pathways
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The ever-increasing demand for energy in our modern world necessitates exploration of innovative and sustainable solutions. However, the research in the integration of piezoelectric materials has highlighted limitations with respect to scalability. This research investigates the potential of piezoelectric materials for harvesting energy from everyday human movement. We look into cost-effective system utilizing piezoelectric sensors embedded under flooring to capture the energy generated by footsteps. This harvested energy can be stored in and boosted for powering devices. This research explores the utilization of piezoelectric energy harvesting technology to create electricity-generating pathways, offering a sustainable solution for powering pathway lights in urban environments. Piezoelectric sensors strategically placed along the pathway surface capture kinetic energy from pedestrian movement, converting it into electrical energy. This energy is stored in rechargeable batteries and undergoes voltage conversion to power pathway lights effectively. A light-dependent resistor (LDR) sensor ensures lights only activate when necessary, optimizing energy usage. An Arduino Uno microcontroller orchestrates light operation based on ambient light conditions. The methodology focuses on efficient energy utilization and provides a practical solution for sustainable pathway lighting. Several prototypes and studies are discussed, highlighting the potential and limitations of piezoelectric energy harvesting technology. The results demonstrate consistent power generation, high energy conversion efficiency, and cost-effectiveness, underscoring the feasibility and effectiveness of the proposed approach.

articleTitle: Smart IoT based Nutrition Alert System for Hydroponic Plant Growth
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Hydroponic farming is a soilless cultivation method that requires precise nutrient management to support plant growth and maximize yield. However, maintaining balanced nutrient levels remains a significant challenge, as improper nutrient distribution can lead to reduced crop productivity. This study presents an IoT-based nutrition alert system that continuously monitors and regulates nutrient concentrations in hydroponic environments. The system integrates IoT sensors to capture real-time data, which is analyzed using an intelligent algorithm to detect nutrient imbalances. It then provides alerts and actionable recommendations to maintain optimal nutrient levels. The proposed system ensures efficient nutrient utilization, reducing dependency on manual monitoring and intervention. By improving nutrient efficiency, the system enhances crop productivity, reduces resource wastage, and supports sustainable hydroponic farming. Experimental results confirm its effectiveness in maintaining proper nutrient balance, leading to healthier plant growth and increased yield.

articleTitle: High Precision 16-bit SAR ADC with Random Forest-based Error Correction for IoT Devices
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The demand for high precision, low power Analog to Digital Converters (ADCs) for IoT applications is steadily increasing, especially for edge devices. This paper presents the design of a 16-bit Successive Approximation Register (SAR) ADC using the Cadence tool in 45nm CMOS technology, achieving high precision while minimizing power consumption. In addition to circuit-level optimizations, we introduce a Random Forest-based error correction algorithm to enhance accuracy by compensating for nonlinearities and mismatches in the ADC. In Comparison to traditional SAR ADC designs, our proposed approach improves energy efficiency while maintaining superior Effective Number of Bits (ENOB) and Signal-to-Noise and Distortion Ratio (SNDR). Simulations confirm that the proposed SAR ADC achieves an ENOB of 15.9 and an SNDR of 54.1dB while consuming less than 4 µW, making it well-suited for IoT edge applications requiring extended battery life and accurate signal processing.

articleTitle: Proactive Purity: Predicting Water Quality with Precision
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Water pollution, driven by industrialization and urbanization, threatens public health, aquatic ecosystems, and livelihoods worldwide. Rivers, being the primary source of water for drinking, agriculture, and industry, are highly vulnerable to contamination from untreated sewage, industrial discharge, and agricultural runoff. Traditional water quality monitoring methods are expensive, time-consuming, and lack real-time capabilities.This study proposes a technology-driven water quality monitoring system capable of processing large data volumes in real-time, identifying pollution patterns, and supporting timely interventions. By integrating advanced monitoring techniques, the system enhances decision-making for water management, ensuring sustainability and ecological balance. The research highlights the critical role of technology in addressing global water pollution balance, further underlining the very important linkage between technology and sustainability.High data volumes from source water can be processed by this system, identifying patterns and trends that indicate fluctuation in water quality. this system is particularly beneficial in areas that experience seasonal and man-made causes of change in water quality. Besides its technological achievements, this project is a giant leap toward the management of water resources.The technology provides authority to decision makers. who together with environmentalists and enables easy accessibility for various tasks to make sensible decisions for drinking water supply as well as irrigation systems and pollution prevention measures for water sources. measures. It has great importance as it combines science and technology in saving vital natural resources and maintaining long-term ecological balance by tackling one of the most urgent worldwide environmental issues.

articleTitle: Hybrid Model for Enhancing Fault Detection System in Nuclear Power Plant using Support Vector Machine and Multivariate State Estimation Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Nuclear power plants (NPPs) are vital for sustainable energy production but require meticulous monitoring to ensure safety and operational stability. This study proposes a hybrid framework integrating Support Vector Machines (SVM) and Multivariate State Estimation (MSE) to enhance real-time fault detection and system reliability in NPPs. While SVMs effectively classify operational anomalies, challenges persist in optimizing kernel selection and managing high-dimensional sensor data. Our approach combines SVM’s predictive capabilities with MSE’s dynamic state estimation, enabling early detection of deviations and improved decision-making. By addressing limitations in real-time data processing and complex nuclear environments, this method supports predictive maintenance and reduces operational risks. The study reviews existing techniques and demonstrates how merging these tools advances monitoring accuracy, safety, and efficiency in NPPs. This paper explored critical gaps in the application of Support Vector Machines (SVM) for real-time monitoring in nuclear power plants (Nuclear Power Plants) and proposed a hybrid approach that combines SVM with the Multivariate State Estimation Technique (MSET).

articleTitle: AI-IoT Solution for Railway Train Collision Prevention on Identical Tracks and Animal Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: It is an IoT-based system that detects and prevents animal incidents Utilizing cutting-edge sensors and continuous monitoring on railway tracks to minimize the risk of train accidents involving animals has been a notable issue. The proposed system integrates various sensors such as LIDAR, infrared (IR), ultrasonic, and vibration sensors with an ESP32 microcontroller to detect animals and obstacles on the tracks. The system constantly observes the track and transmits the data to a mobile application (Blynk) and a web interface for real-time monitoring. The LIDAR sensor measures the distance to objects on the track, while the IR sensor detects the heat signature of the animals. The ultrasonic sensor detects obstacles in close range, and the vibration sensor detects vibrations due to trains, disturbances, etc. When an anomaly, such as an animal, is detected, the system immediately alerts the operator via the Blynk app and provides a notification on the web interface. The ESP32 CAM captures an image of the detected object for visual confirmation. The ESP32 microcontroller facilitates real-time processing and decision making, while the Blynk app provides an intuitive interface for notifications and sensor data visualization. The Web interface allows operators to monitor multiple track sections, access live sensor data, and remotely manage the system. It will save the animals on the tracks and improve railway safety by providing efficient real-time warnings and allowing immediate intervention. Using low-cost IoT components, the system provides a scalable and practical solution to reduce animal-related incidents, contributing to safer and more efficient rail transport.

articleTitle: A Systematic Literature Review on Sound Event Detection and Classification
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Sound Event Detection (SED) has appeared as a fundamental study area due to its broad applicability, including environmental monitoring, healthcare systems, in smart cities, and in industrial automation. Accurate identification and categorization of sound events are essential for developing intelligent systems capable of understanding and responding to acoustic environments. This article represents a systematic literature review (SLR) to explore the advancements and challenges in SED, focusing on feature extraction techniques and classification models. Key challenges, like background noise and overlapping audio signals, are addressed by reviewing feature extraction methods, including Mel-frequency cepstral coefficients (MFCCs), spectrogram analysis, and wavelet transforms. These strategies are foundational for capturing discriminative sound patterns required for accurate classification, and this review exposed the role of advanced classifiers, including deep learning mechanisms like CNNs and RNNs and hybrid approaches that combine machine learning techniques for improved performance.

articleTitle: MXene-Integrated Wearable Sensors for Continuous Bio-Signal Detection and Wireless Health Monitoring
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: MXenes a class of two-dimensional (2D) nanomaterials, exhibit exceptional properties, including high electrical conductivity, flexibility, and surface functionalization, making them ideal for biosensing applications. The research paper focuses on developing a flexible wireless system that monitors and records bio signals generated by human motion, utilizing MXene-based sensors. The integration of MXenes enhances sensor performance, providing superior signal resolution, sensitivity, and stability. The proposed system is lightweight, biocompatible, and designed for wearable health monitoring, capturing signals such as heart rate, muscle activity, and joint movement. The MXene sensors, integrated into flexible substrates, detect mechanical deformations caused by body movements and convert them into electrical signals. A microcontroller processes these signals and transmits them wirelessly to a cloud server or mobile application using Wi-Fi, enabling real-time monitoring and data storage. This system offers significant advantages in personalized healthcare by ensuring continuous, real-time monitoring without restricting user movement. The development of MXene-based wearable systems paves the way for innovative, cost-effective solutions in health monitoring, rehabilitation, and fitness applications, improving accessibility through low-cost fabrication and enhancing the quality of healthcare services.

articleTitle: Advances in Lightning Electromagnetic Field Sensors and Geolocation Techniques: A Review
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Lightning is still a poorly understood phenomenon. Since lightning discharges pose significant risks, including human injury, damage to electronic equipment, adverse effects on aeronautics, etc., extensive research is being conducted on this phenomenon. Lightning Location Systems (LLS) have been instrumental in reducing such threats. This review article examines various LLSs and the sensors employed in them, as well as their operational principles. These sensors detect typical electromagnetic field signatures that arise from lightning strikes, at far-off distances. Lightning activity is monitored across various spatial scales, including local, regional, and global levels, with the help of electromagnetic field sensors. This review paper summarizes various LLSs, focusing on the sensors used and their underlying operational principles. The article explores different geolocation techniques, like Time of Arrival (TOA), Magnetic Direction Finding (MDF), and hybrid approaches, emphasizing their advantages and limitations.

articleTitle: SVM-based Predictive Modeling for Sustainable Solar Solutions in Off-Grid Areas
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The rising need for sustainable energy solutions in off-grid regions has prompted the investigation of creative predictive modeling methodologies. This research examines Support Vector Machine (SVM) techniques to enhance solar energy production and use. SVM, a powerful machine learning instrument, assesses diverse environmental variables, such as solar radiation, temperature, and humidity, to precisely forecast solar energy production. It presents a SVM model to forecast solar energy production in off-grid areas, optimizing resource distribution and improving sustainability with analysis of environmental variations and energy consumption data. The model improves decision-making for deploying solar systems in distant areas using historical data and real-time observations. The prediction skills of SVM enable the creation of customized solar energy systems that address the specific energy requirements of off-grid settlements. This technique enhances sustainability by optimizing solar installation efficiency, decreasing dependence on fossil fuels, and mitigating environmental consequences. The results indicate that SVM-based predictive modeling substantially enhances the dependability and efficiency of solar energy systems, making them more feasible for off-grid applications. It highlights the capacity of advanced machine learning methodologies to promote sustainable energy solutions, hence aiding the worldwide shift towards renewable energy sources.

articleTitle: IoT-Enhanced Disease Prediction: A Machine Learning Approach to Climate-Health Interactions
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The intersection of climate change and human health has increased the need for new solutions to predict and mitigate infectious diseases. This study explores an Internet of Things-enabled, machine learning-based framework to model and analyze the interactions between climate change and health outcomes.
