IoT sensors gather real-time environmental data, which is integrated with weather patterns and disease history. Advanced machine-learning techniques are then applied to detect and evaluate potential disease outbreaks in specific regions. This approach demonstrates the potential, accuracy, and potential of early warning, providing a valuable tool for governments to deploy health services promptly. This research advances understanding of the health-security equation and provides ideas and technologies to improve global health in the face of climate change.

articleTitle: Text-to-Image Synthesis for Architectural Design: Generating Floor Plans using BERT
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Architectural design is a challenging field with limited AI applicability due to the difficulty of translating textual descriptions into visual representations. This work fills the gap by proposing a multi-modal learning framework that combines textual and visual data for AI-based architectural automation. Using BERT embeddings for text and numerical arrays for spatial composition, the approach entails data preprocessing, normalization, and structured alignment to bridge the AI-architectural intent gap. A Python-based pipeline controls text-image relationships, making it usable for automated design generation, classification, and retrieval. Experimental validation using SSIM, and expert assessment, confirms the framework's capability to generate functionally consistent and visually accurate layouts. The results show an AI-assisted design process that improves accuracy, streamlines conceptualization, and enables greater AI-architecture integration. Future work will improve attention mechanisms, increase datasets, and investigate more comprehensive architectural applications.

articleTitle: Design of Scientific Calculator using Arduino
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: In the era of digital technology, the integration of computational tools into education and professional practices has become essential. This project serves as a practical tool for students and professionals and also offers an engaging platform for learning and experimenting with embedded systems and programming. This paper presents the design and implementation of an Arduino-based scientific calculator, leveraging the capabilities of the Arduino Mega 2560. Generally, scientific calculators are built with microcontrollers that handle basic arithmetic operations. However, when additional mathematical functions are required, it leads to increased processing time and higher computational complexity. This paper covers a broad range of mathematical operations, including arithmetic, trigonometric functions, matrix calculations, numerical methods for calculus, and statistical computations for data analysis. By designing scientific calculator exemplifies the potential of Arduino in creating versatile educational tools that foster a deeper understanding of mathematical concepts. This paper aims to offer various mathematical operations, such as integration and modular expansion, allowing for easier execution and reduced time consumption. This calculator is designed to be user-friendly, efficient, and versatile, providing an affordable and customizable solution for educational and practical applications in mathematics and engineering.

articleTitle: LSTM based Pose Estimation and Sign Language Translation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: A vital communication tool for those who are hard of hearing or deaf is sign language. However, communication is severely hampered by the general public's poor comprehension of sign language. There different sign languages software for helping the deaf and dumb people. In order to use those, there is a to need specified software with high end or medium end hardware devices. In order to run-in low-end hardware devices this problem is addressed, a real- time system for translating Indian Sign Language (ISL) that uses deep learning and position estimation to enable fluid interpretation of hand and body movements with limited actions was suggested. Using a complex posture estimation architecture called MediaPipe Holistic, this method recognizes important skeletal landmarks such as torso, face, and hand points. An RNN model for deep learning that is especially made for processing sequential data, the Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) network, is used to assess these properties After training and testing the proposed model the accuracy of 95% is obtained for recognizing the actions in low wend hardware like without GPU. It shows how efficiency and friendly use of all low-end hardware devices that works on only CPU.

articleTitle: YOLOvll-Powered Real-Time Multi-User Fitness Tracking with Voice Interaction
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This study introduces a real-time multi-user fitness tracking system that integrates voice interaction to improve exercise monitoring and is driven by YOLOvll. Accurately tracking the physical activity of several users without wearing sensors while maintaining hands-free operation is the main problem addressed. YOLOvll is used by the system to accurately estimate poses, identify and track important body joints, evaluate arm motions, and categorize exercises into normal and combined lifting modes. For reliable multi-user tracking, it assigns unique IDs. It also uses a speech recognition module to interpret spoken commands for calorie data retrieval, workout mode control, and session termination. A text-to-speech engine also improves user engagement by offering real-time audio feedback. The results show that the system maintains real-time performance while accurately estimating the number of repetitions and calories burned. In addition to removing the requirement for wearable technology, this method improves accessibility and interaction, offering a practical and userfriendly way to track fitness in a variety of settings, including gyms, rehab facilities, and at-home workouts.

articleTitle: Ripeness Detection of Dragon Fruit with Temperature Factors using IoT and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The project focuses on the monitoring and prediction of dragon fruit growth stages using machine learning techniques and environmental data. The four key growth stages of dragon fruit germination, vegetative growth, flowering, and fruiting are analyzed in terms of their optimal temperature requirements. The VGG16, a pre-trained Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) is used to extract relevant features from images captured at each growth stage. The extracted features are then passed to a Long Short-Term Memory(LSTM) network, which processes the sequential data to learn temporal dependencies between growth stages. The LSTM network is designed to predict the future growth stage of the dragon fruit based on the temporal sequence of features extracted from the images. This approach allows for more accurate predictions of the plant’s development, which can aid in better understanding and optimizing cultivation conditions. Alongside environmental data such as temperature and humidity of the field are continuously monitored to ensure optimal growth conditions. These conditions are displayed in real-time, facilitating timely adjustments to the cultivation environment. By combining the power of deep learning and environmental monitoring, this system enables more efficient and precise management of dragon fruit cultivation.

articleTitle: Advanced Time Series Load Forecasting for Distributed Energy Resources with IoT and Deep Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: To improve operational efficiency and reliability, new load forecasting methods are required for integrating Distributed Energy Resources (DERs) into power networks. This paper introduces a new time series load forecasting method that uses Deep Learning techniques, notably Radial Basis Function Networks (RBFNs) and Internet of Things (IoT) data. The proposed approach uses real-time data from IoT sensors to identify complex patterns and variations in energy use. The RBFN design is tuned for high-dimensional input data; it has the potential to predict load demand for DERs with greater precision. With significant decreases in prediction error, the experimental findings show that the RBFN model works better than traditional forecasting techniques. This development promotes sustainability in power systems by efficiently integrating renewable energy sources and improving energy management. In distributed energy management, the results highlight the possibility of integrating deep learning methods with IoT technology to improve load forecasting capabilities. It addresses the issues of load forecasting for DER with use of IoT technology and RBFN. The enhanced model increases accuracy providing improved grid stability, energy efficiency, and real-time demand regulation.

articleTitle: Optimizing Prosthetic Limb Designs using the FEA Simulation and AHP Method
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Currently about 35-40 million people worldwide require prosthetics, the scale of this issue is significant. However, the problems only prolong from there: not only are there limb rejects, the costs of these limbs are beyond a large proportion of the population’s income, the constant maintenance as well as the lack of specialized prosthetics such as those for athletics are only a few of the many more problems associated with this issue. To address this, this research paper goes into depth into research to determine primary factors to create a prosthetic and thus uses these factors to create an AHP matrix to analyze the relative importance of each factor and help the user choose a prosthetic best suited to them and their lifestyle. Using these factors, an ANSYS simulation was developed on different models to visualize the load using FEA and understand how it could be improved. Lastly, the TOPSIS method was implemented to rate the different models before the final model could be developed. The high rating of the running model on the ANSYS simulation and its close second rating in the TOPSIS calculations, resulted in that model being developed for the final design. A combination of primary, through interviews of prosthetic limb centers, and secondary, through official government websites, design websites as well as other websites of official organizations, such as WHO, to ensure high quality data and accuracy. The final features taken into consideration for the prosthetic were: weight, cost, material and application. Some other features implemented into the design were: an adaptable height feature, a steel spring blade to minimize the energy lost and topological optimization to future reduce the weight of the prosthetic, as a result the user gets a comfortable prosthetic well suited for their application.

articleTitle: AI-Driven IoT System for Real-Time Fish Behaviour Monitoring and Automated Feeding in Smart Aquaculture
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper aims at the method of overcoming inefficiency and ecological problems as well as labor scarcity in existing aquaculture with the help of IoT-based Intelligent Aquaculture System. IoT sensors, AI analytics and automated control are woven in the system to take overall feeding, water quality and fish health management. Major takeaways: cut feed water by 20-30%, fish growth rates up 10-15%, fish mortality rate could go down to 10-20%, manual operations carrying 30-50% based reduction, and also energies consumption could reduce with another 20-30%. The real-time monitoring and the automated response to deviations from set point of the system considerably improves productivity as well as reduces operating costs enabling sustainable aquaculture. In this research, the transformative potential of combining AI and IoT in smartening-up of aquaculture practices for global food security is demonstrated.

articleTitle: Analysis of Batch Entry Lining Model with Mandatory Excursions and Stochastic Repair Delays
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Performance under steady state conditions is investigated a model for non-Markovian batch arrival queuing with servers taking extended and brief vacations. In a Poisson stream with batches of varying sizes, clients arrive at the system. A mandatory long vacation or a mandatory short vacation of chance ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf> may be chosen by the server with probability ω<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">1</inf> at each administration completion age. The service channel is presumptively susceptible to breakdowns, and when one occurs, it delays for the repairs to begin. This delay period occurs in two phases. The administration time, delay, short get-away, lengthy vacation time and the redesign process forms are distributed in this manner. Utilizing supplementary factors, we employ the additional variable approach. Under constant state conditions, we derive the line estimate appropriation for any age. In addition, we determine several essential system execution metrics. This broadens some models considered by a few writers. Finally, two fascinating individual examples are explored. Numerous numerical demonstrations have also been done to validate the authenticity of the hypothetical consequences.

articleTitle: Deep Learning and Optimization Algorithms for Intelligent Cloud Resource Allocation: A Survey
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: With the arrival of the cloud computing, modern IT infrastructure has been transformed by the ability to provision resources on demand and scalable over the internet. Nevertheless, due to the dynamic and heterogeneous nature of user demands, such resource utilization, energy consumption, and service quality are difficult to achieve efficiently. The focus of this paper is to provide comprehensive survey of artificial intelligence (AI) based approaches, namely machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) models for predictive resource scaling in cloud environment. It studies combining Neural networks, Ensemble models and Metaheuristic optimization for forecast of Resource Demand and increase the accuracy of allocation. Challenges addressed are minimizing energy usage, lowering operational cost and meeting service level agreements. This survey also presents recent results for feature selection, hybrid optimization and performance tuning strategies appropriate for cloud systems. The insights from this work are meant to assist the further research in intelligent, adaptive, and sustainable cloud resource management.

articleTitle: An Efficient Privacy-Centric Architecture for Smart Home Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: In homes, to operate the home securely is a significant aspect and is challenging in terms of user misbehavior, network vulnerabilities, and data breaches by malicious actors in the operation. Threats like exploitation, and eavesdropping would affect home operations and compromising the sensitive data. The risks increase when the number of devices increases. The scenario demands robust secure architecture in which three aspects are ensured such as decentralized management, advanced security algorithm to avoid privileges misuse, and protect the sensitive information using defense in depth mechanism. The advantage of this system is to provide user data with more security while maintaining system’s efficiency. There are significant practices to be applied such as updating of latest security patches, avoiding physical tampering and theft, strong encryption protocols, strong passwords, and educating users. It exercises key aspects such as physical, data, network, and device. The significant factors considered for the effectiveness of this system are accuracy and cost-effectiveness. The pinpoint considered is home door security, and outcome is accuracy.

articleTitle: Energy-Efficient Wireless Sensor Networks Optimization using Deep Q-Networks for Smart Energy Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Energy efficiency poses a significant difficulty in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs), especially within smart energy applications like smart grids, energy monitoring, and predictive maintenance. This study presents an adaptive optimization approach based on reinforcement learning utilizing Deep Q-Networks (DQN) to improve energy efficiency in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) through the dynamic adjustment of transmission power and routing algorithms. The suggested model is trained and assessed utilizing the LEACH (Low-Energy Adaptive Clustering Hierarchy) dataset within a simulated NS-3 and MATLAB environment. The simulation configuration comprises 100 to 500 sensor nodes distributed inside a 100m x 100m region, each with differing energy limitations, utilizing the IEEE 802.15.4(Zigbee) communication protocol. The performance evaluation is carried out under varying traffic loads and network density, contrasting the proposed DQN-based optimization with classic LEACH, GA-based clustering, and Q-learning models. The results indicate a 27.5% enhancement in network longevity relative to LEACH, a 21.8% decrease in energy consumption per node, an 18.3% advancement in packet delivery ratio, and a 16.7% reduction in end-to-end latency, hence providing dependable data transfer. The findings underscore the efficacy of reinforcement learning in prolonging the lifespan of wireless sensor networks and enhancing energy efficiency, rendering it exceptionally appropriate for practical smart energy applications, including power grid monitoring, industrial IoT, and renewable energy management. The proposed DQN-based optimization dynamically adjusts transmission power and routing strategies, resulting in significant energy savings and improved network performance

articleTitle: AI-Assisted IoT System for Real-Time Electricity Theft
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Electricity theft is a recurring global problem that prevents effective energy distribution and causes significant financial losses for utility corporations. Conventional detection techniques are inefficient, labor-intensive, and prone to errors since they frequently depend on human procedures. This study presents a novel Internet of Things (IoT)-based system for monitoring and detecting electricity theft in real time. Leveraging smart meters and IoT-enabled sensors, the system continuously monitors electricity usage to identify anomalies indicative of unauthorized consumption. Advanced machine learning algorithms analyze collected data to detect theft patterns with high precision. Upon identifying irregularities, the system promptly notifies utility providers and authorities, enabling swift corrective actions. The proposed solution offers a cost- effective and scalable approach for monitoring and securing power distribution networks, significantly reducing revenue losses and improving operational efficiency. Comprehensive simulations and real-world testing validate the system’s reliability, demonstrating its potential to revolutionize electricity theft prevention and enhance the sustainability of energy management systems.

articleTitle: Modelling of Five Level Asymmetric Inverter based DSTATCOM for Power Quality Enhancement using Optimized FOPTI-FOPTID Controller
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper addresses the growing power quality challenges in distribution systems stemming from nonlinear loads and power electronic devices, by introducing a novel five-level asymmetrical multilevel inverter (MLI) based Distribution Static Compensator (DSTATCOM). Unlike conventional approaches, our design minimizes switch and DC source count, enhancing system simplicity and efficiency. To optimize the MLI's switching pulses, we implemented a cascaded fractional-order proportional Tilt integral (FOPTI) and fractional-order proportional Tilt integral Derivative (FOPTID) controller, finely tuned using the Enhanced Pufferfish Optimization Algorithm (EPOA). Simulation results, generated in MATLAB/Simulink, validate the effectiveness of our approach, demonstrating the MLI's ability to achieve five distinct voltage levels. Notably, our optimized DSTATCOM significantly improves power quality, achieving a total harmonic distortion (THD) of 3.96% while maintaining a high system efficiency of 98%. This research presents a substantial advancement in DSTATCOM design, offering a practical solution for enhancing power quality in modern distribution grids.

articleTitle: Design of a Temperature Dependent Industrial Lighting
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper investigates the impact of high ambient temperatures on LED-based industrial lighting systems and proposes an optimized thermal management approach to enhance efficiency, longevity, and performance. Industrial environments such as thermal power plants, metal manufacturing units, and pumping stations experience extreme temperatures exceeding 60°C, which significantly affect LED luminous output, efficiency, and durability. The study analyzes the degradation of LED performance due to thermal stress and evaluates heat dissipation techniques, including heat pipe integration and optimized driver designs. Experimental results demonstrate that proper thermal management can mitigate efficiency losses, extend LED lifespan, and improve overall energy savings. The findings provide a framework for designing reliable high-temperature LED lighting systems for industrial applications.

articleTitle: IoT based Speed Control Monitoring and Accident Avoidance using AI Traffic Sign Detection
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Traffic accidents are a major concern, often caused by driver errors such as speeding and distractions. This paper presents an IoT-based intelligent system for speed control monitoring and accident avoidance using AI-powered traffic sign detection. The proposed system leverages a Multitasking Convolutional Neural Network (MCNN) to detect traffic signs in real-time, analyze vehicle speed, and ensure compliance with road safety regulations. The system is designed to operate by capturing real-time road images using a vehicle-mounted camera, processing these images through an AI-driven recognition system, and integrating with a vehicle’s Electronic Control Unit (ECU) to monitor speed. Upon detecting a traffic sign, the system extracts its features, classifies it using MCNN, and determines the appropriate action. If a speed limit sign is detected and the vehicle exceeds the permitted speed, the system triggers an alert for the driver. If the violation persists, it automatically regulates the vehicle's speed through the ECU. Additionally, seat belt detection is incorporated using an interior camera to ensure driver safety. The system employs IoT for continuous data transmission, allowing remote monitoring and analysis. The combination of AI, IoT, and embedded control mechanisms enhances the effectiveness of traffic management and accident prevention. Experimental results demonstrate enhanced precision in recognizing traffic signs, emphasizing the capabilities of the system for deployment in smart transportation solutions.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of an IoT-based Emergency Alert and GPS Tracking System using MQTT and GSM/GPS Module
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: An optimally optimized emergency response system can prove to be lifesaving by reducing response time during the state of emergency. This paper proposes an IoT-based emergency alert and GPS tracking system implemented on an ESP32 microcontroller and an A9G GSM/GPS module. The system has a continuous log of user position and device battery level and pushes data in intervals through MQTT to the Adafruit IO platform for remote monitoring. To achieve best battery life, the A9G module goes into low power mode in idle mode but keeps GPS monitoring running. One more feature highlighted is the SOS button, which makes an emergency call by sending the user's location as an SMS and calling a pre-configured contact number. The system also maintains data integrity with automatic reconnect of MQTT broker when it loses connection. Low power and battery portable, the system is applicable in personal protection, home health care for elderly, outdoor adventure, and remote area surveillance. The article explains hardware design, software process, MQTT-based data communication, and testing of the performance of the system based on precision, network, and response to emergencies. The results verify reliability and cost saving of the system in real-time monitoring and reporting of emergencies. With its energy-saving and usability design, it helps in the development of IoT-backed safety solutions for real-time tracking and emergency response in case of a need.

articleTitle: Hybrid Weather Station and Solar Tracking System for Renewable Energy Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The suggested technology increases solar energy collecting efficiency by combining dual-axis sun tracking with weather monitoring. To maximise sunshine exposure all during the day, the system automatically orient solar panels along the azimuth (horizontal) and elevation (vertical) axes. An Arduino microcontroller forms the core control unit by processing real-time data from environmental sensors like DHT11 (Temperature and Humidity) and Rain Sensors. Furthermore, utilized to detect the strength of the sunlight and modify the location of the solar panel are light-dependent resistors (LDRs). Servo motors run the tracking system; they enter sleep mode while solar intensity stays constant, lowering power usage. A 12V battery charging mechanism is also part of the system to save the created electricity for continuous running. Offering an 8% energy efficiency gain and operating cost savings, the twin-axis solar tracker significantly boosts energy production over fixed solar panels, according to trial data. This study emphasizes the possibility of using intelligent control systems and renewable energy technology for environmentally friendly purposes.

articleTitle: Self Attention-based Sparse Graph Convolutional Neural Network for Instant Parameter Prediction to Optimize Wireless Sensor Network Performance in Electrical Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: WSNs function as key components across environmental monitoring systems as well as healthcare facilities and industrial automation networks. WSN performance optimization faces ongoing challenges because the networks must deal with restricted energy supplies in addition to shifting operational environments and restricted data transfer capabilities. The current optimization techniques implement static hierarchical approaches combined with heuristic methods yet these prove unable to adjust in real-time thus leading to deteriorating network conditions and resource inefficiency. The research puts forward Self Attention-based Sparse Graph Convolutional Neural Network (SA-SGCN) as an instant parameter prediction framework to optimize WSN performance through automatic adjustments of critical metrics including energy usage and packet success ratios as well as latency and data transfer speed. Real-time prediction becomes possible through the self-attention mechanisms used in SA- SGCN models to detect distant dependencies in the sensor network in combination with sparse graph convolution that decreases computational requirements. The Crested Porcupine Optimizer (CPO) optimizes the hyperparameters of the SA- SGCN model for better efficiency and accuracy measurement. The experimental evidence shows that using the proposed method results in superior performance compared to current approaches because it reaches a prediction accuracy level of 99.9% for WSN configurations. The research presents a dependable energy-efficient adaptive framework for WSNs which enables high scalability and reliable operation within fast-changing environments.

Author Keywords: Self Attention-based Sparse Graph Convolutional Neural Network

articleTitle: Energy Management for PV-Powered EV Charging With Grid Integration and Battery Energy Storage System using Dung Beetle Optimizer
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: An Energy Management (EM) System for Photovoltaic (PV)-powered Electric Vehicle (EV) charging with grid integration and Battery Energy Storage System (BESS) optimizes energy consumption by integrating renewable energy, storage, and grid capabilities. However, drawbacks include the high initial costs associated with installation and infrastructure, as well as on-going operational costs for managing and maintaining both the storage and charging systems. Furthermore, the intermittency of solar energy can lead to inefficiencies in utilizing Renewable Energy Sources (RESs), requiring additional storage capacity to ensure a reliable power supply, while emissions from battery production, operation, and disposal may counteract some of the system’s environmental benefits. To overcome these drawbacks, this manuscript proposes an approach for EM for PV powered EV charging with BESS. The suggested method is Dung Beetle Optimizer (DBO). The major objective of this work is to reduce operational costs, improve energy efficiency, and lower carbon emissions by improving the use of renewable energy, minimizing grid reliance, and optimizing battery storage operations. The DBO optimizes the scheduling of EV charging, the operation of battery storage (charging and discharging cycles), and the interaction with the grid. Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Genetic Algorithm (GA), Adaptive Interaction Artificial Neural Network (AI-ANN) and Adaptive Neuro Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) are some of the existing methods that are compared with the suggested method once it is implemented in MATLAB. By achieving the lowest operational cost of 0.121M$/year and reducing carbon emissions to 505.73ktons, the suggested DBO method outperforms traditional approaches while maintaining high energy efficiency and environmental sustainability in PV-powered EV charging with BESS.

articleTitle: AI-Driven Optimization in Power Electronics: Enhancing Efficiency and Performance
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Power electronics systems demand more energy efficiency, better power loss margins, and improved stability. Traditional control techniques such as Fixed Switching Frequency Control (FSFC) and Fuzzy Logic Control (FLC) are limited due to their lack of fast response, adaptability, and performance in dynamic load conditions. This research presents an AI-based optimization framework by implementing machine learning-based control with AI-driven optimization for predictive decision-making. The optimization framework can enhance energy efficiency by 6.3 percent relative to FSFC and 2.5 percent relative to FLC, decrease power losses by 27.4 percent, and improve thermal stability by 14.5 percent. Furthermore, the response time improved by 38.2 percent, allowing for faster adaptation to load variations. The AI-based optimization approach effectively minimizes overall switching losses and system reliability. The experimental tests demonstrate that AI-based optimization can achieve significantly better outcomes than traditional approaches, demonstrating a scalable and adaptive system in support of smart power electronics and energy management and establishing a foundation for intelligent and more efficient power-control system development.

articleTitle: Real-Time IoT Cybersecurity using Machine Learning-based AI Threat Detection System to Train Generative Robots
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Existing security protocols encounter major cybersecurity difficulties because the online devices' growing popularity continues to spread across networks. These security protocols are ineffective because they do not properly handle current cyber threats. The main goal of this study involves developing enhanced IoT cybersecurity through the development of a threat detection system which brings together adversarial training and deep learning models (CNN-LSTM) and Federated Learning (FL). The system enables distributed Internet of Things devices to work on security model development through Federated Learning while maintaining total privacy of their information. Security procedures controlled by generative artificial intelligence robots alongside real-time attack protection functions decrease security response durations. Through its Federated CNN-LSTM model the system upholds a 1.2% false positive rate alongside a 98.3% accuracy evaluation and 160 milliseconds of exact threat tracking time. The designed system sustains a minimal occurrence of incorrect alarm activations. The developed system provides real-time security for the Internet of Things framework because it enables adaptive protection systems while preserving user privacy in current IoT settings.

articleTitle: Quantum Teleportation: A Paradigm Shift in Secured Communication using Quantum Entanglement
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Quantum teleportation is a new method in quantum communication that allows quantum states to be sent securely using entanglement and classical signals. This research focuses on problems like maintaining strong entanglement, dealing with quantum noise (decoherence) and handling delays in classical communication, which currently limit practical applications. To solve these problems, we built and tested a quantum teleportation circuit using simulation tools and visualized the results using Bloch spheres and statevector analysis. Our results show that quantum states can be teleported accurately while preserving their properties. This proves quantum teleportation is practically achievable and can be used in secure communication, quantum networks, and quantum computers, making it an important step towards building a reliable quantum internet.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicle Charging Demand Prediction using Multiresolution Sinusoidal Neural Network Optimized with Addax Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Electric Vehicle (EV) charging demand prediction, while essential for optimizing charging infrastructure and energy management, faces challenges such as data inaccuracies and uncertainties in user behavior patterns. These issues define inaccurate demand forecasts which cause the wrong placement of charging stations and distribution of energy. Also, as the pattern of the EV charging is not static may change due to many factors such as climate, time of day, price preference among others, the prediction models may not handle the dynamism and hence lower the reliability of the forecast results. To overcome these drawbacks, this manuscript proposes an efficient approach for EV charging demand prediction. The data is gathered from a dataset on EV charging. The data is then sent to pre-processing. Using the Maximum Correntropy Quaternion Kalman Filter (MCQKF), the pre-processing section eliminates missing values and normalizes the input. To forecast EV charging demand, the Multiresolution Sinusoidal Neural Network (MSNN) receives the results of the pre-processing data. MSNN’s weight parameter is optimized using Addax Optimization (AO). The proposed MSNN-AO is utilized within the MATLAB platform. The proposed MSNN-AO technique is compared with the existing techniques such as Long Short-Term Memory Neural Network (LSTMNN), Heterogeneous Spatial-Temporal Graph Convolutional Network (HSTGNN) and Artificial Neural Networks (ANN), respectively. The MSNN-AO method achieves an accuracy of 97%, precision of 95%, and a Root Mean Square Error (RMSE) of 2.2%, demonstrating its superior performance in predicting EV charging demand. This highlights the proposed method’s effectiveness in minimizing prediction errors, reducing RMSE by 22.36%, and improving precision by 14.89% compared to existing methods. The MSNN-AO method’s higher accuracy and precision, coupled with its robust performance, make it a reliable and efficient solution for EV charging demand forecasting.

articleTitle: Employing Machine Learning Algorithms for the Prediction of Alzhiemer’s Disease
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Alzheimer's disease is a neurological condition that progressively worsens over time and impairs thinking, memory, social skills, and behavior. Its onset is most commonly seen in the age groups above 65. The World Health Organization's survey indicates that dementia, including AD, is the sixth largest cause of death globally. For older people, this is the most frequent cause of dementia. The word dementia is used to refer to a wide range of brain disorders that are characterized by behavioural abnormalities, loss of memory and reasoning skills, and difficulty carrying out everyday tasks. In order to lower the death rate, early screening for this condition is essential. Machine learning techniques are quite useful in the identification of the relation between risk factors of Alzheimer’s disease and its incidence. This study examines the relationship between several characteristics that lower the risk of Alzheimer's disease using a benchmarking dataset of 2149 Americans. Early detection of AD and associated symptoms is more successful when classifiers such as Random Forest, Support Vector Machine, K-Nearest Neighbours, XGBoost, CatBoost, and Logistic Regression are used. Classifier performance and AD predictions are evaluated using metrics like as F1-score, Precision, Accuracy, and Recall. According to this suggested study, the Random Forest and CatBoost algorithm predicts the test data with 95.5% accuracy. This score is better than the other modern and latest algorithms.

articleTitle: Designing an Adaptive Intrusion Detection Model for IoT Smart Homes using Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Security threats are now a major concern for smart homes because of their expanding IoT device population. The security methods from traditional times fail to tackle the specific difficulties that arise with IoT ecosystems because of their limited resources and different devices and changing network patterns. A new IDS design built from deep learning components specifically for IoT homes exists as the foundation of this research. The proposed intrusion detection system uses a combination of CNN and LSTM networks to boost detection performance without generating large numbers of false alerts. A set of experimental results shows that the proposed intrusion detection system delivers superior outcomes than existing methods by achieving high accuracy together with quick responses and precise results. The research confirms how deep learning security solutions protect the IoT environments found in smart homes.

articleTitle: AI-Enhanced IoT Systems for Smart Predictive Maintenance in Steel Plants
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper introduces a smart Internet of Things (IoT) system that uses artificial intelligence (AI) to improve operational efficiency and reduce downtime in steel plants through predictive maintenance. It addresses equipment failures in steel plants with deployment of an AI-driven IoT system using neural networks for facilitating accurate defect prediction and minimizing maintenance expenses. The system uses neural networks for continuous operation and proactive maintenance, which are essential in steel production processes to provide productivity and safety. Early problem detection and health monitoring are made possible by integrating IoT devices for real-time data gathering and cloud computing for scalable data processing in the proposed system. Anomalies and impending breakdowns may be foreseen using neural networks trained on time-series sensor data, paving the way for predictive maintenance. The solution improves equipment dependability, optimizes maintenance schedules, and decreases operating costs using historical data and machine learning algorithms. Results from real-world applications show that the system may enhance maintenance plans while reducing downtime in steel manufacturing facilities. The results highlight how technology may revolutionize maintenance procedures, gain insight into proactive equipment management, and help the steel sector progress in smart production.

articleTitle: Deep Reinforcement Learning for Energy Efficiency Optimization using Autonomous Waste Management in Smart Cities
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Smart cities face vital waste management challenges regarding efficiency and sustainability in their development period. The established waste collection approaches that depend on pre-set schedules together with unchanging routes create problems by possessing both inefficient resource usage and elevated fuel usage as well as delayed waste pickup times. The proposed framework builds a Deep Reinforcement Learning (DRL)-based system for dynamic waste collection route optimization using Autonomous Waste Collection Vehicles (AWCVs) with Internet of Things (IoT)-based smart bins. The system uses Deep Q-Networks (DQNs) to analyze traffic conditions data alongside vehicle battery level data with smart bin information from the system so vehicles carry out efficient waste collection operations using minimal energy. The newly proposed algorithm provides 30% distance reduction and 28% faster responses and 30% lower energy usage than baseline heuristic methods do. The conclusions show that AI-powered waste management strategies can create sustainable operations which increase both service performance and overall energy efficiency in cities. The research team plans to apply the proposed approach to actual waste collection systems while exploring methods of deploying multiple agents alongside renewable energy systems to enhance future urban waste management operations.

articleTitle: Real-Time Personnel Localization and Health Monitoring System for Emergency Evacuations in Underground Mining Operations
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Underground mining poses serious threats to miners in the form of cave-ins, explosions, fire, and poisonous gas exposure. Traditional localization techniques tend to fail under such extreme environments, and emergency response is delayed. This paper introduces an indoor real-time localization system that improves miner safety through the combination of an ADXL345 accelerometer, heart rate (HR) and blood oxygen (SpO2) sensors, and iBeacon technology. The system repeatedly tracks miner mobility and vital parameters to identify distress and initiate interventions at the appropriate time. An individual identification number (UID) is assigned to every worker that is saved on the controller to track them specifically. Location, UID, and health information is sent through a GSM module to a central controller system for immediate monitoring. Experimental results show better localization accuracy and quicker emergency response time, making this system a safe and efficient solution for underground mine safety improvement and evacuation optimization.

articleTitle: Optimal Charging Control of No-Insulation HTS Magnets using Pontryagin’s Principle and Advanced Nizar Optimization Technique
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: High-Temperature Superconducting (HTS) magnets employing No-Insulation (NI) and Controlled-Insulation (CI) winding techniques are widely used in particle accelerators and industrial applications due to their enhanced stability and self-protection features. However, these magnets suffer from extended charging times, excessive heat generation, and inefficient energy utilization, limiting their practical performance. Traditional optimization approaches, struggle with long convergence times, overshooting effects, and computational inefficiencies. To address these limitations, this work integrates Pontryagin’s Minimum Principle with the Nizar Optimization Algorithm (PMP-NOA) to optimize the charging process of NI and CI HTS magnets. The system is modeled using a lumped-element circuit approach, capturing azimuthal and radial currents, operative current, voltage drop, and heat generation dynamics. The optimization framework is formulated using a cost function that minimizes charging time and heat dissipation, incorporating constraints on current, temperature, voltage, and cryocooler power. To efficiently solve the problem, Hamiltonian-based optimal control is applied, and the metaheuristic NOA method enhances search efficiency using effective mixing and transformation mappings. The PMP-NOA framework significantly outperforms existing methods, achieving the fastest charging time (220s, 15-29% improvement), lowest temperature rise (3.2K, 28-75% reduction), minimal current overshoot (6%), and highest steady-state accuracy (1.2%). Additionally, it reduces power dissipation (75W, 13-40% improvement) while requiring fewer iterations (10³), making it the most computationally efficient approach. This work establishes PMP-NOA as an optimal control strategy for improving the efficiency, stability, and practicality of HTS magnet applications in high-performance environments.

articleTitle: Smart Information System for Motorcycle
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The performance of a motorcycle and safety depend on routine maintenance. Monitoring of the key parameters reduces the risk of accidents and saves lives. This work introduce an innovative hardware attachment and mobile application (APP) aimed to improve motorcycle safety, maintenance, and security. The suggested system uses various sensors to monitor essential factors such as tyre pressure, oil level, oil viscosity and fuel level with the mileage of the motorcycle. When these parameters fall below the predetermined threshold values, the Bluetooth-connected mobile APP immediately alerts the user by notifications. In addition to the maintenance alerts, the system covers the motorcycle with a GPS and position sensing system. An alert message or call will be automatically sent to designated family members or a helpline, along with the geographical location in the event of a minor or major accident, if any. Furthermore, owner may know the location of their bike in real-time, increasing security measures against theft. The system protects the motorcycle against accidents and inefficiency caused by poor maintenance, and provides effective theft prevention measures with location monitoring.

articleTitle: Bi-Directional Power Control in Grid-Connected Electric Vehicle On-Board Chargers using Spider Wasp Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The bi-directional power control in electric vehicle (EV) on-board chargers aims to maximize charging performance while minimizing size and cost of the system. This presents an increasing technical challenge that further complication of thermal management through greater integration of power conversion components may impact system reliability, efficiency, and longevity. By address these issues this paper proposes a Spider Wasp Optimization (SWO) for enhancing stability in bi-directional power control in EV on-board chargers. The objective is to minimize Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) in EV on-board chargers. By optimizing the converter's parameters, SWO effectively reduces harmonic distortions, leading to improved power quality and smoother operation of bi-directional power control in EV on-board chargers. By then the proposed SWO method is implemented in MATLAB platform and evaluated their performance with various existing methods such as Improved Particle Swarm Optimization (IPSO), Intelligent Neural Herd based Water Drop Optimization (INHWDO), Squirrel Wolf Optimization algorithm (SWOA), Wild Horse-Particle Swarm Optimization (WHPSO) and Assailant Inspired Chimp Optimization Algorithm (AICOA). The proposed SWO method outperforms all the others with the lowest THD of 2.008%, indicating its superior performance in reducing harmonic distortion.

articleTitle: Ternary Adder and Multiplier Circuit Designs with GNRFET and RRAM Technologies
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: To address the limitations of binary logic and keep pace with the demand for higher density, processing capabilities, and energy efficiency, researchers have explored various technologies. Ternary logic technique, which utilizes three logic states (0, 1, and 2), has emerged as a promising candidate. In this work, ternary logic half adder and multiplier circuits are implemented using a combination of graphene nanoribbon field-effect transistors (GNRFETs) and resistive random-access memory (RRAM). The GNRFETs offer excellent electrical properties, while RRAM provides a robust option for storing multiple resistance states in a single cell. The proposed half adder and multiplier circuits are designed using basic gates, universal gates and decoder circuits, respectively. The circuits are simulated using the HSPICE simulator with a supply voltage of 0.9 V. The performance of the proposed GNRFET and RRAM based ternary logic circuits is compared with existing carbon nanotube FET (CNTFET) and RRAM based ternary circuits. The proposed circuits exhibit significant improvements in terms of power, delay, and power-delay product (PDP) up to 50.09%, 28.29% and 64.53%, respectively than the CNTFET and RRAM based circuits.

articleTitle: Design and Fabrication of an Adaptive Smart Socket for Intelligent Energy Management in Industrial and Domestic Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Traditional electrical sockets come with significant drawbacks when it comes to energy efficiency and power management. They often lead to unnecessary energy drain, wastage, and power losses, especially in domestic and industrial settings. One of the major shortcomings of conventional sockets is the lack of smart control features, causing appliances to consume power continuously—even when in standby mode. Additionally, the absence of remote accessibility and inefficient power distribution among multiple connected devices results in increased wattage wastage, higher operational costs, and reduced appliance lifespan. To overcome these challenges, this paper introduces the design and fabrication of an Adaptive Smart Socket, a cost-effective and user-friendly solution for better energy management. This smart socket is built around the ESP-8266 microcontroller, enabling wireless control, real-time energy monitoring, and scheduling. It incorporates Web View Configuration for easy accessibility and OTA (Over-the-Air) updates, ensuring seamless firmware upgrades without manual intervention. The system was designed using EasyEDA simulations, fabricated in the lab, and rigorously tested in real-world scenarios to validate its performance and efficiency. The results show that the proposed smart socket significantly reduces energy wastage, optimizes power distribution, and provides users with enhanced control and ease of access. Its low-cost and scalable design makes it a promising step toward smart energy management in modern electrical systems, paving the way for a more efficient and sustainable power ecosystem.

articleTitle: Optimizing Inverted Pendulum Stability: Performance Analysis of Self-Tuning Fuzzy PID and PID
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The inverted pendulum system is a typical control problem for comparing advanced control approaches because of its unstable and nonlinear characteristics. Balancing the kind of system described is fundamental to many branches of engineering such as robotics, aeronautical systems, and automobile dynamics. In this work, the comparative ability of Self-Tuning Fuzzy PID and the traditional PID to stabilize an inverted pendulum system is investigated. The main issue resolved is the performance constraint of fixed-gain PID controllers in dynamic operating conditions. For this purpose, the Self-Tuning Fuzzy PID controller uses a fuzzy inference system to adaptively vary PID gains in real time, which supports better adaptability and disturbance rejection. In contrast, the traditional PID controller with fixed gain parameters renders suboptimal output when the operating conditions change. Simulations carried out in the Simulink platform compare the two control schemes in terms of stability parameters such as overshoot, settling time, rise time, and steady-state error. Outcomes show that the traditional PID controller has a rise time of 1.2s, an overshoot of 20%, and a settling time of 5s, resulting in slower stabilization and more oscillations. The Self-Tuning Fuzzy PID controller greatly enhances transient response, minimizing rise time to 0.8s, overshoot to 5%, and settling time to 2.5s, thereby stabilizing faster and with better robustness.

articleTitle: IoT Enabled Electricity Manager
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The conventional control meter tracks power utilization for homes and businesses over a set period, basically for charging purposes. Be that as it may, this approach is inclined to human blunder, delays in month-to-month utilization readings, and mistakes in charging. To address these issues, a present-day control administration framework has been created with improved observing capabilities. This framework tracks voltage and current expended by each apparatus, giving nitty gritty day by day reports through a portable app. The information is too sent to a cloud database. At the conclusion of each month, the framework naturally sends a rundown alarm to clients, specifying control utilization by each gadget, add up to units utilized, and evaluated costs. This report is moreover shared with the electricity board (EB) for straightforwardness and responsibility. Each client has an interesting login ID to get to their information, encouraging coordinate communication with the EB office with respect to charging. If clients fall flat to pay their bills inside the assigned period, their accounts are hailed by the EB office, driving to a transitory control detachment. Upon installment, the benefit is promptly restored.

articleTitle: Arduino based Multi-Purpose Agricultural Robot Powered by Internet of Things (IoT) Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Agriculture is essential for human life, and farmers dedicate significant effort to plowing fields and applying fertilizers. The proposed method benefits farmers by integrating robotics with agriculture, enabling autonomous movement across fields to cultivate, plant seeds in predetermined rows, and irrigate efficiently. The robot operates using clean, renewable energy from solar panels, reducing reliance on conventional power sources and minimizing environmental impact. High-performance DC motors ensure precise and efficient movement, allowing smooth navigation across various terrains. Servo motors facilitate accurate seed planting, while a specialized DC motor pump ensures proper pesticide application to protect crops. For effective grass cutting, a high-torque DC motor enhances the robot’s versatility in multiple agricultural tasks. An Arduino microcontroller serves as the robot’s central processing unit, coordinating interactions among components to ensure real-time task execution. Additionally, an intuitive Android application enhances user-friendliness, allowing operators to remotely control and monitor the robot. The application connects to the robot via the Internet of Things (IoT) technology, ensuring reliable communication between the mobile application and the agricultural robot. The proposed robotic model, named IoTAgriRobot, operates on a solar-powered system and is compared with a traditional Bluetooth-Controlled AgriRobot (BCAR) to evaluate its efficiency. IoT functionality is enabled using the ESP8266 Wi-Fi module. This Solar-Driven Independent Multi-Purpose Agriculture Robot integrates clean energy, advanced motor technology, and an intelligent microcontroller to enhance farming efficiency while reducing environmental impact.

articleTitle: An Efficient Radix-8 Factored Systolic Array for Machine Learning Acceleration
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research shows that there is a lot of room for improvement at the logic level, even if SAs have a common structure, and it suggests two new SA that use factoring and radix-8 multipliers. Eliminating shared hard-multiple generation and booth encoding across all Processing Elements (PEs) may assist to reduce the overall size and time of the SA. The proposed method employs a parallel prefix adder to finish the addition of a radix-8 multiplier at each processing element. We refer to this design as Factored Systolic Arrays (FSA). Furthermore, we use Kogge-stone (KS), a parallel prefix two-operand adder that significantly decreases critical route time while requiring extra hardware.It has low gate complexity and high performance. In comparison to the usual radix-4 SA, the suggested FSA design reduces space, power consumption, and latency over a wide range of bit widths. Modelsim is used to conduct simulations of the suggested design, which was produced in Verilog HDL. Xilinx ISE is used to provide a comparative study of current and future techniques.

articleTitle: IoT for Sustainable Development: Enhancing Environmental Efficiency and Resource Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT) has recently become an innovative technology in the computing system that is expected to play a great role in achieving sustainable computing by conserving resources while minimizing the impact of the environment and increasing energy efficiency in different sectors. This survey focuses on IoT and sustainability, and presents important technologies, applications, and issues that define this rapidly developing domain. This paper explores Smart Cities, Smart Agriculture, Green Data Centers, and Environmental Monitoring that is supported by IoT devices and their ability to enhance the utilization of energy through the use of low energy sensing and communication. The survey also discusses the limitations of energy usage, expansiveness, security, and compatibility that make IoT green solutions difficult to adopt. In addition, it examines the future directions such as the integration of AI and IoT, development of edge computing, the use of blockchain for green IoT, and the application of quantum computing in addressing the energy problems. In conclusion, the paper presents the call for more interdisciplinary research and cooperation between the academia, the industry and governments towards the creation of a more sustainable IoT environment.

articleTitle: A Hybrid CNN-XGAOA Approach for Photovoltaic Power Output Prediction using Environmental Features
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Concerns over the reliability of power networks have been heightened by the extensive usage of PV systems, which provide power intermittently. Nevertheless, utilities may integrate large amounts of PV electricity into the distribution network with the help of auxiliary services and contemporary management practices, all without compromising electrical quality. Plant and grid operators require accurate predictions of power output in order to incorporate PV technology into existing power systems efficiently. This research automates image processing in order to forecast PV power output using a CNN. Dataset cleaning and Pearson coefficient correlation testing were part of the preprocessing to eliminate noise. A hybrid version of the AOA was used to improve XGBoost, an extreme gradient boosting classifier, instead of CNN's fully linked layers. For better classification results. In terms of PV power forecasts, the CNN-XGAOA model performed admirably, with a classification accuracy of 98.34%. Reliable predictions of solar power generation are crucial to the reliability of electricity networks. In order to include PV systems into contemporary power networks, the CNN-XGAOA model accurately predicts PV power output.

articleTitle: GUARDTRACK: RFID and Wi-Fi based Smart Entry System
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: It is challenging to maintain effective and secure access control in modern workplaces due to unauthorized access, RFID tag cloning, and the vulnerabilities of single-layer authentication systems. Conventional methods, e.g., paper logs and independent RFID authentication, are vulnerable to security intrusions, identity spoofing, and employee tracking inefficiencies. To overcome these issues, this paper introduces GUARDTRACK, an IoT-based smart entry system that integrates Wi-Fi-based tracking and RFID-OTP authentication for enhanced security. The system consists of two prime parts. First, an ESP32 Wi-Fi module tracks the attendance of workers by recognizing static IP assignments when registered devices enter the network. Second, a Security Room authentication system requires workers to scan an RFID card, triggering an OTP (One-Time Password) delivered via a GSM module to be received at their registered telephone number. Entry is granted only after successful verification of OTP for providing multi-layered protection. Experimental testing confirms that GUARDTRACK securely blocks unauthorized access while permitting easy entry for authorized personnel. The system offers high tracking accuracy, real-time authentication, and high RFID cloning resistance, providing a cost-effective and scalable access control solution.

articleTitle: Simulation of WO3 Thin Film Transistor for Biosensors
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper introduces a WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> thin-film transistor (TFT)-based biosensor that detects glucose, proteins, and other biomarkers in blood. It addresses the growing demand for real-time, very sensitive medical diagnostics. Tungsten trioxide (WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>) TFTs are very sensitive, stable, and biocompatible, making them a suitable biosensing platform. Existing WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> TFT biosensors have restricted response time, low sensitivity, and inadequate performance evaluation for biomarker detection. A Silvaco ATLAS-based simulation is used to examine the electrical properties, carrier mobility, and threshold voltage shifts of the proposed biosensor. The device has a threshold voltage shift of 0.42 V, an ON/OFF current ratio of 10<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">6</sup>, and a subthreshold swing of 110 mV/dec, indicating high sensing capabilities. WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf> TFTs outperform traditional biosensors in terms of response time, selectivity, and label-free detection. The study suggests that WO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>- based biosensors could be useful in point-of-care diagnostics and wearable health monitoring, with potential for device improvement and clinical integration.

articleTitle: Building a Decentralized Renewable Energy Marketplace using Blockchain Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Nowadays, the transition towards decentralized energy systems calls for creative ways to facilitate prosumer-consumer energy trading efficiently. Existing energy markets face challenges such as high transaction costs, lack of transparency, and reliance on centralized infrastructure, leading to inefficiencies in energy trading and imbalance in supply and demand. This study presents the implementation of a blockchain-based platform that enables peer-to-peer (P2P) energy trading. The platform guarantees that energy transactions are secure, transparent, and automated by utilizing Ethereum smart contracts. The suggested design uses a decentralized application for prosumer-consumer interaction and uses Internet of Things devices for energy monitoring in real time. The system has potential to completely transform conventional energy markets. The results show how well it facilitates transparent and secure energy transactions.

articleTitle: Realtime Tracking Device for Women Safety
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The safety of women is still a major worldwide concern, underscoring the necessity of creative technology-based solutions to offer protection and comfort. In order to facilitate dependable, long-distance communication in emergency scenarios, this article presents a wearable women's safety gadget that makes use of LoRa (Long Range) technology. The gadget has a panic button that, when hit, instantly sends a distress signal to local authorities and authorised contacts over a LoRaWAN network. The device's low power consumption design guarantees a long battery life, which is necessary for continuous use in a variety of settings. The device's embedded motion sensors may identify distress situations by detecting unexpected movements or falls, and its GPS capabilities allows for real-time position monitoring. You may strike a balance by mixing LoRa and cellular, with cellular handling real-time voice where feasible and LoRa being utilised for emergency warnings and non-urgent data transfer. A cloud-based system processes the data, enabling real-time notifications through SMS and mobile apps to deliver prompt reactions. In addition to delivering real-time communication choices in urban settings, this strategy offers a reliable, hybrid solution that is perfect for rural locations.

articleTitle: Fabrication and Performance Analysis of Perovskite Solar Cells for High Energy Conversion
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Perovskite solar cells (PSCs) have drawn interest as an affordable substitute for traditional photovoltaics; nevertheless, large-scale implementation is hampered by problems like stability, charge recombination, and inconsistent manufacture. With its advantageous optoelectronic characteristics, BaZrS₃ is a promising chalcogenide perovskite for next-generation solar applications. In order to evaluate its potential, a BaZrS₃-based solar cell is simulated using Silvaco software, which optimizes charge transport and photon absorption within an ITO/NiO/BaZrS₃/ZnO/Al structure. The design and manufacture of PSCs are examined in this work, with an emphasis on improving charge extraction through precisely tailored electron and hole transport layers and reducing charge recombination to increase stability and efficiency. Current-voltage tests and other electrical characterisation assess the device's overall performance, stability, and power conversion efficiency. The suggested manufacturing process contributes to more dependable solar cells by ensuring film homogeneity, increasing efficiency, and improving charge transport. Furthermore, study confirms the viability of chalcogenide perovskite for upcoming photovoltaic applications and offers insightful information for improving large-scale PSC manufacture.

articleTitle: Implementation of Smart Parking Access Control and Visitor Authentication using Raspberry Pi 4 And Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Inefficient parking management, unauthorized vehicle access, and reliance on manual supervision remain significant challenges in urban environments. Traditional parking systems struggle with slow response times, security vulnerabilities, and inefficient space utilization. This study presents a smart parking access control and visitor authentication system using Raspberry Pi 4 and machine learning to address these issues. the system integrates a USB camera for license plate recognition, an IR sensor for vehicle detection, and a servo motor for automated gate control, managed by Raspberry Pi 4. A web-based platform facilitates real-time monitoring, ensuring enhanced security and operational efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate a 95% accuracy in vehicle detection, a 98% success rate in blocking unauthorized vehicles, and an average response time of 2.4 seconds, with temporary permit recognition processed in 3 seconds. these improvements significantly enhance security, automation, and user experience in parking management. Future research will focus on integrating additional sensors, optimizing recognition models for extreme weather conditions, and exploring AI-driven anomaly detection for enhanced security.

articleTitle: Smart Energy Management Leveraging Twin Adaptive Pulse Coupled Networks for Dynamic Energy Optimization in IoT-based Electrical WSN
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Internet of Things (IoT)-driven Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) undergo fast growth hence requiring sophisticated energy optimization methods to keep the networks operational longer with reliable data handling. Traditional energy management practices lead to early node failure combined with inefficient network routes and non-even energy distribution which blocks network development and operational performance expansion. The three main factors that cause WSNs to be energy inefficient are improper node positioning along with excessive routing overhead and uneven distribution of power consumption across sensor nodes. The current network management approaches do not provide adequate dynamic energy distribution which results in premature network failure. This research establishes "Smart Energy Management leveraging Twin Adaptive Pulse Coupled Networks for Dynamic Energy Optimization in IoT-Based WSN (MG-TwinAPC-ReP)" to address these challenges. The proposed framework MG-TwinAPC-ReP features four layers which (1) strategic node deployment coverage, (2) Cluster-Based Routing Protocol Using Modified Greylag-Goose Optimization, and (3) Energy management through adaptive load balancing using Twin Adaptive Pulse Coupled Network's dual synchronization model and (4) uses Reformed Poplar Optimization to optimize networking parameters. Experimental results indicate remarkable performance capabilities which lead to a 99.82% increase in network lifetime and 99.74% energy conservation together with 99.91% reliable data delivery and 99.65% reduced latency compared to traditional IoT-WSN systems. The proposed scalable self-adapting energy-efficient WSN model provides an optimal solution for smart cities together with healthcare and agriculture and industrial IoT applications which drives sustainable IoT-driven WSN deployment into the future.

articleTitle: A Survey on Intelligent Attack Mitigation and Latency Optimization in High-Speed Edge Networks using Deep Learning and Bio-Inspired Algorithms
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: As the Internet connected devices and cyber– physical systems (CPS) are exponentially increasing, edge computing has become a crucial enabler to support real time processing in high-speed networks (HSNs). However, integrating edge computing into broadband infrastructure is a challenging problem and that includes mitigating security risks such as DDoS and time-delay attacks and keeping ultra-low latency. Explored for this survey are some recent technologies on how to detect attacks and optimize latency on the edge, focusing on forms of deep learning and bioinspired approaches. It analyzes the lack of effectiveness in traditional mitigation strategies and represents new means, based on the use of ensemble learning, dimensionality reduction and hybrid models. Distributed edge infrastructures are specially emphasized on real time implementation, computational overhead and security. This paper attempts to contribute valuable insight for researchers developing robust, scalable, and intelligent edge-based solutions in high-speed networking environments by consolidating recent methodologies and their outcomes.

articleTitle: Fire Hawk Optimizer-based PI-Synergetic Hybrid Control for Suppressing Circulating Currents in Parallel Inverter-based Electrical Drive Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Electrical drive systems utilizing parallel inverters are widely employed in various industrial applications due to their efficiency and flexibilityStill, one major disadvantage of these systems is the existence of zero-sequence circulating currents (ZSCC) that can distort circulate current and deteriorate the performance with higher losses. In this research work a new strategy that encompasses a synergistic hybrid control associated with a PI deliver optimized through FHO to manage ZSCC in electrical drive systems with parallel inverters is presented. The primary objective of this study is to develop an effective control strategy that mitigates circulating currents (CC) while maintaining system stability across different operating conditions and minimizing Total Harmonic Distortion (THD). The proposed FHO method fine-tunes the parameters of the PI controller, resulting in improved control performance and adaptability. At that point, the suggested approach is put into practice on the MATLAB platform and contrasted with a number of current approaches, including Particle Swarm Optimization (PSO), Bacterial Foraging Optimization Technique (BFOT), and Genetic Algorithm (GA). The proposed method achieves a THD of approximately 3.16%, significantly lower than existing methods, thereby validating the effectiveness of the proposed synergetic hybrid control in enhancing the operational efficiency of electrical drive systems.

articleTitle: Smart Factory Integration with IIoT and Machine Learning for Optimized Manufacturing
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Smart manufacturing has transformed through the IIoT and ML integration, which allows real-time monitoring, predictive analytics, and autonomous decisions. Traditional manufacturing systems go through significant difficulties because their predictive maintenance worked poorly, it could not detect defects effectively, and experienced high equipment downtime. A dual applied IIoT-ML structure that combines LSTM technology for predictive maintenance with CNN solutions for defect identification and reinforcement learning approaches for production improvement. The LSTM model reached 96.7% accuracy together with 2.1% false alarm reduction and the CNN model achieved 96.2% accuracy and better defect detection. The implementation of reinforcement learning optimization methods helped reduce downtime by 42.7% while decreasing energy use by 19.8%, which led to an OEE enhancement to 91.5%. The validation of the system occurred through AnyLogic digital simulation. The outcomes indicate that artificial intelligence-based manufacturing facilities increase operational efficiency while lowering expenses and elevating product quality, which leads to totally autonomous production systems.

articleTitle: Sustainable Cluster Head Selection in Wireless Sensor Networks Through Bio-Inspired Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The selection of cluster heads is a critical challenge in Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) because it has a direct impact on the overall performance, network lifetime, and energy efficiency. The Crayfish Optimization Algorithm (COA) is a bio-inspired metaheuristic approach that is introduced in this study. It is intended to improve cluster head selection by emulating the foraging and decision-making behavior of crayfish.
