COA optimizes the selection of cluster heads by considering residual energy, connectivity, and network coverage. This is achieved by utilizing a pheromone-like memory mechanism to balance exploration and exploitation, thereby facilitating adaptive learning and enhanced convergence. The simulation results indicate that COA substantially improves data transmission efficiency, extends the lifespan of networks, and reduces energy consumption in comparison to current methods. It is well-suited for large-scale, dynamic WSN environments due to its robustness and scalability.

articleTitle: Hybrid BERT-XGBoost Model for High-Impact Research Prediction in Construction Management
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Some of the sub-disciplines that make up CEM include scheduling, quality control, human aspects, sustainability, and cost estimation. Many researchers have turned to scientometric analysis to gauge the relative merits of various research philosophies. To find seminal studies and direct future research, high-impact research prediction is essential in the field of construction management. Feature selection was carried out using the ReliefF Method, and the study makes use of other data preparation approaches, including missing value imputation, data reduction, and data transformation. The incorporation of a BERT-based CM extraction method is a significant breakthrough in this methodology. It outperforms existing techniques when it comes to finding obfuscation, encryption, and evasion strategies. To further improve the accuracy of predictions, the BE-XGBoost classifier is also presented. With a recall of 93.30%, an F1-score of 97.43%, an accuracy of 97.38%, and a precision of 95.52%, the experimental findings show that the suggested model performs better than prior models. The results show that the model is good at predicting research with a big impact in the field of construction management. This study lays the groundwork for future advancements in research prediction procedures by integrating state-of-the-art extraction and classification techniques, which is a substantial contribution.

articleTitle: Enhancing Resource Scheduling Efficiency in Cloud Data Centers Through Hybrid Optimization Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research addresses the critical issue of ineffective resource scheduling in cloud data centers, which frequently leads to higher consumption of energy, more expensive operations, and worse system performance. Given the pivotal role of cloud data centers in facilitating scalable and efficient computing resources, optimal resource scheduling is critical for performance maximization and operational cost reduction. Integrating advanced met heuristic techniques like Genetic Algorithms (GA) and particle Swarm Optimization (PSO) with machine learning models, a hybrid optimization framework is proposed to allocate resources adaptively. The hybrid model effectively manages exploration and exploitation by leveraging the global searching capabilities of GAs and the fast convergence behavior of PSO, hence overcoming multi-faceted complexities and heterogeneity prevalent in cloud infrastructures. Of note, the inclusion of machine learning elements further augments the predictive ability of the model, facilitating dynamic updates in response to changes in load and diverse user requirements. Those experimental results show that significant improvements in scheduling efficiency are achieved to minimize both the job completion times and the energy consumption without violating the SLAs.

articleTitle: Bio-Sensor Integrated PCB for Wearables
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This project presents an efficient Bio-Sensor Integrated PCB Method for enhancing signal integrity analysis in high- speed PCB designs. Bio-sensors are critical for evaluating voltage and timing margins, providing insights into signal quality. The proposed method utilizes advanced computational algorithms to model and predict signal behavior under noise, jitter, and crosstalk conditions, enabling accurate simulation of high- frequency signal transmission. By incorporating adaptive filtering, it isolates key performance metrics such as eye height, eye width, and bit error rates, ensuring detailed analysis with minimal computational effort. Experimental results validate the method’s effectiveness in improving design validation efficiency, reducing design cycle times, and enhancing the reliability of high- speed communication interfaces. This scalable approach addresses the growing demands of next-generation electronic systems, offering a practical and cost-effective solution for PCB designers.

Author Keywords: PCB Design High-Speed Signals Jitter Analysis

articleTitle: ML Enhanced Autonomous Night Patrol Robot for Intelligent Security
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The ML-Enhanced Autonomous Night Patrol Robot discussed here is designed to enhance security in any environment when carrying out operations during the night. Using advanced sensor technologies such as LiDAR, ultrasonic sensors, and night vision cameras combined with machine learning algorithms, the robot can navigate complex terrain independently and correctly detect and classify any danger in real-time. Through the utilization of deep learning models, the surveillance of the robot is enhanced as it can recognize objects and adapt to dynamic security conditions. Edge computing also facilitates easy management of data in real-time and interaction with security personnel, which ensures timely incident responses. Overall, the proposed robot provides an extensible solution for smart security applications, significantly enhances security efficiency, and reduces reliance on human patrols.

articleTitle: Fault-Tolerant and Efficient EV Charging with PI and MPC-Controlled LCC Converter
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This work addresses issues regarding the faults detected in a shared charging channel of electric vehicles by focusing primarily on the phase-shift modulated high-frequency full-bridge LCC Resonant DC-DC converter. Its inefficiency in and unreliability towards handling the faults pose it to more reliable fault-detecting techniques. A proposed PI and MPC based closed loop system is established in order to make the overall performance of this system better with faults as well. The study considers simulation of circuit diagrams that already exist and their modified versions. It also considers diagrams with fault conditions and evaluates dynamic behavior of the converter. Key performance metrics, namely overshoot, rise time, settling time, and steady-state error, have been compared using both control strategies. The design of the converter is done on the basis of the small-signal model and MATLAB simulations validated the effectiveness of the proposed system along with some experimental results. The aim is to improve the fault-tolerant and efficient performance of EV charging systems by including a strategy of control that is reliable and adaptive.

articleTitle: A Smart IoT-Enabled Wildfire Monitoring and Early Detection System using Convolutional Neural Networks and Sensor Data Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Wildfires pose a significant threat to ecosystems, biodiversity, and human settlements, with climate change and deforestation exacerbating the frequency and intensity. Conventional forest fire detection methods, including satellite-based monitoring and ground surveillance, suffer from limitations such as delayed detection, high false alarm rates, and dependency on manual intervention. Existing sensor-based detection systems often lack integration with intelligent decision-making frameworks, leading to inefficient fire prevention strategies. The absence of real-time processing and predictive capabilities further reduces the effectiveness of current methodologies in mitigating wildfire risks. This work presents an IoT-based deep learning approach utilizing Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for real-time forest fire detection and prevention. Data is collected from satellite images, drone feeds, and IoT sensors, including temperature, humidity, gas concentration, and infrared readings. Advanced data preprocessing techniques, including image augmentation, normalization, and feature extraction, enhance the robustness of the model. A CNN-based classification model is implemented to analyze fire patterns and assess risk levels. The system is trained using sensor data and image datasets, ensuring high detection accuracy with minimal false positives. The key features of this methodology include real-time wildfire detection, automated risk assessment, and deployment on IoT edge devices for immediate decision-making. The integration of sensor-driven insights with deep learning improves early detection capabilities while reducing reliance on manual surveillance. Efficient data handling and cloud-based alert mechanisms enable proactive measures against fire outbreaks. The proposed system enhances wildfire monitoring by ensuring fast response times, improved accuracy, and scalable deployment in fire-prone regions.

articleTitle: Design and Simulation of a Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) based Biosensor for Glucose Detection using COMSOL Multiphysics
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The design and simulation of a Surface-Enhanced Raman Scattering (SERS) biosensor for non-invasive glucose detection are presented, aiming to provide an alternative to conventional invasive monitoring techniques. The proposed sensor utilizes gold nanoparticles on a silicon substrate to enhance Raman signal intensity through localized surface plasmon resonance (LSPR), enabling precise and highly sensitive glucose detection without blood sampling.COMSOL Multiphysics simulates the electric field distribution and evaluates the enhancement factor across various nanoparticle configurations. Key design parameters, including nanoparticle size, spacing, and excitation wavelength, are optimized to maximize sensitivity. Simulation results demonstrate a significant enhancement in Raman signal intensity, confirming the feasibility of the proposed SERS biosensor for real-time, non-invasive glucose monitoring in biomedical applications.

articleTitle: Flood Forecasting System based on Water Monitoring using IoT-Machine Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Floods are among the most devastating natural disasters, resulting in massive loss of life, widespread property damage, and overall economic disruption Conventional flood monitoring systems, which depend on manual data gathering and old models, tend to lag behind interventions This project suggests an IoT-based flood forecasting system for real-time monitoring, precise predictions, and timely warnings. IoT sensors monitor water level, rainfall, and moisture in flooded regions and send information to a cloud platform for processing. Machine learning models analyze the data, combining hydrological, meteorological, and geographic variables to improve prediction. The system employs low-power IoT sensors with communication protocols such as LoRa WAN, Zigbee, or cellular networks for real-time monitoring. Modular and scalable, it adjusts to varied environments. Visualization interfaces and mobile/web interfaces offer decision-makers and community’s clear data and timely notifications, enabling proactive disaster management, evacuation planning, and resource allocation. Simulated and tested through real-life applications, the system proves to have efficient early flood detection, minimizing damage and enhancing resilience in limited-resource areas.

articleTitle: Development of a USB-based UHF RFID Reader
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The increasing demand for efficient and cost-effective RFID solutions in automation and IoT applications has driven the development of a USB-based UHF RFID Reader. This research presents a compact, power-efficient RFID reader that enables seamless tag detection and real-time data transmission in HEX or ASCII format. The system integrates Human Interface Device (HID) and USB serial communication modes, ensuring platform independence and ease of use. The hardware implementation involves schematic design, PCB layout, and firmware development using OrCAD, KiCAD, and MPLAB IPE. Extensive testing, including power-on verification, functional evaluation, and card write operations, was conducted to ensure reliability and performance. The results confirm the RFID reader's capability for stable and high-speed data transfer with minimal power consumption, making it ideal for inventory management, secure access control, industrial automation, and IoT applications. Future enhancements could include encryption for secure communication, multi-frequency support, and cloud integration for remote monitoring. This study demonstrates a scalable and cost-effective approach to RFID-based automation, contributing to the advancement of smart tracking systems.

articleTitle: Sustainable Energy Consumption Forecasting in Smart Grids using Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average Model
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: With the increase in global energy needs, anticipating sustainable energy use has become essential, especially in smart grids. This research uses the Autoregressive Integrated Moving Average (ARIMA) model to forecast sustainable energy usage in smart networks, addressing demand variability. Data gathering historical energy usage data from smart grids, including parameters such as meteorological circumstances, temporal variables, and user behavior. Utilizing the ARIMA model, examine time series data to discern patterns and seasonal fluctuations in energy use. The model's parameters are refined to improve predictive accuracy, offering significant insights for utility firms. The findings demonstrate that ARIMA proficiently identifies the fundamental trends in energy use, resulting in enhanced resource distribution and minimized energy waste. Results indicate higher predictive precision, facilitating effective energy management and increased system dependability. This forecasting method facilitates the incorporation of renewable energy sources into the system, enhancing sustainability. It illustrates the efficacy of ARIMA in improving decision-making for energy suppliers and facilitating a shift towards more sustainable energy systems in smart grids.

articleTitle: Development of a Compact IoT-Enabled Air Purification System for Indoor Air Quality Improvement
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This study details the development of a compact, low-cost, IoT-enabled solar-powered air purification system targeted at the increasingly problematic urban air pollution issue in an environmentally friendly way. Research suggests that the majority of standard air purifiers intended for small and medium-sized rooms use up to 0.003 kWh (3 watts) an hour, while some advanced models differ depending on fan speed settings [1]. Urban air pollution has dire health implications, especially in dense cities where indoor air quality is vital. The system integrates three kinds of filters: HEPA, nylon, and polypropylene (surgical mask), which were evaluated for their efficiency in capturing particulate matter, especially PM2.5 and PM10. Based on the results, polypropylene fabric, commonly used with surgical masks, is revealed to be the most economically sensible as well as efficient filter material that has achieved an impressive degree of filtration efficiency at 87.50% using three layers whereas maximum recorded HEPA filters reached efficiencies of 78.29% over the same layer number. HEPA offers high filtration efficiency but happens to be costlier to make it less practical compared to low-budget applications. Nylon filters, as though cheap, showed lower efficiencies: two layers achieved a maximum of 56.25%. It operates with solar energy, which greatly reduces its dependency on the power grid and thus makes it an energy-sustainable device. The addition of IoT features enables real-time air quality monitoring and allows the system to dynamically adjust its operation to deliver optimal performance. Its modular design ensures ease of assembly, scalability, and suitability for diverse indoor environments. This innovative system exemplifies a highly successful integration of cost-efficiency, sustainability, and technology-and hence makes it an accessible and practical solution to improve air quality, particularly in resource-limited and energy-constrained settings.

articleTitle: Implementation of a Solar Driven Semi-Autonomous Eco-Friendly Grass Cutter
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research focuses on developing a solar-powered semi-autonomous grass cutter designed to meet the growing demand for eco-friendly and efficient lawn maintenance solutions. The system operates on renewable solar energy, utilizing photovoltaic panels to power the device while storing excess energy in a rechargeable battery for uninterrupted operation, even during low-light conditions. With its ability to detect and avoid obstacles in real time, the grass cutter reduces manual intervention and ensures smooth operation. Additionally, Bluetooth connectivity allows users to remotely control and monitor the device via a mobile app, offering flexibility and ease of use. This grass cutter is an ideal solution for maintaining outdoor spaces such as gardens, parks, sports fields, and industrial lawns. By combining sustainable energy, advanced automation, and user-friendly remote control, it not only minimizes labor costs but also enhances productivity and aligns with modern environmental goals. Practical, efficient, and versatile, this innovation paves the way for smarter, greener approaches to lawn care and outdoor maintenance.

articleTitle: Osprey Optimization Algorithm and Position-Aware Graph Neural Network for Enhanced Vehicle-to-Grid Control System
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Optimized Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) Control System enhances energy management by leveraging Electric Vehicle (EV) as flexible storage units, enabling controlled energy exchange with the grid to improve power distribution and overall system efficiency. The system encounters difficulties in reducing total EV charging and discharging plan costs while maintaining high operational efficiency and power grid integrity throughout varying electrical circumstances. To address these challenges, this paper proposes a hybrid approach for optimized V2G control system. The proposed method integrates the Osprey Optimization Algorithm (OOA) and Position-Aware Graph Neural Network (PAGNN); therefore it is called the OOA-PAGNN technique. The main goal is to reduce total costs, enhance grid stability, and generate revenue for EV owners through an optimized V2G framework. OOA is utilized to optimize the charging and discharging schedules of EVs, ensuring effective energy flow management and enhancing grid stability. While, PAGNN is utilized to predict energy demand and generation by analyzing the spatial distribution of EVs, enabling optimized energy allocation. By then, the proposed method is implemented on the MATLAB platform and evaluated with various existing approaches such as Artificial Neural Network (ANN), Mixed-Integer Quadratic Programming (MIQP), Particle Swarm Optimization-Trained Artificial Neural Network (PSO-TANN), Recurrent Proximal Policy Optimization-Long Short-Term Memory (RPPO-LSTM) and Competitive Swarm Optimization-Imperialist Competitive Algorithm (CSO-ICA). The OOA-PAGNN model successfully optimizes V2G control while lowering expenses by -1.458$ while maintaining 98.6% system efficiency.

articleTitle: A Machine Learning-based Smart Water Management Framework for Agricultural Irrigation using a Stacked Ensemble Model
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Employing SWM in agricultural irrigation enhances efficiency, reduces costs, and boosts crop yield, while simultaneously benefiting the environment. We can now accurately quantify the water requirements of each plant, thanks to technological breakthroughs. The harmonious integration of diverse technologies poses a significant barrier to efficient solid waste management. Agriculture utilises around 70% of global freshwater, making effective water management essential for maintaining a sustainable food and water supply. In their quest for optimal irrigation, they utilised RF, RFE, and SelectKBest for feature selection after processing features with blanks. The ideal irrigation timetable for plants was established using a stacking ensemble technique. The recently constructed EM-MoNet network also facilitated SWM. This model utilised a two-stage transfer learning methodology that included re-training with the target dataset to improve its accuracy. The proposed method shown utility with an accuracy of 98.23% on a local dataset. This study highlights the importance of SWM in precision irrigation, which enhances sustainable agriculture by augmenting crop yields and reducing water consumption.

articleTitle: Automated Drone-based Solar Panel Cleaning for Enhanced Efficiency and Sustainable Solar Power Generation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The amount of solar power that solar power systems produce depends on the degree to which photovoltaic (PV) panels remain clean. The passage of dust and dirt on PV panels together with other pollutants creates substantial energy output reduction due to blocked sunlight absorption. The cleaning techniques which include manual washing or robotic systems face difficulties particularly in large solar farm settings. Techniques used for cleaning photovoltaic panels typically require extensive labor expenditure and result in high cost and potential panel damage when executed without proper treatment. This paper analyzes drone-based solar panel maintenance which achieves automatic cleaning while minimizing environmental impact. Devices that combine sensors and spraying systems together with autonomous flight controls provide an effective solar panel maintenance approach which minimizes human involvement while maximizing cleaning performance. An evaluation of drone-based cleaning systems examines their technological aspects through an investigation of system design and operational methods and performance evaluation. The research evaluates the primary obstacles that prevent drone-based cleaning implementation as part of its findings. Two major technological impediments along with autonomy issues and two operational challenges affect drone-based solar power operations. The research works to create a cost-effective drone-based solution that maintains PV panel efficiency by fixing identified implementation hurdles which will enhance solar power sustainability.

articleTitle: Design and Development of Cost-Effective Terahertz Device for Medical Diagnosis
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Terahertz (THz) technology is in high demand because of its use in wireless communication, spectroscopy, and imaging. The exorbitant price of THz devices, however, continues to be a major obstacle to their widespread use. An STM32 microcontroller, Node-MCU, and a number of auxiliary electronic parts, including a relay board, L298N motor driver, DC motor, Ni-Cr coil, and an AC-to-DC converter, are used in this research to create an affordable terahertz device. Through the use of a Flutter-developed Android application, the system can be remotely handled to efficiently create and control THz radiation. Firebase ensures smooth communication between the mobile interface and the hardware by managing and storing data in real time. Together, the STM32 and Node-MCU regulate the power source, motor, and heating components to maximize efficiency and reduce expenses. The goal of this research is to create a THz device that is both economical and efficient, suitable for a range of uses such as material analysis, medical imaging, and security screening. IoT integration improves accessibility and usability by enabling users to remotely monitor and operate the system. The suggested remedy offers a workable way to lower the cost and increase the accessibility of THz technology for use in industrial and research settings.

articleTitle: Smart Energy Conservation in Homes using Fully Residual Convolutional Networks for Solar Power Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: DG is a power production strategy that enhances efficiency by reducing carbon demand peaks, emissions, and transmission losses through the deployment of multiple smaller on-site energy sources located within individual buildings. Although net metering aids in balancing energy supply and demand, scaling distributed generation across several houses to support intermittent renewable energy sources remains challenging. Furthermore, distributed generation is not economically attractive for widespread implementation given the existing energy price framework. To maximise Smart Energy Conservation and Solar Power Forecasting, meticulous data preparation is crucial for addressing these challenges. This paper reviews the methodologies and procedures employed in data preparation in prior studies. Our approach employs a FCN architecture, utilising ResNet101 as the backbone, with integrated upsampling skip links to enhance prediction accuracy. The proposed method achieves an accuracy of 96.56%, outperforming leading models and techniques in solar power forecasting. These findings underscore the importance of robust machine learning algorithms and meticulous data preparation for smart homes to optimise the use of renewable energy. Efficient distributed generation utilisation in residential applications facilitates smart energy conservation, hence enhancing energy sustainability and improving the accuracy of solar power forecasts.

articleTitle: An IoT-Enabled Battery Capacity Monitoring System for Solar Panels in Electric Vehicles with Self-Attention and Bidirectional LSTM Models
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The expansion of automobiles significantly contributes to deteriorating air quality by augmenting the demand for non-renewable fossil fuels. Solar panels incorporated within EV provide a viable energy solution that may address this issue. Nonetheless, there are challenges to address during this transition, particularly with energy efficiency and battery management. This study concentrates on efficient energy usage, analyzing the components of electric vehicles' battery management systems and their interrelations. A significant issue in charging electric vehicle batteries is the inefficiency that arises when cells with a high SOC charge more rapidly than those with a low SOC. Particle swarm optimization was employed to minimize features, while z-score normalization was utilized to preprocess data for optimal performance. To enhance analytical efficiency, the proposed SA-BiLSTM model integrates a self-attention mechanism with multi-channel features, enabling it to replicate the capabilities of solar panels in electric vehicles without necessitating manual panel arrangement. Achieving a classification accuracy of 97.37%, SA-BiLSTM existing methodologies, as per performance assessment. The results indicate that solar panels in electric vehicles can address battery optimization issues and enhance sustainability. Future research should focus on enhancing these strategies for improved integration with RES in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Signature-based Antivirus Scanner for Effective Malware Detection and Security Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The Antivirus Scanner application is a robust tool designed to enhance computer security by enabling users to selectively scan specific directories and detect potential malware using a comprehensive database of known malicious signatures. Utilizing the MD5 hash algorithm, it efficiently compares each file's hash against stored malware signatures to accurately determine its safety status. During the scanning process, the application provides real-time feedback through a progress bar and categorizes each file as either "Safe" or "Infected", presenting the results in a well-organized format for easy interpretation. Additionally, it quantifies detected threats, offering users a clear assessment of the severity of identified malware, thereby supporting informed decision-making regarding the appropriate actions to secure their systems. This tool plays a critical role in proactively identifying security risks and preserving data integrity against potential cyber threats.

articleTitle: Novel Cathode and Anode Materials for Energy Storage
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Energy storage systems are crucial for developing new technologies, but existing battery materials do not have the energy density, durability, or efficiencies required. This study was focused on developing new materials for the cathodes and the anodes to optimize energy storage capabilities. We assessed the synthesis and characterization of new materials to improve the electrochemical characteristics, mainly energy density, charge-discharge cycles, and stability. We used advanced characterization techniques like X-ray Diffraction (XRD), Scanning Electron Microscopy (SEM), and Electrochemical Impedance Spectroscopy (EIS) to evaluate their structural characteristics, morphology, and conductivity. The results show significant improvement in energy density, cycling stability, and charge-discharge efficiency, suggesting potential high-performance and long-lasting energy storage devices. This research presents a contribution to material science for next-generation batteries, and we identify the potential for new advanced materials for enhancing energy storage performance across multiple applications, advancing the development of sustainable and more efficient energy storage systems.

articleTitle: An Expected Cardiovascular Disease Detection using Deep Learning Techniques
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Many avoidable deaths globally are caused by cardiovascular diseases (CVD), which pose a serious threat to global health. Often, individuals remain ignorant of the risk factors or the presence of CVD until severe symptoms, such as heart attacks or strokes, appear. The need for sophisticated diagnostic instruments that can identify cardiovascular risk factors early on is highlighted by the delay in diagnosis and treatment. Timely action made possible by early detection may lessen the chance of life-threatening events and enhance long-term health outcomes. Retinal imaging is one of the non-invasive diagnostic methods that has attracted increasing attention in recent years. One effective technique that might be essential for determining cardiovascular risk factors is retinal imaging. The central nervous system is directly linked to the retina, a thin layer of tissue found at the back of the eye. Its distinct position and form allow it to offer important insights into the general health, especially the cardiovascular system, of an individual. Because retinal blood vessels may be imaged and studied, anomalies in these veins may indicate the existence of cardiovascular diseases. As a result, retinal imaging has become a viable non-invasive technique for CVD prevention and early detection. Retinal imaging offers a unique, non-invasive way to observe blood vessels and detect cardiovascular risk factors, as abnormalities in the retina often reflect broader systemic issues like high blood pressure, diabetes, and atherosclerosis. These retinal changes, linked to cardiovascular diseases (CVD), can signal increased risks of stroke or heart attack. Advances in image processing and machine learning now enable more precise detection of these abnormalities, with AI algorithms identifying patterns that might indicate CVD. This early detection capability allows for proactive interventions, potentially reducing the global burden of CVD and improving patient outcomes.

articleTitle: IoT and AI for Efficient Forest Fire Detection, Monitoring, and Risk Prediction With Real-Time Alerts
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Wildfires pose severe threats to ecosystems, wildlife, and human settlements, necessitating efficient early detection and monitoring systems. This research introduces a real-time wildfire detection and risk assessment system powered by IoT and AI. The proposed system continuously monitors environmental parameters such as temperature, humidity, and gas concentrations using IoT-based sensors for early fire detection. AI-driven models analyze both historical and real-time sensor data to identify high-risk areas, improving predictive accuracy. A cloud-integrated architecture facilitates data collection, processing, and transmission between sensor nodes, cloud servers, and a mobile alert system. Fire response teams can leverage the system’s real-time fire alerts, GPS-based tracking, and predictive analytics via a smartphone application, enhancing emergency response coordination. Extensive testing demonstrates high accuracy, efficiency, and scalability, significantly reducing detection times while improving resource allocation. Designed for cost efficiency and adaptability, this framework presents a proactive strategy for wildfire prevention, disaster mitigation, and environmental protection.

articleTitle: Solar based Smart Cropping Defence System using IoT based on Birds and Animals
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Preserving their harvest from wild animals and unauthorized intrusions is a significant difficulty for farmers. The Farm Guardian, a solar-powered, IoT-enabled automated crop protection system, helps solve this. This technology uses an ESP8266 NODEMCU microprocessor alongside touch sensors and ultrasonic sensors to detect movement and touch. Should dangers be discovered, the HCSR04 ultrasonic sensor's continuous object distance monitoring sets off a buzzer and warning system. A solar-powered electric fence keeps animals or trespassers off the perimeter, hence enhancing security by means of a slight deterrent shock. Using the Blynk app, the system sends alerts and actual data to an Android phone belonging to a farmer, therefore enabling remote monitoring effective operation with a 12V solar photovoltaic power source changed to 5V DC for the control unit and sensors. Output modules for buzzers, LED indicators, a servo motor, and a user interface LCD screen constitute the system. Automated, affordable, environmentally friendly means of crop protection using renewable energy is provided by Farm Guardian. The suggested strategy maintains ecologically sustainable farming methods, secures the farm efficiently, decreases dependence on traditional fences, and lowers human interference.

articleTitle: Automated Segregation of Degraded Vegetables in Industrial Settings using YOLO and OpenCV
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research paper focuses on the development of an automated system for segregating degraded vegetables in industrial environments using YOLO (You Only Look Once) and OpenCV. The segregation of degraded vegetables is crucial in industrial environments, particularly in scenarios involving storage and preservation. Storing damaged produce not only increases costs but also affects the quality and shelf life of the entire batch. Prompt identification and removal of degraded vegetables are vital to ensuring consistent quality control, minimizing waste, and maintaining product standards. The proposed solution enhances the effectiveness and precision of vegetable sorting, reducing human errors and labour expenses. YOLO, a real-time object detection algorithm, identifies and classifies vegetables based on their visual quality, while OpenCV, a robust computer vision library, aids in image processing and feature extraction. The system processes images of vegetables on a conveyor belt, leveraging the combined techniques of YOLO and OpenCV to distinguish between fresh and degraded items. This project is designed to be scalable and adaptable. The proposed work is suitable for various types of vegetables and industrial environments. This cost-effective solution improves productivity, reduces operational downtime, and streamlines the quality control process, making it ideal for large-scale vegetable sorting in industrial settings.

articleTitle: EcoHarvest: Integrating IoT Technology for Sustainable Soil and Air Management in Agriculture
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Green agriculture now relies on technology and there are numerous hurdles that have to be met, including soil erosion, global warming, and food availability. CA together with improvement of soil carbon and soil quality are of central importance to health of the soils and enhanced agricultural yields. Conservation tilted is the practice of leaving a portion of the soil residue after harvest, crop rotation is the practice of growing different crops in one area sequentially and nutrient managed is the practice of applying nutrients necessary for plant growth in correct quantities at the right time frequencies they’ re all beneficial to the soils as they reduce environmental degradations ,improves productivity of the soils. In this regards, IoT based solutions are seen as a promising solution for monitoring and managing soil and environment status. Through the application of the Capacitive Soil Moisture Sensor V1.2 and DHT11 Temperature and Humidity Sensor real time data can be obtained in regard to soil moisture, temperature and humidity. Information collected from these sensors is fed into cloud computing solutions which enhance optimal watering and gains Yield optimization and more appropriate decisions making. The ability of this system to acquire, log and sort the data acquired via the Arduino microcontroller and specialized libraries is seamlessly enhanced by the integration of the two. The analyzed data indicates reliable associations between the measured characteristics of soil moisture and environmental factors that can be helpful to design effective recommendations for improving the state of the soils and using water resources for sustainable agriculture.

articleTitle: A Novel Deep Learning Approach for Extraction of Water Bodies using Satellite Imagery
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This paper presents SegxResNet, a novel deep learning framework for the precise extraction of water bodies from satellite imagery. The primary challenge in water body segmentation lies in the variability of their size, shape, and spectral properties, which often leads to information loss in conventional models due to max-pooling operations. To overcome this, SegxResNet integrates SegxNet and ResNet-50 architectures, leveraging their strengths to improve segmentation accuracy. The methodology involves an encoder-decoder structure, where SegxNet processes the input, ResNet-50 extracts deep features, and the SegxNet decoder generates the final segmented output. The accuracy of the segmentation is evaluated against ground truth images, with an inverse segmentation refinement step further enhancing precision. Experimental results demonstrate that SegxResNet significantly improves segmentation accuracy, outperforming traditional models and highlighting its potential for enhanced remote sensing applications in water body extraction.

articleTitle: Advanced Multilevel Power Conversion for Solar and Wind Integrated Energy Systems
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Efficiency, dependability, and scalability are major issues when integrating renewable energy sources like solar and wind into hybrid power systems. Multiport DC-DC-AC converters are one viable solution. By facilitating the smooth integration of wind and solar energy into a single system, these converters maximize power flow between energy storage devices, the grid, and renewable energy sources. Soft-switching reduces the losses connected with conventional hard-switching techniques, thereby increasing the power converter’s lifetime and efficiency. Standard converters lose efficiency and operational life due to energy dissipation and component wear caused by the simultaneous overlap of voltage and current during switching events. On the other hand, MOSFETs can be switched in a manner that minimizes these overlaps thanks to soft-switching. resulting in longer device lifespans, reduced electromagnetic interference (EMI), and less heat emission. This converter design’s modularity makes it easy to scale and adapt, which makes it especially suitable for renewable energy sources. An applications where it would be necessary to gradually increase system capacity. Because each converter module functions separately, maintenance is made easier and system expansion is made possible with minimal downtime. By reducing oscillations that could jeopardize grid stability and power quality, this flexibility helps to improve voltage regulation. By producing high-quality AC outputs with low harmonic distortion, the converter not only increases efficiency but also improves power quality, which is essential for maintaining steady grid operation and safeguarding connected devices. By offering increased dependability, scalability, power quality, and efficiency, this technology encourages the wider use of resulting in longer device lifespans, reduced electromagnetic interference (EMI), and less heat emission. This converter design’s modularity makes it easy to scale and adapt, which makes it especially suitable for renewable energy.

articleTitle: AI-based Smart Control Systems for Induction Brazing in Industrial Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Induction brazing is extensively used in the automotive, aerospace, and electronics industries, where precision and repeatability are crucial. Conventional brazing systems rely on fixed parameter values and manual monitoring, leading to inconsistencies in joint quality, inefficient energy consumption, and higher defect rates. This study addresses these issues by developing an AI-driven smart control system that integrates machine learning and deep learning to optimize the brazing process, detect defects, and enable predictive maintenance. The system employs convolutional neural networks (CNNs) for computer vision-based defect classification and anomaly detection algorithms to identify deviations in real time. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system enhances defect detection accuracy to 97.2%, improves process efficiency by 23.5%, and reduces energy consumption by 18.7%. These findings highlight AI’s potential to improve brazing reliability and efficiency. However, computational overhead remains a limitation. Future research will focus on enhancing scalability and real-time adaptability to facilitate broader industrial adoption and seamless integration into manufacturing environments.

articleTitle: Advancing Stress Diagnostics using EEG and Deep Learning Methods for Early Stress Identification: A Systematic Literature Survey
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Stress is a growing global concern with significant psychological and physiological consequences, necessitating improved diagnostic methods for early detection and intervention. Electroencephalography (EEG) has emerged as a promising noninvasive tool for stress assessment, offering real-time insights into neurological responses. However, traditional methods struggle with the complexity and variability of EEG signals. This review systematically analyzes recent advancements in machine learning (ML) and deep learning (DL) applied to EEG-based stress detection. We assess various models, including Convolutional 1D (CONV1D), Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM), and Bidirectional Gated Recurrent Units (BiGRU), and their effectiveness in identifying stress patterns from EEG data. The study also explores the broader implications of EEG in diagnosing Alzheimer's disease and enabling brain-computer interfaces (BCIs), which enhance human-computer interactions, particularly for individuals with mobility impairments. Our findings suggest that integrating ML/DL with EEG can significantly enhance stress detection accuracy, paving the way for automated and scalable mental health diagnostics. By bridging the gap between neuroscience and artificial intelligence, this research contributes to the development of more precise, accessible, and preventive stress-monitoring solutions.

articleTitle: Efficient Smart Vehicle for Crippled Person by using Standalone Photovoltaic System
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The development of a solar-powered wheelchair integrated with health monitoring and communication features aims to enhance the mobility and safety of users. This innovative system utilizes a Maximum Power Point Tracking (MPPT) controller to efficiently harness solar energy, ensuring sustainable and eco-friendly wheelchair operation.MPPT system optimizes the charging of the battery, enabling uninterrupted use. Additionally, the wheelchair is equipped with a Blood Pressure (BP) sensor to continuously monitor the user's health status, providing real-time insights into vital parameters. These health metrics are transmitted to a remote platform using GSM and IoT technologies, The system is designed to ensure user safety, as it automatically triggers emergency alerts to pre-configured contacts in the event of abnormal blood pressure readings or critical health situations.This feature ensures prompt assistance and intervention, providing peace of mind to both the user and their caregivers. The integration of solar power, health monitoring, and communication technologies makes this wheelchair a sustainable, reliable, and proactive solution to support the mobility and well-being of individuals, particularly those with chronic health conditions or limited access to immediate medical care.

articleTitle: Optimal Scheduling of Microgrid with Electric Vehicle Integration in Smart Grid using Progressive Graph Convolutional Network
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Electric vehicles (EVs) integrated into microgrids (MGs) provide multiple benefits but create complex optimal scheduling problems which emerge from energetic unpredictability and fluctuating renewable energy sources (RESs) as well as dissimilar EV charging behaviors. Standard scheduling approaches show poor results when trying to handle complex energy systems because they do not apply effective adaptations to changes. The paper introduces a Progressive Graph Convolutional Network (PGCN) to perform optimal scheduling for MGs with embedded EVs. The proposed method uses Levelized Cost of Energy minimization (LCOE) as its main objective and increases grid reliability performance. The PGCN model delivers predictions of energy needs together with renewable power output and EV charging activity patterns and electric grid distribution patterns to enable better planning decisions. By then, the proposed method is implemented on MATLAB platform and compared with various existing methods such as Hybrid Genetic Ant Colony (HGAC), Artificial Neural Network and Particle Swarm Optimization (ANN-PSO), Opposition-based Competitive Swarm Optimizer (OCSO), Gray Wolf Algorithm (GWA), and Genetic Algorithm (GA).With a LCOE of 0.048 $/kWh the proposed PGCN method demonstrates superior cost-effectiveness as it beats all other methods for energy scheduling and management.

articleTitle: Design and Implementation of a Smart Speech Interface using OCR and TTS APIs on ESP32-CAM
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Traditional TTS (TTS) systems are large, expensive, and inefficient, making them unsuitable for use by those competing in the eyeball challenge. These have limited portability and rely heavily on hardware for Optical Character Recognition (OCR) and TTS. The article describes a low-cost, lightweight solution based on the ESP32-CAM module, OCR, VoiceRSS, TTS, and Application Programming Interfaces (API). An amplifier module uses OCR to turn the text acquired from images into high-quality speech. The benefits include portability, real-time computing, and decreased power usage. The test results were outstanding, with 98% precision for high-contrast text, 92% for low-contrast text, and 89% for small print. Furthermore, it achieved high voice intelligibility (9/10) and low average power consumption (0.72W). These results support the proposed system's potential as an effective and appropriate solution for assistive reading devices in a variety of settings.

articleTitle: Optimizing Crop Spraying with Smart Drones using Deep Neural Networks and Image Processing
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Due to climate change, environmental issues, and the necessity to nourish a growing human population, intelligent drones for agricultural spraying are gaining popularity. The utilisation of IoT smart drones in agriculture enhances food security by facilitating more precise operations, optimising resource utilisation, and reducing environmental impact. The proposed process consists of three steps: data preparation, feature extraction, and model training. Agricultural images are subjected to scaling, denoising, augmentation, and background elimination in the preprocessing phase. Significant attributes such as hue, shape, density edge, and HOC are identified by the feature extraction module. The study employs an ABiLSTM model that utilises historical data to determine optimal timings for crop spraying, hence enhancing prediction accuracy. The results indicate that the ABiLSTM model effectively addresses challenges in complex feature classification and prediction, achieving an impressive 95.62% accuracy rate. This study illustrates how AI-powered smart drones may transform precision agriculture, offering a sustainable and economical solution to the issues encountered by modern farmers. This research establishes a foundation for future AI-driven agricultural techniques that can enhance crop management through deep learning and the Internet of Things. This will assist farmers in fulfilling future food supply demands.

articleTitle: Autonomous Voltage Stabilization in Hybrid Energy Grids with Reinforcement Learning
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The growing incorporation of renewable energy sources into hybrid energy networks requires creative ways to maintain voltage stability. This work investigates using reinforcement learning (RL) algorithms to autonomously regulate voltage levels in hybrid energy systems that include solar, wind, and traditional power sources. It presents an innovative RL-based controller that dynamically modulates the output of distributed energy resources (DERs) in response to variable load demands and generation fluctuations. This research addresses voltage fluctuations in hybrid energy networks using RL. The proposed RL-based system improves voltage stability, flexibility, and efficiency, outperforming traditional techniques in both simulations and practical applications. The RL agent uses real-time data to learn optimum control techniques to reduce voltage variances successfully. The efficacy of the proposed system is assessed by simulations on a benchmark microgrid model, revealing substantial improvements in voltage regulation and system resilience relative to traditional control approaches. The results demonstrate that the RL-based method improves voltage stability and optimizes overall energy utilization efficiency within the grid. It emphasizes the possibility of incorporating AI-driven solutions in managing hybrid energy systems, facilitating the development of more sustainable and dependable energy infrastructures.

articleTitle: VLSI based Cascaded Integrator Comb (CIC) Filter for RADAR
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Efficient filtering methods in contemporary radar systems are needed to process high-frequency signals with little distortion and noise. The Cascaded Integrator-Comb filter has a popular choice for decimation and interpolation because of its easy hardware implementation and low complexity. The focus of this project is the VLSI implementation and simulation of a 100 MHz Cascaded Integrator-Comb filter for real-time radar applications.The CIC filter is implemented using Verilog HDL and simulated in Xilinx Vivado for the evaluation of important performance characteristics like latency, power consumption, and resource consumption. The architecture includes cascaded integrator and comb stages that efficiently suppress the aliasing effects and improve the signal quality. The simulation outputs confirm the behavior and effectiveness of the CIC filter in the processing of high-speed radar signals with signal integrity.Using VLSI design methodologies, the project presents an efficient and hardware-friendly solution for real-time radar signal processing. The research proves that high-speed digital filtering can be implemented in ASIC or FPGA-based radar systems, and it advances VLSI-based signal processing.The current version maintains VLSI simulation in Xilinx Vivado as the central theme and steers clear of FPGA implementation while still taking on real-time applications.

articleTitle: Advanced Neural Network Models for Optimal Energy Management in Microgrids with Integrated Electric Vehicles
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: EV and BSS are putting a pressure on power networks, and chaotic charging techniques are a major contributor to this. Due to the nonlinear, unpredictable, and energy-intensive character of electric car charging demands, smart microgrids must have optimal energy management. Our regional energy management system optimises operations for electric vehicles and battery storage by orchestrating grid-connected charging using a price-incentive scheme. The system will implement smart microgrids. They hope to achieve this by maximising the profits from battery storage systems and decreasing the costs of charging electric vehicles. To improve search performance, a new method combines GA with NB. Dimensionality reduction, unbalanced dataset classification, and min-max normalisation are all data preprocessing tasks that genetic algorithms are used for. The proposed NBGA hybrid model outperforms previous imputation methods by a whopping 98% in trials where feature selection is not used. In order to make energy management systems better, evolutionary algorithms and naive Bayes classification are used. Through reducing the impact of uncoordinated charging, the suggested method improves the stability and economic feasibility of smart microgrids.

articleTitle: Physics Informed Deep Neural Network for SOC Prediction for Lithium-Ion Batteries
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: In this work, we discuss a better method for State of Charge (SOC) estimation in lithium-ion batteries through the use of Physics-Informed Neural Networks (PINNs). SOC estimation is critical for battery longevity, efficiency, and safety, but conventional methods such as Coulomb Counting and Equivalent Circuit Models (ECMs) tend to encounter inaccuracies due to aging and environmental variations. Although machine learning (ML) models provide enhanced accuracy, they need extensive data and are non-physical in nature. Overcoming these, PINNs use battery electrochemistry principles and integrate them with deep learning to achieve more robust and flexible SOC estimates. By embedding physical equations in the learning, PINNs eliminate data dependency along with enhancing the generalization to varying conditions. The findings indicate that PINNs surpass both conventional and ML-based methods and are a potential tool for real-time Battery Management Systems (BMS). The computational efficiency needs to be optimized in future work to facilitate practical application in electric vehicles and energy storage systems.

articleTitle: A High-Performance Architectural Design for FIR Filtering in Fixed and Reconfigurable Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The FIR filter architecture is proposed that achieves high-speed operation focused on both fixed and programmable applications. Instead, we take a transpose form configuration of a block FIR filter in an area-delay efficient way, which is effective for medium-to-large orders of the filters we introduce a generalized block formulation for transpose FIR filters, providing a unified approach for implementation. Moreover, we also present a low-complexity architecture based on the Multiple Constant Multiplication (MCM) strategy for fixed FIR filters, which helps in inordinate reduction in associated complexity and resources. The proposed architecture shows significant savings in terms of the Area-Delay Product (ADP), when compared to the traditional direct-form FIR filter architectures when they are implemented using digital blocks, which is especially true for medium and large sizes. The direct-form implementation is more efficient for low filter lengths, but as they increase, it becomes impractical, where the proposed architecture applies. This renders the design highly beneficial for reconfigurable and resource-efficient FIR filter applications. To verify the functionality of the proposed architecture, the design is coded in Verilog HDL, modeled in ModelSim and synthesized in Xilinx tools. Extensive experimental results validate that the proposed architecture save a huge amount with respect to resource usage as well as delay, thus are very beneficial for future digital signal processing applications. Therefore, the proposed method offers a flexible and efficient design of fixed and reconfigurable FIR filters that meets the increasing demand for high-performance and low-complexity digital filter structures.

articleTitle: A High Efficient and Cost Effective Waste Sorting Solution using Advanced Sensors and AI
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The rapid increase in global waste, including plastic, metal, electronic waste (e-waste), and hazardous materials, necessitates an efficient and automated waste management system. Traditional manual waste sorting is labor-intensive, error-prone, and poses health risks due to exposure to hazardous materials. Existing automated solutions, such as IoT-based waste monitoring and basic sensor-based segregation, suffer from low classification accuracy, high misclassification rates, and limited adaptability to complex waste types. This research addresses these challenges by proposing an AI-driven waste segregation system integrating machine vision, YOLO (You Only Look Once) object detection, and Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) for real-time waste classification with improved precision. The system utilizes an ESP32-CAM microcontroller to capture and process images, metal sensors to distinguish ferrous and non-ferrous metals, and gas sensors to detect hazardous gases such as methane (CH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">4</inf>), carbon monoxide (CO), and ammonia (NH<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">3</inf>). Motorized actuators then autonomously direct waste into designated bins, reducing human intervention and increasing sorting efficiency. Experimental results demonstrate that the proposed system achieves a classification accuracy of 97-98%, significantly outperforming manual sorting (83-85%). Additionally, misclassification rates were reduced by fivefold, particularly in hazardous waste detection, where errors dropped from 1.5 kg to 0.3 kg per 100 kg of waste processed. The integration of advanced AI models and sensor technologies ensures precise waste categorization, optimizing recycling processes, minimizing landfill waste, and enhancing workplace safety. This scalable and cost-effective solution supports smart city initiatives and sustainable waste management by automating waste segregation with high efficiency, adaptability, and minimal operational costs.

articleTitle: Electric Vehicles for Sustainable Transportation: A Case Study of Malawi
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The worldwide transition to electric vehicles (EVs) presents a viable approach to diminish dependence on fossil fuels and lower greenhouse gas emissions. This study introduces a MATLAB-based simulation model intended to evaluate the viability of implementing electric vehicles (EVs) in Malawi Africa, with the objective of diminishing reliance on imported oil. The model assesses the energy, economic, and environmental effects of electric vehicle adoption in urban and rural areas by analyzing local driving patterns, energy consumption data, and grid capacity factors. The MATLAB simulation integrates essential EV components, including battery performance, motor efficiency, and charging infrastructure requirements, to evaluate possible fuel savings and pollution reductions. Findings suggest that electric vehicles (EVs) may substantially decrease fuel consumption and mitigate greenhouse gas emissions; however, physical and economic obstacles, like the necessity for charging stations and battery recycling facilities, persist. This study offers significant insights into the advantages and obstacles of electric vehicle adoption in developing nations, putting up particular laws and incentives to encourage the construction of infrastructure and the general use of electric vehicles. The results advocate for the shift to electric mobility in Malawi, providing a route to enhanced energy autonomy and sustainability.

articleTitle: Optimization of Vertical Axis Wind Turbine Farm Parameters for Enhanced Power Generation Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research focuses on optimising 3D-printed Vertical Axis Wind Turbines (VAWTs) to enhance power output efficiency and, in turn, cost-effectiveness. VAWTs can make use of multi-directional winds, unlike Horizontal Axis Wind Turbines(HAWTs), making them suitable for urban and off-shore applications. Moreover, VAWTs operate with fewer moving parts, allowing for easier maintenance and lesser noise than HAWTs. However, wake effects and turbulence will reduce power efficiency, so a great deal of precise design and layout optimisation is required to capture maximum energy. The work investigates the performance of up-scaled N20 motors for energy conversion from wind using the Savonius VAWT with different Length/Diameter ratios. Various configurations of turbines were tested in a controlled environment, and then the voltage output was measured and converted to power using a standard formula. The best results were observed with the configuration consisting of 22 turbines with L/D ratio: 3.333, which produced a power output of 8.778 W. It was found that the relationship in L/D ratio, number of turbines, and power generated is a non-linear relationship, which shows that configuration is of utmost importance for maximum efficiency. One of the principal difficulties with VAWTs is the wake effect and turbulence, which adversely affect power efficiency [1]. Optimized VAWT farms can reduce both installation and maintenance costs and thus present a viable alternative for renewable energy systems. Hence, this study is based on designs of cost-effective, highly efficient VAWT systems that provide better power density for producing sustainable energy.

articleTitle: Hybrid Graph Attention Network Model for Smart Water Management and Dam Level Forecasting
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The cultural, historical, economic, and environmental sustainability of India is significantly influenced by the water resources provided by dams. Dams are crucial for various purposes, including flood control, irrigation and industrial water supply, and enabling river navigation. Accurate forecasting models are crucial for optimizing dam operations and mitigating hazards in successful stormwater management. This project aims to estimate dam levels using hybrid modelling tactics and data preprocessing methods. Conventional models often yield erroneous forecasts of dam water levels due to their intricate nonlinearity and spatio-temporal variability. To address this, it provides a Hybrid GAT Model that integrates fuzzy logic with dynamic spatio-temporal grammar and an attention-based network. The model combines a fuzzy inference method and an earthquake structure to analyses historical SWM values, accounting for unknown factors affecting dam levels. The findings indicate that the proposed model surpasses existing approaches, with an MAE of 24.33 and an R-value of 0.863, signifying high predictive accuracy. To enhance water resource planning, optimize dam operations, and develop superior disaster mitigation strategies, our findings underscore the necessity of hybrid DL models.

articleTitle: Dual Active Bridge Converter Output Current Ripple Prediction in EV Battery Chargers Through Multimodal Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The prediction of converter output current ripple in Electric Vehicle (EV) battery chargers stands as a vital condition to maintain stable charging with safe battery operation by reducing voltage fluctuations and delivering steady currents. The prediction of converter output current ripple faces difficulties because the complex dynamics of converter behavior changes according to various load conditions and environmental factors. This measurement inaccuracy threatens the capability to make optimal power transfers and reduces loss management ability thereby affecting the life span and operational performance of the EV battery. This research presents a framework to predict the amount of current oscillation in chargers for EV battery systems powered by Dual Active Bridge (DAB) Converter. The proposed technique utilizes Multimodal Adaptive Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Network (MASTGNN) as its method. The proposed method aims at both enhancing current ripple prediction accuracy and optimizing converter performance together with improving EV battery lifespan during charging. A MAST-GNN process predicts output current ripples in DAB converters used for EV battery charging through modeling which evaluates the behavior changes of voltage and current and power when operational parameters vary. Implementation of the proposed method in MATLAB will undergo comparison testing with CNN as well as BESO-ANFIS and ANN together with other existing methods. By achieving an accuracy of 97% in current ripple prediction and maintaining a high converter efficiency of 98.5%, the proposed MASTGNN method outperforms traditional approaches without compromising the stability and performance of the EV battery charging process.

articleTitle: Proactive Detection of Cardiac Arrest After First Occurance using Smart Shirt Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: By developing a "smart shirt" with a variety of sensors, this work suggests a method to confirm a heart attack after the initial incident. In order to continuously monitor vital body characteristics including heart rate, blood oxygen level, and body temperature, the technology incorporates essential parts like a diode ECG sensor, a MAX30100 pulse oximeter, and an LM35 temperature sensor. The work is done by the Arduino microcontroller, which rapidly interprets data from the sensors and analyses the activity of the heart. In addition to facilitating wireless communication, the Sim800L GSM module enables the system to identify symptoms of cardiac illness and send emergency notifications to carers or physicians. The jumper-connected, battery-operated device is made to be adaptable and simple to incorporate into regular clothes, enabling patients to get.

articleTitle: Intelligent IoT System with AI and ML Integration for Smart Home Automation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI), Machine Learning (ML), and the Internet of Things (IoT) is transforming smart home automation by enhancing security, energy efficiency, and user convenience. This paper presents an AI-powered IoT system that employs real-time monitoring and adaptive automation to optimize household operations. The system utilizes ultrasonic sensors for water level monitoring, motion sensors for automated lighting and fan control, and DHT11 sensors for climate regulation. AI-driven facial recognition ensures secure access control, while predictive energy management reduces electricity consumption by dynamically adjusting appliance usage. The system effectively detects hazards such as gas leaks and fires in real time, triggering immediate alerts and safety measures. With seamless device coordination and automated responses, this framework enhances home security, energy efficiency, and overall automation reliability. Despite challenges in data security and system integration, the findings highlight that AI-ML-driven IoT automation is a viable solution for creating self-sustaining and intelligent smart homes.

articleTitle: Interpretable Clothing Size Prediction: CNN and XAI for Personalized Recommendations
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research work proposes a clothing size prediction method based on customer images using Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and incorporating Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI) methods. The proposed CNN model directly computes size recommendations based on typical key visual attributes about body dimensions and fitting preferences of clothing. Both training and testing were performed with a set of images of labeled customers; the overall accuracy of the model reached 89%; precision and recall were higher than 90% for the majority of size categories. The blend of XAI enabled the visualization and even the explanation of the modality to show how any particular feature of the visual managed to portray such a conclusion. It also makes the model highly interpretable and thus very reliable for e-commerce applications, where accurate size predictions and recommendations are especially important. It is possible to state that the proposed method can promisingly improve the shopping experience through more accurate and individualized forecasts of the size of the clothes, minimizing high rates of return and thereby increasing customer satisfaction.

articleTitle: Crested Porcupine Optimizer for Intelligent Estimation of Current Ripple in Power Factor Correction Interleaved Boost Converters for Electric Vehicle Charging
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Enhancing efficiency and power quality (PQ) in electric vehicle (EV) charging systems depends on power factor correction (PFC) interleaved boost converters (IBC). Traditional methods to assess current ripple produce misleading results which leads to decreased system performance and increased power losses. This research presents the Crested Porcupine Optimizer (CPO) as a novel solution for intelligent current ripple estimation in electric vehicle charging systems to overcome existing method limitations. The main goal consists of minimizing ripple formation while also reducing Total Harmonic Distortions (THD). The Proportional-Integral (PI) controller gain parameter optimization occurs through CPO processing which raises the converter performance standards. The proposed solution implemented on MATLAB while evaluated performance with Artificial Neural Network (ANN) and Bald Eagle Search Optimization (BESO) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM). Results show the CPO approach delivers THD at 0.99% which supports effective harmonic suppression to enhance PQ for EV chargers. The evaluation demonstrates that CPO successfully enhances the current ripple estimation capability to improve PFC IBC system operations in EV charging applications.

articleTitle: A LoRa based Emergency Communication Device for Disaster Response
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: During disaster scenarios, rescue efforts are delayed by communication breakdowns caused by inaccessibility of cellular networks and Wi-Fi. The proposed model overcomes the problem with a self-powered long-distance communication system utilizing LoRa technology and Arduino hardware. With a hand-cranked power generator, it operates continuously without needing an external power source. The device features a NEO-6M GPS chip and oxygen sensor to relay real-time position and environmental information over a LoRaWAN network. The proposed model has pre-formatted emergency messages appearing on an OLED display, which are relayed with sensor readings to a connected LoRa receiver via a Wi-Fi-enabled web interface and app. This system provides an affordable, dependable, and energy-efficient disaster management solution that facilitates real-time tracking and enhanced coordination in rescue operations. The study proves that the proposed model's internal power source and uninterrupted data transmission greatly improve situational awareness and response effectiveness in emergency situations.

articleTitle: Smart Sampling and Residual Bottleneck Dense Network for Reliable and Energy-Efficient Routing in WSNs
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The fundamental requirement for WSNs made up of power-efficient and inexpensive sensor nodes depends on short-distance multi-hop communication. The potential of WSNs expands through new digital electronics and wireless communications technology despite the ongoing critical challenge related to energy efficiency. The main energy issues in WSNs stem from the excessively high control signal overhead between base stations and sensor nodes together with packet losses that require retransmissions to reduce energy efficiency. The proposed routing technique solves energy inefficiencies by employing RBDN-HMOA as an energy-efficient routing method. The proposed approach lowers system power consumption through its algorithm which picks distance and energy residual-based optimum forwarding nodes and adapts sampling rates automatically. The algorithm adopts Human Memory Optimization Algorithm (HMOA) to optimize network parameters. Research data shows that experimental results demonstrate both power efficiency and enhanced data transfer rate. The network demonstrates scalability because both throughputs reach 1100 kbps and energy usage reduces to 0.08 J when using 10 nodes. The RBDN-HMOA creates a practical method which extends network duration in practical deployments by diminishing WSN energy utilization without compromising data integrity.

articleTitle: Advanced PLC-based Automation for Converging System and Warehousing
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The increasing complexity of industrial convergence and warehousing operations presents challenges such as inefficient product handling, high manual intervention, and unoptimized space utilization. To address these issues, this research develops an advanced automation system integrating Programmable Logic Controllers (PLCs), Internet of Things (IoT) sensors, and AI-driven technologies. The designed framework automates critical functions, including product merging, collision avoidance, and real-time inventory tracking, ensuring seamless operations.In the convergence station, diffuse and capacitive sensors regulate product flow, preventing collisions and improving throughput.The intelligent warehouse utilizes AI-powered Automated Guided Vehicles (AGVs) with multi-function forks for enhanced stacking and picking.
