Space availability, alignment, and equipment status are monitored using IoT sensors to support predictive maintenance and less downtime. Siemens PLCs execute interlocked ladder logic with fail-safe mechanisms for continuous, error-free operations. Real-time dashboards enhance inventory visibility and operational decision-making.This automation system significantly reduces manual intervention, increases efficiency and optimizes warehouse space utilization. In addition, energy-efficient Automated guided vehicle planning promotes sustainability through decreased environmental impact. The solution lays the way for future innovations like digital twins and autonomous decision-making using AI, making it adaptable to changing manufacturing and logistics requirements.

articleTitle: Creating a Real Time Public Transport Information System utilizing GPRS Technology
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Efficient public transportation systems are critical to sustainable urban development, yet they often face challenges such as delayed operations, inadequate fleet management, and limited real-time visibility for passengers. This research addresses these issues by proposing a real-time public transport information system utilizing GPRS technology, which combines GPS and GSM modules to improve the operational efficiency of public transport systems. The system provides real-time vehicle location tracking, SMS notifications when a vehicle starts, and allows passengers to request vehicle location updates or remotely control the vehicle via SMS commands. By integrating affordable components such as Arduino Uno, SIM800L GSM modules, and NEO-6M GPS modules, this system is cost-effective, scalable, and operates without the need for continuous internet connectivity. This feature makes it particularly suitable for areas with limited network infrastructure. The outcome of this research demonstrates that the proposed system offers a feasible, reliable, and affordable solution to enhance passenger convenience, improve operational control, and facilitate scalable fleet management, making public transport more efficient and safer.

articleTitle: A Novel Approach to Mitigating Air Pollution and Climate Change with Graph Convolutional RNN Models
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: There is a connection between climate change and air pollution due to the fact that weather patterns impact the transportation and degradation of pollutants. Variations in humidity, vertical mixing, and wind speed all have an impact on the transport, dispersion, emission, and deposition of pollutants, which in turn impacts air quality. Because of shifts in precipitation, atmospheric chemistry, and pollutant removal mechanisms, air quality is predicted to deteriorate in highly populated regions as a result of climate change. Both primary and secondary pollutants, such as particulate matter and near-surface ozone, may be formed more quickly as a result of climate change. To enhance air pollution prediction, a comprehensive data preparation stage was used to scale data and errors, identify and eliminate anomalies, and more. It used RMSE, MAE, and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup> measures to assess GCRNN performance with and without DPFS. Using DPFS greatly improved the accuracy of predictions for PM10 concentrations, with RMSE=1.342, MAE=0.264, and R<sup xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</sup>=0.532. Air quality predictions seem to be a good fit for DL, according to these results. Air pollution is becoming worse due to climate change, and this study demonstrates how advanced prediction models can assist.

articleTitle: Impact of Multi-GNSS Signal Strength on Smartphone Battery Consumption
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of environmental conditions, multi-GNSS satellite signal strength, and battery levels on smartphone power consumption during location-based services (LBS). Using data collected from three Android smartphones under varying conditions (Open Sky and Urban Canopy), we examine the relationship between GNSS signal quality, positional accuracy, and battery drain. Results show that signal strength remains relatively stable across different battery levels in both environments, with urban areas experiencing weaker signals due to obstructions. Interestingly, some satellite constellations, like BeiDou and QZSS, exhibit stable or improved signal strength as battery levels decrease, suggesting optimizations in the GNSS chipsets. Power consumption was higher in open sky conditions, where stronger signals required continuous GNSS sensor activity. In contrast, urban environments saw lower power drain as the device struggled to maintain connections. Significant variations in power drain were observed across devices, with more efficient smartphones like Vivo V23e 5G and ASUS MAX PRO consuming less power. The study highlights the potential for optimizing GNSS systems to reduce battery drain without sacrificing accuracy, contributing to more energy-efficient LBS applications in smartphones.

articleTitle: Deep Hybrid Neural Network Models for Estimating Compressive Strength in Eco-Friendly Materials
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The cement industry's significant carbon dioxide emissions considerably impact greenhouse gas levels, establishing it as a major polluter. Moreover, the extraction of natural resources for concrete manufacture has been excessive due to rapid population growth and escalating construction demands. This depletion has created an urgent need for environmentally benign alternatives that do not compromise compressive strength. The paper examines four data transformation methods: statistical normalisation, min-max normalisation, non-linear transformation, and whitening transformation. The Autofeat approach is employed for automatic feature engineering and selection to enhance data preprocessing. The application of inter- and intra-periodic convolutional blocks facilitates the extraction of superficial features from sequences of varying dimensions utilising a CNN model with a DSDB architecture. To enhance the extraction of profound sequence information, a transformer module using GWT captures comprehensive temporal dependencies. The proposed approach facilitates the prediction of the compressive strength of eco-friendly materials with an accuracy of 97.46%. These results illustrate that advanced data transformation and feature extraction enhance the prediction of material performance, highlighting the potential of deep learning to optimise sustainable construction materials, thereby facilitating more efficient and environmentally sustainable building solutions.

articleTitle: Predictive Modeling for Safety Risk Assessment in Bridge Construction using ARIMA and LSTM
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Due to the heightened hazards associated with construction compared to operational phases, particularly in coastal regions, it is imperative to conduct safety risk assessments throughout the bridge construction process, especially for large and complex structures. The existing evaluation methodologies are inadequate for addressing risk correlations, as they rely on subjective weight assignments and do not reveal essential risk factors necessary for management and prevention. This study establishes the importance of safety risk indicators by employing deep learning algorithms on data received from many origins and categorized into two decision-making groups. A hybrid ARIMA-LSTM model is proposed for the effective management of nonlinear risk components. Upon estimating parameters and eliminating linear trends from the speed series data, the ARIMA model transmits the residuals to the LSTM network, which processes the normalised nonlinear components. Upon synthesizing both outcomes, we obtain our conclusive risk predictions. The model surpassed prior methodologies with an RMSE of 18.453, MAE of 15.287, and MAPE of 0.132, evaluated across two test driving cycles and two real-world driving scenarios. The enhanced safety management, augmented predictive accuracy, and support in decision-making for complex bridge projects illustrate the effectiveness of hybrid models in Safety Risk Assessment for Bridge Construction.

articleTitle: Neural Networks for Performance Prediction of Biogas-Powered Hybrid Engines
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Artificial Neural Networks (ANNs) have revolutionized the evaluation of performance predictions across multiple disciplines, including internal combustion engines. However, concerning biogas-hybrid engine performance implementation, it remains a topic of contention or significance due to the interdependencies of fuel composition, combustion dynamics, and emissions characterizations. This undertaking will highlight the performance of an ANN-based predictive model implementing biogas-diesel fuel hybrid performance predictions in consideration of combustion characteristics, emissions, and power output stability. Contrasting other machine learning models such as Random Forest, I demonstrate that ANNs present better accuracies for predicting natural gas biodiesel. Additional exploration will invite contemplation for the implications of ANNs for improving gas turbine efficiencies, hybrid system architectures, and overall sustainable energy strategies, all of which will determine the development of the most-accurate dataset, translations, and application. This study will further analyze the evolving nature of ANNs which would include features like real-time data collection that might offer a more finely tuned optimization of the biogas hybrid routes. Ultimately, the nature and performance of the study will serve to facilitate a discourse around recent developments, challenges, and future paths for AI-enabled sustainable energy opportunities.

articleTitle: Improving Reliability in Wireless Sensor Network for Sensor Nodes using Vice Cluster Head
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Enhancing the operational lifespan of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) is crucial in energy-constrained environments where recharging or replacing nodes is not feasible. Network longevity is typically evaluated based on the time to initial node failure and application-specific parameters. Over the time, Clustering has emerged as an effective strategy to improve WSN durability, minimizing communication loads by grouping nodes under a central Cluster Head (CH). However, traditional probabilistic clustering protocols often result in suboptimal CH placement, leading to imbalanced energy consumption and lacking a backup lead. This paper proposes a LEACH with Cluster Head and Vice cluster head (LEACH-CHV) method with centralized clustering approach utilizing the LEACH algorithm and fuzzy logic that employs election and implementation of the Cluster Head (CH) and Vice Cluster Head (VCH) which enhances the reliability of WSNs by ensuring continuous network operation, which mitigates the risk of communication failures due to unexpected CH depletion, promoting equitable energy distribution, extending network endurance and it's future work.

articleTitle: Active and Reactive Power Control in Three-Phase Grid-Connected Electric Vehicles using Node-Level Capsule Graph Neural Network
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Active Power (AP) together with Reactive Power (RP) control systems that operate with three-phase Grid- connected Electric Vehicles (EVs) control power exchanges between vehicles and grids and preserve voltage stability. The power quality together with voltage stability suffers from changes in the conditions of the grid and the manner of EV charging. When AP and RP power coordination is not done properly it causes the grid to experience more stress and reduces the total system reliability. To overcome these drawbacks, this manuscript proposes technique for enhancing AP and RP control in three-phase grid connected EVs. The proposed method is named as Node Level Capsule Graph Neural Network (NCGNN). The proposed method aims to enhance power distribution efficiency, improves voltage stability, and ensures effective power exchange between the grid and EVs while minimizing power imbalances. NCGNN predicts optimal AP and RP for grid-connected EVs to ensure balanced power exchange and voltage stability. Spider Wasp Optimizer-Multi-scale Hypergraph-based Feature Alignment Network (SWO-MHFAN), Adaptive Interaction Artificial Neural Network (AI-ANN), and Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS) are some of the existing methods that are compared with the proposed method once it is implemented in MATLAB. By attaining an error of 1.8% for AP and RP control and preserving a high efficiency of 98.7%, the suggested approach outperforms traditional methods without reducing the stability and dependability of power exchange in grid-connected EVs.

articleTitle: Exploring Sustainable Computing: IoT, Big Data, and Energy-Efficient Solutions
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: As a result of the quick expansion of the Internet of Things (IoT) and Big Data, there are emerging issues related to resource utilization, power management, and system size. As IoT ecosystems continue to grow, questions about sustainability while sustaining performance have emerged as a key topic. This survey paper explores the current literature on IoT, Big Data and green computing systems that have been proposed for use in the future with an emphasis on solutions that can reduce the carbon footprint of these systems whilst maintaining functionality. It introduces IoT and Big Data and their fundamental theories, discusses challenges including energy issues, data issues, real-time issues, and security issues, and introduces sustainable computing approaches including cloud, edge, and fog computing. Further, the paper discusses energy efficiency methods such as machine learning, low power design, energy harvesting, sustainability driven data analysis and predictive maintenance. The survey also points out the outstanding research issues in terms of scalability, energy-performance, and security-sustainability. Lastly, suggestions for further studies involve enhancing interaction between AI systems, creating energy-sensitive AI models, and enhancing the performance of combined structures. Hence, the objective of this paper is to present an understanding into constructing large-scale, energy efficient, and secure IoT systems, which can advance the sustainability of future IoT and Big Data systems.

articleTitle: IoT-Enabled Smart Shoes for Visually Impaired Navigation and Safety
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Navigating safely and independently is a significant challenge for visually impaired individuals due to their inability to detect obstacles, uneven terrain, and other environmental hazards. Traditional mobility aids such as white canes provide limited assistance, and guide dogs are costly and require extensive training. To overcome these limitations, this research introduces an IoT-enabled smart shoe designed to enhance mobility and safety. The proposed system utilizes ultrasonic and infrared sensors to detect obstacles in real time, an Arduino Nano microcontroller for processing sensor data, and a Bluetooth module to transmit alerts to a connected mobile application. The system provides audio feedback through earphones, allowing users to receive real-time verbal alerts for safe navigation. Experimental evaluation demonstrates that the smart shoe achieves high accuracy in obstacle detection (96%), offers stable and reliable real-time feedback, and is designed for ease of use. A comparison with existing assistive technologies highlights the system’s effectiveness in improving independent mobility and reducing collision risks. Future developments may include AI-based navigation enhancements, extended battery life, and advanced sensor fusion for better adaptability in complex environments.

articleTitle: SAFESTRIDE 360: IoT-Powered Smart Stroller
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The Smart Stroller based on IoT meets the demands of contemporary parenting by combining automation, security, and convenience. Manual strollers demand constant control, which is a challenge for parents in terms of safety and convenience. This study aims to develop an intelligent stroller with a human-following feature, obstacle detection, slope braking with auto, and sunshade with weather sensitivity, all with the aim of minimizing parental effort while maintaining the safety of the child. Moreover, voice control through mobile apps improves user experience, enabling remote control. Sensors, motors, and microcontrollers combined provide real-time data processing, enhancing childcare product functionality. The proposed system greatly improves infant mobility solutions, providing hands-free control and improved safety. Future developments can involve AI-based navigation, real-time camera monitoring, GPS tracking with geofencing, baby crying detection, and a solar-powered energy system for improved sustainability. The Smart Stroller is a groundbreaking innovation in childcare technology, reducing parental effort while providing a safe and comfortable experience for children and caregivers alike.

articleTitle: Lifecycle-based Optimization of Home Energy Management: PV–Battery–EV Scheduling using Giant Trevally Optimization
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: In particular, the efficient home energy management systems have become essential as renewable energy technologies such as PV systems, batteries, and EVs utilize in the residential ambiance. Previous techniques in Home Energy Management Systems (HEMS) lacked efficiency in handling dynamic energy scenarios, optimizing battery control, and achieving a cost-effective yet sustainable approach. This study proposes cost-efficient solutions that enhance the durability of Energy Storage Systems (ESS) while promoting environmentally sustainable energy consumption. To make the PV, batteries, EVs and the grid interactive, this study decomposes the full HEMS as elucidated below. As such, the suggested methodology means the detailed system characterization and mathematical modeling of PVs, batteries, and EVs, further, along with the effective approaches to the optimal flow and scheduling of appliances. GTO is used in the study to ensure that critical factors such as battery capacity and DoD are fine tuned to justify the life, viability, and affordability of the system. The proposed system incurs a cost of 3.899 EUR, experiences an energy loss of 0.423 kWh, and extends battery longevity to 7.940 years.

articleTitle: Advanced Energy Management in Smart Grids using Lyrebird Optimization Algorithm
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Integration of a hybrid wind turbine (HWT) and a battery energy system (BES) is expected to take place under the framework of a Smart Grid (SG) to optimize energy generation, storage, and distribution and enhance stability and efficiency. One aspect of such systems is a challenge concerning the effective management of Renewable Energy (RE) fluctuation to achieve balanced operation among renewable generation and energy demand. This paper proposes a Lyrebird Optimization Algorithm (LOA) to optimize energy demand forecasting and management within the hybrid system. The LOA is used to minimize Mean Absolute Percentage Error (MAPE) in energy demand forecasting within the SG system. By optimizing energy demand forecasting, the LOA effectively improves accuracy in energy management and forecasting within the SG. Its adaptive optimization ensures that forecasting errors are minimized across various operating conditions, enhancing overall efficiency of the energy distribution system. By then the proposed LOA method is implemented on the MATLAB platform, and its performance is evaluated by comparing it with existing optimization techniques such as Improved Grey Wolf Optimization (IGWO), Multi-Objective Optimization (MOO), Multi-Objective Wind Driven Optimization (MOWDO), and Coati Optimization Algorithm (COA). The results show that the proposed LOA method provides superior performance in minimizing MAPE, achieving the lowest MAPE value of 2.90%, indicating its enhanced accuracy in energy demand forecasting and optimization.

articleTitle: Next-Gen Energy Meter with Load Control using ESP32
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The growing demand for energy-efficient solutions in smart homes has led to the development of IoT-based energy-saving and monitoring systems. This project focuses on utilizing the ESP32 micro controller to monitor and control household energy consumption in real time. By integrating sensors, which like ultrasonic and cloud connectivity, users can optimize their energy usage, reduce wastage, and lower electricity bills.

articleTitle: AGRI-SMART HUB: A Multilingual Integrated Platform for Comprehensive Farming Solutions and Support
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This research work proposes an integrated web platform that uses machine learning and web development to solve pressing challenges in agriculture. While the world population increases exponentially and the land for farming is constant, deforestation and climate change lower crop yields, posing a threat to food security. For a growing population's demand, we need to shift from conventional farming to a technological approach. Nowadays everybody has access to phones and the internet. Our website aims to strengthen farmers by providing them with new resources and government schemes for enhanced productivity and sustainability. This study integrates the multiple machine learning models that fulfill the farmers' needs. These include a crop recommendation system that uses parameters such as rainfall, humidity, soil pH, and moisture to suggest suitable crops. our crop yield prediction model that analyzes rainfall and NPK (nitrogen, phosphorus, potassium) levels to forecast yields; and a transfer learning-based CNN model that takes the leaf as input and detects the disease in the early stage. Moreover, we use Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) to assist farmers so that they can use the government's issues pdf regarding agriculture and ask questions based on that pdf, which they did not understand in their regional language. This study highlights the potential of technology-based solutions in revolutionizing agriculture and responding to the global issue of food security in an increasingly dynamic world.

articleTitle: Green Data Centers: Advancing Sustainability in the Digital Era
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The advancement of digital technologies, and the increased use of data-driven applications, have driven data center demand around the globe. Although crucial in contemporary architecture, conventional data centers are major energy hogs and detrimental to many environmental concerns including high carbon footprint and resource depletion. Green data centres are the new concept to counter the negative impacts of conventional data centres and these are more energy efficient, integrated with renewable power sources and use unique cooling technologies. These are: server virtualization, liquid and immersion cooling, waste heat to power recovery, and the use of clean energy such as solar and wind energy. AI driven power management, edge computing, and photonic interconnects are some of the new trends that continue to revolutionize the efficiency and sustainability of these facilities. However, challenges like high initial investment, policy instabilities, and technological limitations to renewable energy systems integration have not been addressed. Solving these problems should involve policy makers, managers and scholars in the field of supply chain management. Green data centres are the future in which, through the use of innovative technologies such as quantum computing, AI optimisation as well as modularity in the design of data centres, an increase in masses’ digital needs will be well served while at the same time being environmentally sensitive. With the help of such innovations, green data centers can set an example for the development of the new green economy.

articleTitle: Compact Annular Slot Antenna for Millimeter-Wave MIMO(Multiple Input Multiple Output) Applications
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: This work presents the design of a compact annular slot antenna for millimeter-wave applications, addressing the challenge of achieving good isolation, stable performance, and reasonable gain on a cost-effective substrate. The antenna is designed on an FR4-epoxy substrate (ε<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">r</inf> = 4.4, tan δ = 0.02), which provides a balance between affordability and electrical performance. It operates within the 26–36 GHz frequency range and features a triple-port configuration. By using optimized slot positioning and a well-structured feed network, the antenna achieves an isolation of -28 dB while maintaining good gain and efficient radiation characteristics. Simulation and fabrication results confirm its performance, demonstrating its suitability for high-frequency communication systems. Additionally, its capability to support MIMO applications makes it a strong candidate for next-generation wireless networks.

articleTitle: Adaptive Solar Energy Storage with Deep Learning for Improved Grid Resilience
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Implementing renewable energy sources, especially solar power, into the electrical grid has distinct difficulties and potential for improving system resilience. This research investigates an adaptive solar energy storage system using deep learning methodologies, particularly Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks, to enhance energy management and grid stability. The proposed system utilizes past solar generating data and usage patterns to forecast future energy needs and generation capacities. LSTM allows the model to efficiently reflect temporal interdependence and variation in solar energy output, facilitating more precise forecasting. The adaptive storage system modifies its charging and discharging processes in real time, optimizing efficiency and reducing energy waste. LSTM-based forecasting improves the storage system’s response to variations in supply and demand, enhancing load balancing and grid resilience. This method facilitates a change in renewable energy sources while enhancing the resilience of grid infrastructure to sustain delays. Findings indicate that integrating flexible energy storage using advanced deep-learning methodologies may significantly improve the efficacy and dependability of solar energy systems. This paper challenges solar energy intermittency with LSTM-based adaptive storage, enhancing forecasting precision, grid resilience, and energy efficiency enhancing stable energy management and optimized battery use.

articleTitle: Real-Time SOH Estimation for EV Li-Ion Batteries using ML & Digital Twin
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: In this research, a Digital Twin model is implemented alongside a machine learning model and monitoring technique for electric vehicles (EVs) battery health tracking in order to enable real-time tracking. Optimal performance and longevity of electric vehicles (EVs) hinges on proper management of their lithium-ion (Li-ion) batteries. The algorithm primarily applied in this research is the K-Nearest Neighbors (KNN) algorithm which leverages data from the battery’s cycling charge and discharge processes to guess its health status (SOH) and how long it will still be useful (RUL). Sensors measure real-time values like voltage and current as well as temperature, and these are further processed in the cloud via NodeMCU microcontroller with Wi-Fi. These transferred values are used to construct a Digital Twin technology model that accurately represents the battery model and guesses how the battery will act in different situations to increase KNN performance. Accurate monitoring enables proactive maintenance, sophisticated early issue detection, and improved efficiency and lifespan of the battery which enhances the overall functioning of the EVs. Analyzing dataset from the real world confirms the approach used helps predict monitoring health checks and planning for unforeseen events. The technology improves the operational efficiency of electric vehicles (EVs) increases power system performance, improves the overall energy consumption, drives thorough quality inspection, and significantly reduces maintenance costs which greatly. This work focuses on the application of machine learning and Digital Twin technologies for EV battery management, which enhances the sustainability and intelligence of electric vehicles.

articleTitle: Survey of AI and Optimization Methods for DoS Attack Detection in WSNs
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)

authors.preferredName: Kamparapu V V Satya Trinadh Naidu

abstract: The use of Wireless Sensor Networks (WSNs) in modern IoT applications is very important, as they can monitor and transmit data in different environments. Although their open communication nature, limited energy, and computational capacity render them highly vulnerable to Denial-of-Service (DoS) attacks that will deteriorate network performance and reliability significantly. This survey covers all aspects of recent developments using artificial intelligence (AI) based techniques for the detection and prevention of DoS attacks in wireless sensor networks (WSNs). It gives particular attention to the integration of deep learning models and metaheuristic optimization strategies in terms of making their detection accuracy better, minimizing predication of false positives, and improving the model’s adaptability in the way of constraints of resource limits. Real time DoS detection has been studied under the perspective of different ensemble learning strategies, hybrid deep learning frameworks, and feature selection methods. The paper also examines the efficiency of the dimensionality reduction and heuristic tuning techniques in improving model performance. It also discusses future research directions, challenges and open issues that are meant for guiding future innovation in this domain.

articleTitle: Inductive Wireless Charging for Electric Vehicles: Design Calculations and Power Loss Estimation
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Inductive wireless charging technology for electric vehicles (EVs) offers a contactless and efficient method of power transfer. By eliminating the need for physical connectors, it enhances user convenience and reduces maintenance. However, optimizing system parameters such as coil alignment, resonant frequency, and coupling efficiency is crucial to minimize power losses and maximize overall efficiency. This paper presents a detailed design approach for an inductive wireless charging system, including theoretical modelling, power transfer calculations, and power loss estimation. The paper begins with an overview of the wireless charging system architecture, covering the key components such as the transmitter coil, receiver coil, resonant circuit, and power electronics. The inductive power transfer (IPT) model is developed to analyze mutual inductance, coupling coefficient, and resonant frequency. Performance calculations are conducted to determine power transfer efficiency, taking into account factors such as coil misalignment, air gap variations, and core material selection. Additionally, comprehensive power loss estimation is presented, including ohmic losses in the coil windings, eddy current losses in conductive materials, and core losses in ferrite materials. The total power losses are calculated based on real-world operating conditions, and optimization strategies are proposed to improve system performance. By implementing enhanced coil design, resonant compensation, and power electronics optimization, system efficiency can exceed 90%.This study provides valuable insights into the design and optimization of inductive wireless charging stations for EVs, contributing to advancements in sustainable and efficient charging solutions.

articleTitle: Smart Railway Track Obstacle and Crack Detection System with Automated Alert Mechanism
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: Railway safety is a major issue, as obstruction of the tracks and structural collapses can cause fatal accidents. In this project, a Smart Railway Track Obstacle and Crack Detection System is introduced to improve railway safety by using real-time tracking and automated alarms. Ultrasonic sensors are used to detect obstructions on the track, whereas infrared (IR) sensors detect cracks, ensuring early warning for possible dangers. A Z44N MOSFET regulates the braking response of a 12V DC motor, replicating an emergency brake system. The system also includes an LCD display for immediate status reporting and GSM module for instantaneous SMS notification to railway authorities, allowing for quick intervention. Through the combination of various sensing technologies and automated reporting, this system presents a new and proactive solution to railway safety, reducing risk factors of track obstructions and cracks. The solution proposed improves dependability, minimizes human involvement, and provides timely reactions, greatly enhancing railway accident prevention.

articleTitle: A Multi-Resolution Deep Learning Approach for IoT-Integrated Biomedical Signal Processing using CNN-LSTM
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: The rapid advancement of Internet of Things (IoT) technology and deep learning has enabled real-time health monitoring for elderly individuals and patients. This work proposes an IoT-based health monitoring system integrating Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTM) networks to analyze physiological signals and detect anomalies effectively. A network of biomedical sensors, including ECG, EMG, EEG, heart rate, blood pressure, SpO2, temperature, accelerometer, gyroscope, and respiratory rate sensors, continuously collects health data. These sensors transmit real-time physiological signals using wireless communication protocols such as Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, LoRa, and NB-IoT, ensuring seamless data acquisition and remote monitoring. To enhance signal quality, the preprocessing stage employs Wavelet Transform (WT) for denoising biomedical signals, mitigating motion artifacts and environmental noise. Discrete Wavelet Transform (DWT) is applied to extract meaningful features while preserving critical health information. Additional preprocessing steps, including feature normalization, segmentation, and feature extraction, improve deep learning model efficiency. The proposed CNN-LSTM hybrid model leverages CNN for spatial feature extraction and LSTM for capturing temporal dependencies in time-series biomedical data. The architecture includes multiple convolutional layers with ReLU activation, batch normalization, max-pooling, bidirectional LSTM layers, dropout regularization, and an attention mechanism. Model training utilizes labeled medical datasets with an Adam optimizer and binary cross-entropy loss function. Performance evaluation considers accuracy, precision, recall, F1-score, and AUC-ROC metrics. Results demonstrate improved anomaly detection for conditions such as arrhythmias, respiratory irregularities, and early stroke indicators. Deployment in real-time health monitoring applications facilitates continuous patient assessment, fall detection, and predictive medical alerts. This system enhances proactive healthcare solutions by integrating IoT and deep learning for real-time, intelligent, and automated health monitoring.

articleTitle: Machine Learning Enhanced Dual Axis Solar Tracker for Optimized Energy Efficiency
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: In recent years, electricity has become an important component in people’s lives. Living is unimaginable without electricity. The increasing electricity demand has caused electricity distributors to heavily rely on fossil fuels. Not only are fossil fuels a type of non-renewable resource whose sources are depleted day by day but also, they are also responsible for harm to the environment. Therefore, a need arises for the replacement of fossil fuels. The best replacement for it is renewable energy, which is easily replenished as well as not harmful to the environment. The most abundant renewable energy is Solar energy generated from the sun. It is found that the efficiency of solar panels is maximum when the sunrays fall perpendicular to the panel. Since traditional solar panels are fixed, the panel only receives a limited number of perpendicular sunrays, hence the efficiency is less. In summary, non-renewable sources for electricity are on the verge of depletion and traditional solar panels have very less efficiency. This research work proposes a working dual-axis solar panel that can theoretically increase efficiency by 40% compared to the efficiency of traditional solar panels. By implementing an ML model, which trains itself with the data collected by the panel over time, it further increases efficiency and minimizes energy loss.

articleTitle: Evaluation of PMDC, BLDC, and SRM Motors for Electric Vehicles with SoC and Range Analysis
publicationTitle: 2025 5th International Conference on Trends in Material Science and Inventive Materials (ICTMIM)
abstract: A comparative study is conducted on Permanent Magnet DC Motors (PMDCs), Switched Reluctance Motors (SRMs), and Brushless DC Motors (BLDCs) for EV applications, putting particular emphasis on state of charge (SoC) and driving range. MATLAB-based simulation has been used to study motor performance with lithium-ion batteries as the supplier. PMDCs are characterized by high efficiency and power density but are limited due to dependence on rare-earth materials. SRMs are easily constructed and cheap, but they are noisier and vibrate more. BLDC motors stand in between performance and cost. Simulation results show that PMDCs provide the maximum range per charge, BLDC motors have average performance, and SRMs are most durable with low efficiency. This study presents valuable guidelines for motor selection for EV applications, optimizing powertrain performance based on considerations of SoC and range.
